title: Battery Storage Operations & Maintenance Technician (Mid-level)
description: Terra-Gen is seeking a BESS (Battery Energy Storage System) Technician II to perform scheduled and unscheduled fieldwork required to operate and maintain the project to standards above industry best practice. Fieldwork includes, but is not limited to commissioning new systems, troubleshooting, testing, preventive maintenance, corrective maintenance, training of on-site personnel and assisting site visits. The BESS Technician may also be assigned the responsibility for observing the quality and safety practices of contractors performing BESS technical maintenance and commissioning type work. The ideal candidate would be a self-starter and reports to and takes directions from the Remote Operations Site Supervisor. This is a full-time position and may include working on-call as scheduled, overtime, nights, weekends and/or holidays. Some travel may be required for this position. This role provides opportunities for professional growth. ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES The candidate may perform work independently and/or in a team environment, depending upon skills, experience and job task. Responsibilities include troubleshooting and repair of DC, low voltage AC, data acquisition, meteorological stations, ESS system components, including grounded circuits, safely and efficiently while using all safety practices. Tests to be performed by a technician include but are not limited to: Open circuit voltage; Operating DC current; Power Meter verification; Megger Test; and Resistance test. Understand, participate and promote general workplace safety and the ability to follow established environmental and safety standards as well as assist Terra-Gen to improve upon the existing standards. Ability to excel individually or in a team atmosphere within a collaborative, cross-functional and diverse organization. Ability to establish and maintain a positive and professional working relationship with all individuals. Maturity, professionalism and excellent communication skills, both verbally and in writing with superiors and colleagues. Models professional behaviors of conduct that reflect positively on themselves and the company. Developed interpersonal skills, strong work ethic with High-energy. Detailed orientated with excellent hands-on abilities. Perform preventive maintenance on BESS systems to include thermography of low and medium voltage equipment. Audit third party systems as directed for potential safety concerns, quality of worked performed and possible improvement opportunities. Identify, coordinate, and observe contracted workers performing troubleshooting and repairs to OEM equipment to include medium voltage equipment. Document time, material, expenses and maintenance records in O&Ms computer-based maintenance management system (CMMS). Complete assigned training and qualification requirements within a specified time frame, including meeting or exceeding minimum test score requirements. Prepare reports and communicate to site management the results of maintenance activities. Prepare and implement switching orders. Applies technical aptitude and skill performing field tasks, learning progression and ability to apply training along with the ability to recognize and use stop work authority. Apply cybersecurity policies and incident response. Recognize and identify lift hazards (crane, rough terrain forklift, etc.). Complete Safe work permits and conducts level appropriate JHA’s. Perform root cause analysis and implement corrective actions as needed. Perform other qualified duties assigned including procedure development and revision. $32.00 - $37.00 per hour Requirements QUALIFICATIONS: Practical knowledge of electrical systems, BESS systems and their components and how to safely LOTO the equipment. Knowledge of building and structural construction techniques. Ability to safely and efficiently troubleshoot system failures, to include ground faults. Strong analytical, diagnostic, and problem-solving skills. Excellent verbal, written, communication and presentation skills. Strong prioritization skills. Driver’s license. Ability to train others. Journeyman or licensed industrial electrician preferred. Certified inverter training by Power Electronics preferred. EDUCATION and/or EXPERIENCE: High school graduate or GED. 3-5 years’ experience at a Utility-scale Solar Plant. Practical experience with electrical wiring and basic construction practices required. Technical/science/engineering degree, certificate with energy systems preferred. Experience with metering and test equipment. Ability to organize, prioritize and complete multiple tasks simultaneously. Ability to demonstrate a responsive, customer service approach to listening and responding to requests. Ability to communicate status of work activities and issues with peers and management as they relate to projects and tasks. Experience reading and interpreting electrical, I&C, and mechanical drawings and technical manuals. Proficient with the use of the Microsoft Office Suite (Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Outlook). OSHA 30 and CPR qualification preferred. NFPA 70E preferred. COMMUNICATION SKILLS: Provide information/analysis to leadership and department managers. Create written reports/memos/emails to effectively communicate findings internally and externally. Effectively and professionally communicate with leadership, project managers and engineers. Effectively and professionally communicate with vendors and contractors. Effectively and professionally communicate with Quality/Product Development/Purchasing departments. MATHEMATICAL SKILLS: Ability to analyze operating data, identify anomalies and recommend and implement corrective actions. Ability to calculate figures and amounts such as percentages, lengths, and electrical values. Ability to apply concepts of algebra, geometry, and statistical analysis. Ability to analyze and troubleshoot problems with utility scale PV and BESS systems. REASONING ABILITY & DECISION-MAKING SKILLS: Ability to solve practical problems and deal with a variety of concrete variables in situations where only limited standardization may exist. Ability to interpret a variety of instructions furnished in written, verbal, diagram, architectural or electrical drawing, or schedule form. PHYSICAL DEMANDS: Be able to inspect and work maintenance activities in outdoor construction type areas without handicap access. Regularly required to stand; walk; sit; use hands to finger, handle, or feel; and reach with hands to dexterously maneuver small parts in confined spaces, such as wires, screws, and various components within electrical equipment. Regularly required to kneel, crawl, climb ladders and stairs, use scissor lifts and cherry picker. Lift 50 pounds unassisted Lift 50 pounds unassisted and up to 100 pounds assisted. WORK ENVIRONMENT: Some of the work will be performed in an office environment; however, the environment for field inspections exposes the employee to the risk of electric shock, heights, moving mechanical parts, fumes, and airborne particles. Additionally, while working outdoors, the employee is exposed to heat, cold, inclement weather, and ultraviolet radiation from the sun. The noise levels may require hearing protection. title: Staff Solar Performance Engineer - Solar (Multiple Locations)
description: Description The Power global practice at Burns & McDonnell provides a comprehensive approach to power generation solutions from project siting and permitting through turnkey construction and startup and commissioning. Our experience covers the full breadth of renewable power generation technologies, including: utility-scale solar, battery storage, hydrogen, carbon capture, and nuclear plant services. Burns & McDonnell's Power global practice is seeking to hire an experienced Solar Performance Engineer to support our collection of active utility-scale solar engineering, procurement, and construction (EPC) projects through preconstruction, commissioning, testing, and project turnover. This role will focus on solar energy modeling, performance guarantee support, and performance testing for projects typically ranging from 65 MWdc to 400 MWdc. The Solar Performance Engineer will serve as a technical resource across project phases, helping to establish expected plant performance during preconstruction and validating actual performance during commissioning and testing prior to substantial completion. The successful candidate will work closely with engineering, construction, commissioning, project management, and clients to develop site-specific performance test procedures, analyze SCADA and meteorological data, evaluate equipment performance, detect and resolve performance deficiencies, and support successful demonstration of contractual performance guarantees. This position is suited for an individual contributor or technical lead who is comfortable operating in both office and field environments. A successful individual is one who can translate plant design assumptions and contractual obligations into executable testing and analytical methods for EPC project delivery. Responsibilities  Develop and maintain project energy models for utility-scale solar projects using PVsyst to support preconstruction, proposal development, technical reviews, and performance guarantee assumptions.  Review design inputs and assumptions affecting modeled energy and performance, including meteorological data, equipment selection, loss assumptions, clipping, module soiling, and module degradation.  Support the technical review of performance guarantee exhibits, contracts, and test requirements. This includes identifying commercial and technical risks during both contract negotiations and project execution.  Develop capacity and availability test procedures in alignment with contract requirements, project design, and industry-accepted performance methodologies.  Perform capacity and availability test analyses to validate plant performance, determine pass/fail results, and write technical reports to support substantial completion.  Analyze SCADA, inverter, tracker, and MET station data to validate plant behavior, identify underperformance drivers, and support troubleshooting during commissioning and performance testing.  Validate equipment and plant-level performance by comparing measured field results to modeled expectations and design intent.  Coordinate with peers across the engineering, construction, startup and commissioning, and project management teams in order to prepare projects for successful performance testing and final turnover.  Support development of data collection requirements, instrumentation checks, and MET station validation needed for accurate performance testing.  Prepare technical memoranda, performance analyses, and test reports that clearly communicate assumptions, results, risks, and recommended corrective actions.  Perform on-site commissioning, test execution, punch list resolution, and substantial completion support.  Contribute to continuous improvement of Burns & McDonnell's performance modeling, testing procedures, templates, and best practices across the solar EPC portfolio by staying up-to-date on industry trends, modeling methodology, and applicable codes or standards.  Comply with all company policies and standards, including by promoting a strong safety culture.  This role builds on the analytical and cross-functional foundation of Burns & McDonnell's solar engineering work while emphasizing performance validation and project closeout.  Support other duties as assigned to drive successful completion and closeout of EPC solar projects.  All other duties, as assigned. Qualifications  Bachelor Degree in Electrical Engineering or related degree from an ABET accredited program.  3 years of related professional electrical engineering experience, with solar EPC consulting experience preferred. title: Mechanical Engineer (Rotary Actuators) - Space Solar
description: Position Details: Location: Los Angeles (Hawthorne), CA Employment Type: Full-time Department: Starlight Solar Travel: Occasional The Mission Starpath develops and manufactures the technologies that will enable humans to live on the Moon and Mars. Starlight manufactures the lowest cost and highest performance space solar ever, which will power the majority of new satellites built on Earth and all of Starpath's equipment on the Moon and Mars. As a Mechanical Engineer focused on rotary actuators, you will design, analyze, and qualify the rotating mechanisms that deploy and orient Starlight's solar arrays — solar array drive assemblies, deployment hinges, latches, and gimbals — that must operate flawlessly through launch, deployment, and years of continuous motion in the space environment. — torque margin, friction budgets, stiffness, backlash, jitter, and life — and verify performance against requirements through hand calculations and FEA Specify lubrication, materials, and surface treatments suited to vacuum, thermal cycling, and radiation; manage tribology and wear over mission life Design and execute mechanism qualification and acceptance testing — functional, life, vibration, shock, thermal-vacuum, and torque-margin testing Partner closely with electrical, controls, and avionics teams on motor drive electronics, feedback sensing, and closed-loop control of actuators Work with manufacturing to design for assembly, alignment, and rate production of precision rotating hardware Push back on unnecessary complexity — simplify mechanisms, reduce part count, and cut overhead wherever it doesn't add value Required Qualifications: Bachelor's or advanced degree in mechanical, aerospace, or a related engineering discipline 1 years of mechanism, actuator, or precision mechanical design experience (internship and academic experience applicable) Proficiency with 3D CAD and the ability to produce detailed engineering drawings with GD&T Preferred Qualifications: Master's degree in an engineering discipline Hands-on experience designing rotary mechanisms — actuators, gearboxes, gimbals, hinges, or drive assemblies — for flight or other high-reliability applications Proficiency selecting and integrating brushless DC motors, harmonic drives, planetary gearheads, and precision bearings Familiarity with space-rated tribology — dry-film and wet lubricants, bearing preload, and life testing under vacuum and thermal cycling Experience with slip rings, twist capsules, or other rotary power/signal transfer devices Working knowledge of motor drive electronics, encoders/resolvers, and closed-loop position or velocity control Experience executing mechanism qualification campaigns — life test, thermal-vacuum, vibration, and shock — and correlating results to analysis Familiarity with aerospace mechanism standards and practices (e.g., NASA-STD-5017, AIAA mechanisms guidance) Exposure to solar array deployment systems, SADAs, antenna pointing mechanisms, or similar spacecraft mechanisms Exposure to aerospace, space, or other high-reliability hardware environments EAR Requirements: To conform to U.S. Government export regulations, you must be a (i) U.S. citizen or national, (ii) U.S. lawful, permanent resident (aka green card holder), (iii) Refugee under 8 U.S.C. § 1157, or (iv) Asylee under 8 U.S.C. § 1158, or be eligible to obtain the required authorizations from the U.S. Department of State. title: Field Service Technician II – Solar
description: WORK ARRANGEMENT: ON-SITE, FIELD-BASED. THIS IS NOT A REMOTE OR WORK-FROM-HOME JOB. This role is performed in person, outdoors, on solar sites in and around Faribault, MN. You must already live within commuting distance of Faribault, or be prepared to relocate there at your own expense before your start date. You may see this listed as "field-based." That means you drive from your home to job sites rather than reporting to an office each morning. It does not mean you can work from another city or state. Applications from candidates who are not located in — or actively relocating to — the Faribault area cannot be considered for this posting. Territory: [30–90 minutes typical, rarely over 3 hours]. Overnight travel: [under 10%]. Schedule: [M–F, 7am–3pm or 8am–4pm]. On-call: [rotational Saturday 8am–12pm]. Overtime: [paid biweekly; 40–45 hours typical; 1.5x over 40]. SOLAR EXPERIENCE HELPS. IT IS NOT REQUIRED. STRONG ELECTRICAL AND DIAGNOSTIC SKILLS ARE. Energy Support Services keeps solar and energy storage systems safe, reliable, and producing clean power. As a Field Service Technician II – Solar, you’ll work independently on advanced inspections, preventative maintenance, and system troubleshooting — operating safely in high-voltage environments without direct supervision, guiding junior technicians on site, and progressing along a defined pathway toward Technician III. If you have two or more years of serious hands-on technical work in any industry and you’re the person people bring the problem nobody else could figure out, we want your application. COMING FROM ANOTHER TRADE? THIS IS THE PART TO READ. We hire experienced technicians out of other industries at this level regularly, and we build the solar knowledge on top. Here’s how your background translates: Automotive, diesel, or heavy equipment — Root-cause diagnosis, circuit tracing, reading schematics, using a scan tool and DMM, working to torque spec, and writing up findings. You’ll trade flat-rate for a salary, and your tool box for ours. HVAC/R, especially commercial or light-industrial — Control circuits, contactors, VFDs, three-phase power, service calls run solo, and preventative maintenance on a schedule. Very close cousin to this work. Telecommunications, broadband, or utility line work — Working at height, terminations, test equipment, prints, and outdoor work in every kind of weather. Your safety habits are already right. Industrial maintenance, wind, or power generation — Lockout/tagout discipline, medium-voltage awareness, PM programs, and CMMS documentation all carry directly across. Military technical specialties — Power generation, electrical systems, avionics, and electronics maintenance transfer cleanly. The tools you’ll learn (and their equivalents you may already know) I/V curve tracer — measures the performance curve of a string of solar modules to find underperformance. Conceptually similar to putting a vehicle or motor on a load test. Megohmmeter ("Megger") / insulation resistance tester — finds insulation breakdown and ground faults. If you’ve used one in industrial or motor work, it’s the same instrument. Infrared thermography — thermal imaging to find hot spots in connections and modules. If you’ve used a thermal camera on bearings, panels, or refrigerant lines, you’re already there. Drone-based aerial thermal inspection — we pay for your FAA Part 107 and teach you the flight work. PAY $75,000 – $95,000 annually, depending on experience and qualifications. WHAT WE OFFER Tools and equipment: provided. Company truck, company fuel/credit card, and vehicle maintenance card. You will never spend your own money on tools here — no tool truck payment, no tool debt. Bonus: Up to an 8% performance bonus, paid annually. Apparel: Company-provided PPE and flame-resistant clothing kit (bibs, jackets, pants, shirts) at no cost to you. Health: Medical, dental, and vision. We pay 80% of your health insurance premiums. Retirement: 401(k) with up to a 7.5% company match. Time off: PTO accrued each pay period — 120 hours/year (years 0–2), 160 hours (years 3–9), 200 hours (10 years) — plus 11 paid holidays. Family: 8 weeks of paid parental leave. Insurance: Company-paid Life and AD&D insurance at 1x your annual salary. Certifications — we pay, you keep them: OSHA 10/30, NFPA 70E/70B, FAA Part 107 (drone), and our internal O&M Tech course series. These certifications stay with you for the rest of your career. Advancement: A published Field Tech Development Pathway with defined progression to Technician III. You move up on demonstrated capability, not on how long you’ve been here. Education: Tuition reimbursement up to $10,000 per year for approved programs. WHAT YOU'LL DO Safety Lead by example in promoting a safe working culture in the field. Perform approved hazardous electrical energy control procedures and select the exact PPE required for each task. Participate in and actively critique Pre-Job Briefs and Job Safety Analysis (JSA). Apply personal lockout/tagout as a worker, or serve as work leader once approved. Inspections and preventative maintenance Perform comprehensive electrical and mechanical inspections of solar energy systems. Conduct advanced preventative maintenance including infrared thermography, insulation resistance testing, and I/V curve tracing — all of which we train you on. Help build and implement preventative maintenance schedules for your assigned sites. Troubleshooting Independently diagnose and troubleshoot system and operational issues. Operate and troubleshoot safely in 600VAC and 1500VDC environments without direct supervision. Note: 1500VDC is a higher DC voltage than most trades encounter — this is exactly why our safety training is extensive, paid, and mandatory before you work unsupervised. Use specialized diagnostic tools and root-cause analysis to handle equipment repairs and replacements. Documentation Create and maintain detailed, accurate records of inspections, maintenance, and repairs with minimal oversight. Prepare clear technical reports and actionable equipment recommendations for the Team Lead. Knowledge sharing Stay current on industry best practices, safety updates, and emerging technology. Share your expertise and give supportive guidance to junior technicians on site. Help improve the quality, clarity, and safety content of our training materials. Support your teammates and take on other duties as assigned. WHAT YOU NEED High school diploma or equivalent. 2 years of hands-on technical, electrical, or mechanical work in any industry — solar, electrical, automotive, diesel, HVAC/R, telecommunications, wind, power generation, industrial maintenance, utilities, or a military technical specialty. Solid working understanding of electrical fundamentals — AC and DC theory, series and parallel circuits, grounding, and safe work practices around energized equipment. Confident with a multimeter and able to read, interpret, and work from electrical schematics or engineering drawings. Strong analytical, time management, and problem-solving skills, and a track record of working independently without someone checking on you. Strong communication skills and the patience to bring a junior technician along. Valid driver’s license and clean driving record. Helpful, but we’ll train and certify you Solar-specific or grid-tied PV system experience. FAA Part 107 drone certification — we pay for it. OSHA 30 and NFPA 70E — we pay for these as well. Hands-on time with I/V curve tracers, megohmmeters, or insulation testers — or comparable diagnostic instruments from another trade. Familiarity with Data Acquisition Systems (DAS) or SCADA — the monitoring systems that report site performance remotely. PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS Drive a vehicle confidently and with a high degree of safety. Stand for long periods and walk distances up to three miles per day. Navigate ladders, stairs, scaffolding, and ramps while maintaining three points of contact. Have visual acuity for depth perception, no field-of-vision issues, and the ability to distinguish between colors. Work comfortably in a range of climate conditions, including extreme heat (above 100°F) or extreme cold (below 32°F), for periods of more than one hour. Exert up to 50 pounds of force occasionally, up to 30 pounds frequently, and up to 10 pounds constantly to move objects. title: Lead Field Service Technician III – Solar
description: WORK ARRANGEMENT: ON-SITE, FIELD-BASED. THIS IS NOT A REMOTE OR WORK-FROM-HOME JOB. This role is performed in person, outdoors, on solar sites in and around Roseville, Minnesota. You’ll drive from your home to job sites rather than reporting to an office — but you must live in the Roseville region, or relocate there before your start date. You may see this listed as "field-based." That means you drive from your home to job sites rather than reporting to an office each morning. It does not mean you can work from another city or state. Applications from candidates who are not located in — or actively relocating to — the Roseville area cannot be considered for this posting. Territory: [30–90 minutes typical, rarely over 3 hours]. Overnight travel: [under 10%]. Schedule: [M–F, 7am–3pm or 8am–4pm]. On-call: [rotational Saturday 8am–12pm]. Overtime: [paid biweekly; 40–45 hours typical; 1.5x over 40]. MASTER ELECTRICIANS: NO PRIOR SOLAR EXPERIENCE REQUIRED. WE WILL TRAIN YOU. Energy Support Services keeps solar and energy storage systems safe, reliable, and producing clean power. As a Lead Field Service Technician III- Solar, you’ll be the technical authority in the field — leading complex inspections, troubleshooting, and repairs, owning your sites, shaping how the work gets done, and mentoring the technicians coming up behind you. There’s a defined pathway to Technician IV. The license and the electrical judgment are what we can’t teach quickly. Photovoltaics we can. If you hold an active Minnesota Master Electrician license, we will consider you fully with zero solar background. Relocation note : We offer a $3,000 sign-on bonus and relocation assistance to qualified candidates. If you’re a licensed Master Electrician somewhere else in the country and you’ve been curious about renewable energy, this is the posting to look at. COMING FROM ANOTHER SIDE OF THE ELECTRICAL TRADE? This role requires a Master Electrician license because Minnesota law requires it for the electrical work involved. It does not require a solar background. Master Electricians join us from: Commercial and industrial electrical contracting — service work, troubleshooting, code compliance, and permitting. Nearly everything transfers; you’ll learn PV-specific equipment and DC systems. Utility, generation, or substation work — medium-voltage practice, switching, and grounding discipline map directly onto solar plant work. Facilities, manufacturing, or plant electrical leadership — PM programs, LOTO systems, and crew oversight are the same skills we need here. Marine, military, or shipyard electrical — strong safety culture and independent judgment in the field, which is what this job runs on. What you’ll learn on our dime PV system architecture — modules, strings, combiner boxes, inverters, and grid-tie behavior. Solar-specific diagnostics: I/V curve tracing, insulation resistance testing, and infrared thermography. FAA Part 107 drone certification for aerial thermal inspection. OSHA 30, NFPA 70E/70B, and our internal O&M Tech course series. PAY $92,000-115,000 annually , depending on experience and qualifications, plus a $3,000 sign-on bonus and relocation assistance for qualified candidates. WHAT WE OFFER Tools and equipment: provided. Company truck, company fuel/credit card, and vehicle maintenance card. You will never spend your own money on tools here — no tool truck payment, no tool debt. Bonus: Up to an 8% performance bonus, paid annually. Apparel: Company-provided PPE and flame-resistant clothing kit (bibs, jackets, pants, shirts) at no cost to you. Health: Medical, dental, and vision. We pay 80% of your health insurance premiums. Retirement: 401(k) with up to a 7.5% company match. Time off: PTO accrued each pay period — 120 hours/year (years 0–2), 160 hours (years 3–9), 200 hours (10 years) — plus 11 paid holidays. Family: 8 weeks of paid parental leave. Insurance: Company-paid Life and AD&D insurance at 1x your annual salary. Certifications — we pay, you keep them: OSHA 10/30, NFPA 70E/70B, FAA Part 107 (drone), and our internal O&M Tech course series. These certifications stay with you for the rest of your career. Advancement: A published Field Tech Development Pathway with defined progression to Technician IV. You move up on demonstrated capability, not on how long you’ve been here. Education: Tuition reimbursement up to $10,000 per year for approved programs. WHAT YOU'LL DO Safety Ensure all work is performed in accordance with safety policies and procedures. Verify the correct PPE is available and being used properly. Create Personal Lockout/Tagout (PLOTO) and switching lockout plans for approval. Act as work leader for Pre-Job Briefs, Job Safety Analysis, personal LOTO, and switch-plan LOTO. Inspections and preventative maintenance Lead comprehensive inspections of solar power plants. Develop and implement preventative maintenance programs for your sites. Supervise and train junior technicians on inspection and maintenance procedures. Troubleshooting Diagnose and resolve complex system issues, including grid integration and communications faults. Use advanced diagnostic tools and software to address system performance problems. Develop and implement corrective action plans. Documentation Create and maintain comprehensive documentation of inspections, maintenance, and repairs. Prepare technical reports and presentations for management. Provide oversight and direction on work order documentation to junior technicians. Leadership and knowledge Stay current on industry trends and emerging technology. Provide technical guidance and mentorship to junior technicians. Contribute to the development of training materials and procedures. Other duties as assigned. WHAT YOU NEED Active Minnesota Master Electrician license — or an active Master Electrician license in another state that you can convert to a Minnesota license before your start date. We’ll help you navigate the process. The licensed electrical experience your Master license reflects, plus a demonstrated ability to lead work in the field. Proficient knowledge of electrical systems and the ability to read and interpret complex electrical schematics and engineering drawings. Strong analytical, problem-solving, and decision-making skills. Demonstrated ability to lead and mentor technicians in the field. Excellent communication and interpersonal skills. Valid driver’s license and clean driving record. Helpful, but not required — we train and certify you Solar industry or grid-tied PV experience. Master Electricians are considered fully without it. Associate’s degree in electrical engineering or a related field. OSHA 30 and NFPA 70E certifications — we pay for these. FAA Part 107 certification — we pay for this too. Experience with I/V curve tracers, megohmmeters, and insulation testers, or comparable instruments from other electrical work. PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS Drive a vehicle confidently and with a high degree of safety. Stand for long periods and walk distances up to three miles per day. Navigate ladders, stairs, scaffolding, and ramps while maintaining three points of contact. Have visual acuity for depth perception, no field-of-vision issues, and the ability to distinguish between colors. Work comfortably in a range of climate conditions, including extreme heat (above 100°F) or extreme cold (below 32°F), for periods of more than one hour. Exert up to 50 pounds of force occasionally, up to 30 pounds frequently, and up to 10 pounds constantly to move objects. This role involves work on electrical systems associated with solar photovoltaic (PV) equipment. In accordance with Minnesota law, individuals performing electrical work must hold a valid electrician license issued by the Minnesota licensing board. Electrical work must be performed within the scope of the individual’s license classification or under the supervision of a licensed electrician, as required. All work must comply with applicable state codes, permitting requirements, and the National Electrical Code (NEC). title: Mechanical Engineer (Structures) - Space Solar
description: Position Details: Location: Los Angeles (Hawthorne), CA Employment Type: Full-time Department: Starlight Solar Travel: Occasional The Mission Starpath develops and manufactures the technologies that will enable humans to live on the Moon and Mars. mechanisms Perform structural analysis using hand calculations and FEA to size hardware for launch, landing, thermal, and operational loads, maintaining positive margins with appropriate factors of safety Generate detailed manufacturing and assembly drawings with proper GD&T, and select materials, fasteners, and joining methods suited to the space environment Define and execute structural qualification and acceptance testing — static load, vibration, shock, and modal — and correlate analytical models to test data Work closely with manufacturing to design for manufacturability and rate, and with thermal, avionics, propulsion, and controls teams to integrate structures into the larger system Drive mass optimization and design simplification without compromising structural integrity Push back on unnecessary complexity — simplify load paths, reduce part count, and cut overhead wherever it doesn't add value Required Qualifications: Bachelor's or advanced degree in mechanical, aerospace, structural, or a related engineering discipline 1 years of mechanical design or structural engineering experience (internship and academic experience applicable) Proficiency with 3D CAD and the ability to produce detailed engineering drawings with GD&T Preferred Qualifications: Master's degree in an engineering discipline Proficiency with FEA tools (e.g., Nastran, Abaqus, Ansys, or Femap) for static, dynamic, thermal, and fatigue analysis Experience designing flight hardware that has survived launch and operated in space, or other high-reliability hardware for extreme environments Familiarity with launch and landing load environments — quasi-static loads, random vibration, shock, and coupled loads analysis Hands-on structural test experience — static load, vibration, shock, and modal survey — including test-to-model correlation Experience with lightweight, load-optimized structures across machined, sheet-metal, welded, and composite/bonded construction Knowledge of materials selection, fasteners, and joint design for thermal cycling, vacuum, and radiation environments Experience designing mechanisms such as deployables, hinges, latches, and actuators Familiarity with aerospace structural standards and margin policies (e.g., NASA-STD-5001, GEVS) Exposure to aerospace, space, or other high-reliability hardware environments EAR 1157, or (iv) Asylee under 8 U.S.C. § 1158, or be eligible to obtain the required authorizations from the U.S. Department of State. title: Estimator

Review proposed schedules for establishing installation rates and general project execution. Create and manage detailed quantity and costs take-offs from either, conceptual, preliminary or detailed engineering packages . Prepare estimates / true-ups at different levels of project completion , as requested. Organize, research, and strategically plan for estimate preparation, pricing, scheduling, and final submission to the customer. Review options and recommend best solution based on cost, engineering, quality or availability of materials. Facilitation and formulation of crew sizing, resources and productivity. Demonstrates proficiency in development, issu ance and management of RFP’s to qualified vendors and subcontractors. Responsible for compiling comparison metrics to determine most commercially and technically compliant costs . Calculates various statistical data: quantity take-offs, material price lists, labor costs, equipment cost, and specialty items. Tracks and researches historical data (purchase orders, subcontracts, productivity analysis reports, etc.) and compiles summary reports and bridging documents to develop guidelines and precedence for future estimates. Works with Preconstruction Manager to review and approve components of the bid package, submittals and decisions through the process. Prepares and presents internal preview and final estimate review process with the Preconstruction Team. Communicates with site teams over the phone and in person at the project sites concerning items such as work methods, production requirements, and historical data. Complies with BUILD Renewables Company policies and procedures and displays professional ethics in the bid process. Input, evaluate and manage all cost data within BUILD Renewables estimating software (HCSS). Track project clarifications and assumptions made during the estimating process. Assist the project team with generating project cost allocations. Other related responsibilities as assigned. Additional Functions Keep informed of new technologies and processes that could lower costs and/or improve quality. Investigate and evaluate labor in the local and regional market to determine estimate requirements on wages, per-diem, housing, travel and other requirements necessary to ensure the estimate captures the appropriate plan and cost. Ability to work accurately and quickly under pressure. Ability to work on multiple assignments simultaneously. Qualifications Bachelor’s degree in Construction Management , Construction Engineering or equivalent experience. Minimum of 2 years of renewable energy industry estimating experience, includi ng knowledge of estimating techniques , cost control and material pricing. title: Solar Maintenance Technician
description: THE ROLE: Solar Maintenance Technician Spruce Power, a leading provider of solar energy to over 53,000 customers, is the nation’s 1 independent residential solar servicing company, and offers customers a comprehensive, end-to-end servicing solution including financial asset management, account services, billing, fleet management, and customer support to third-party asset owners and retail customers. Spruce is headquartered in Denver, CO, with a presence in Houston, TX and the Bay Area, CA. This role is envisioned to be located in New Jersey. Spruce is seeking a Solar Maintenance Technician who is responsible for the inspection, repair, and maintenance of solar energy systems, ensuring their optimal performance and longevity. This role involves conducting routine checks, troubleshooting system issues, and performing necessary repairs or replacements. Solar Maintenance Technicians also assist with system installations and provide technical support to clients. They work closely with solar engineers, project managers, and other team members to ensure efficient operations and customer satisfaction. Key Responsibilities Include: Inspect and maintain solar energy systems: Diagnose and troubleshoot technical problems related to solar PV systems, including electrical and mechanical issues. Carry out repairs, replacements, or adjustments to solar components as needed. Develop and implement a preventive maintenance program to ensure optimal performance and longevity of solar systems. Maintain accurate records of all maintenance activities, including inspections, repairs, replacements, and parts used. Collaborate with engineers and project managers to ensure proper equipment setup and integration. Address customer inquiries, concerns, and complaints related to solar system performance. Offer technical guidance and troubleshooting assistance over the phone, through email, or during site visits. Ensure customer satisfaction and provide education on system operation and maintenance. Operate a company-issued vehicle with respect and integrity. Keep up to date with the latest trends, technologies, and best practices in the solar industry. Other duties as assigned by management. QUALIFICATIONS Proven experience in solar maintenance or a related field. Must possess a current and valid Residential or General Electrician license. title: Licensed Traveling Electrician - Commercial Solar
description: marsenergygroup.com MARS Energy EPC – Midwest is entering a new phase of growth, and we’re looking for multiple licensed electricians at the Journeyman level or above to join our field team. You’ll work hands-on across Utility-Scale and Commercial & Industrial (C&I) Solar and Battery Energy Storage System (BESS) projects throughout the Midwest. In this role, you won’t just install systems- you’ll lead on-site execution, support safety excellence, and mentor the next generation of apprentices. Licensing Requirement: A valid electrical license (Journeyman, Master, or equivalent contractor-level license) is required for this role. This is not a role where unlicensed work experience qualifies as a substitute. Licensing is required to meet Illinois apprenticeship ratio regulations and to maintain compliance during audits. Reliable transportation and personal tools are required to ensure you're ready to hit the ground running. Must reside in the greater Chicagoland area or be willing to relocate prior to start date. Prevailing wage rates apply depending on scope of work and specific project. TRAVEL REQUIREMENTS: This is a 100% travel position. Project assignments may be located throughout Illinois and the Midwest region, including Illinois, Indiana, Wisconsin, Michigan, Iowa, Minnesota, Missouri, and other surrounding states as business needs dictate. Employees should expect frequent travel and may be required to stay overnight for several days or multiple weeks at a time depending on project location and duration. MARS Energy provides travel accommodation in accordance with company policy. Depending on project location and travel distance, employees may qualify for company paid lodging, per diem, and/or mileage reimbursement. Candidates must be willing and able to travel extensively throughout the Midwest and work away from home for extended periods when required by project needs. JOB RESPONSIBILITIES: Travel to project sites throughout Illinois and the Midwest region as required to support utility-scale solar, C&I solar, and BESS construction projects. Install, repair, and maintain electrical components and systems in accordance with National Electrical Code (NEC) and local regulations. Perform wiring, conduit installation, panel mounting, and terminations for solar PV systems. Conduct testing and troubleshooting to ensure the integrity and safety of electrical systems and components. Read and interpret electrical schematics, blueprints, and technical specifications. Ensure all installations meet MARS quality and safety standards. Collaborate with other trades and project teams to ensure timely and efficient project completion. Mentor apprentices and less experienced electricians, ensuring they adhere to company safety and performance standards. Adhere to all company and industry safety protocols, including lockout/tagout procedures. Report and sign off on apprentice OJT (on the job training) hours to the electrical superintendent. EDUCATION/CERTIFICATIONS: Journeyman license or equivalent required Advanced classroom training of electrical theory and code required OSHA 10 / 30 certification strongly preferred High school diploma required EXPERIENCE: 3 years of experience in commercial or industrial electrical within the Solar industry preferred. 4 years of general electrical experience with the ability to prove hours required. Must have in-depth knowledge of NEC Code and OSHA 1926 Construction standards. Experience working with Three Phase Services (208V and 480V). OSHA 10 or 30 certification is a plus. Must maintain a valid driver's license, reliable transportation, and a clean MVR to support travel requirements. SKILLS/KNOWLEDGE/ABILITIES: Must have in depth knowledge of NEC Code and OSHA 1926 Construction standards. Ability to find and reference NEC codes as it relates to each project. Ability to read and interpret blueprints and schematics. Strong troubleshooting and problem-solving skills. Acute attention to detail with excellent communication skills. Ability to work in various conditions, including rooftops of any height/pitch, ladders, and confined spaces. Ability to lift, pull, push materials up to 50lbs. consistently to complete assigned job tasks. Ability to meet hard and fast deadlines while managing multiple projects. PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS & WORKING CONDITIONS: Ability to lift, carry, push, and pull materials and equipment weighing up to 50 lbs. consistently throughout the workday. Able to stand, walk, bend, kneel, and climb ladders or stairs for extended periods. Comfortable working in elevated positions, including rooftops of varying heights and pitches, aerial lifts, and scaffolding. Must be able to work in confined spaces and tight electrical enclosures as required by project scope. Willing and able to work in all weather conditions (heat, cold, rain, snow, wind) typical of Midwest job sites. Ability to operate hand and power tools safely and efficiently for prolonged periods. Must be capable of driving long distances to project sites and maintaining alertness during travel (clean MVR required). Regularly required to do Personal Protective Equipment (PPE) including hard hats, safety glasses, gloves, harnesses, and arc flash gear. Ability to communicate clearly on noisy, active construction sites using both verbal instruction and hand signals. BENEFITS: 401(k) 401(k) matching Dental insurance Health insurance Life insurance- paid for by company Paid Holidays (6) Paid time off (PTO) - Accrual begins Day One! Sick time Vision insurance Cell phone stipend

description: At Sunrun, we’re on a mission to change the way the world interacts with energy, and we’re building a company and brand that puts power at the center of life. We’re unlike any other residential energy company. Our vertically integrated model gives us total control over every part of the energy lifecycle – from sale through installation and beyond – so you can find endless opportunities for growth. Come join a career you can grow in and a culture you can run with. Who We Are We’re on a mission to make energy more reliable and affordable for more people. We provide an opportunity with storage and solar to help people access greater energy independence without the big upfront costs. Sunrun is the largest dedicated residential solar and storage company in the country and has a mission to bring stably priced resilient power to the masses. About Sunrun Since 2007, Sunrun has grown into America's 1 home solar and battery company. We got here by putting our people’s safety and growth first. title: Senior Project Manager
description: About UGE UGE is a full lifecycle renewable energy development company specializing in distributed generation and utility-scale solar PV and Battery Energy Storage Systems (BESS). We develop, design, build, and operate clean energy assets across the United States from the first site assessment through to commercial operation. We're a mission-driven team that moves fast, solves hard problems, and is genuinely committed to accelerating the clean energy transition. The Opportunity The Senior Project Manager (SPM) is responsible for taking conceptual designs to operational reality. This role requires a deep understanding and experience in leading multiple complex projects simultaneously while supporting other Project Managers on their projects and shepherding their successes. This includes planning, scope delineation, design collaboration, procurement coordination, contracting, installation, and closeout/handoff to Portfolio Operations. The SPM creates and tracks project schedule progress against milestones, formulates and tracks full Development and EPC budget and payment forecasting needs, tracks and audits prevailing wage/certified payroll records for projects, and prepares identified reports to UGE Management. The SPM must possess a comprehensive knowledge of C&I or community solar components, installation methods, quality control, best practices, AHJ/Utility process and communication requirements, regulatory standards, scheduling, budget tracking and forecasting, progress payment schedules, subcontracting, risk management, and closeout packages. What You'll Do Strategic Oversight and Leadership: Provides overarching leadership and strategic direction for multiple projects across any region(s). Assumes responsibility (schedule and cost) for the successful completion of projects, from Notice to Proceed (NTP) to Commercial Operation Date (COD) and Portfolio Operations hand-off, ensuring alignment with organizational goals and objectives. Advanced Contractual Management: Spearheads negotiations and final recommendations regarding contracts, playing a critical role in the recommendations and management of construction activities, consultants, and vendors. Owns contractual oversight responsibilities on projects for major subcontractors, ensuring safety, compliance, quality, and efficiency. Budget and Financial Management: Oversees the preservation and optimization of the IRR from the NTP budget approval stage through the handoff to Portfolio Operations. Responsible for the overall EPC budget from NTP to Final Completion, making key decisions to preserve the as-modeled condition of the project. Team Leadership and Development: Directly oversees internal resources for task management, providing leadership, mentorship, and support to other Project Managers. Fosters professional development and growth within the team, offering guidance and coaching to lower levels of Project Managers and subordinate roles. Acts as a role model, setting high standards and expectations for project execution and team performance. Cross-Functional Collaboration: Facilitates and enhances collaboration between Development, Engineering, Procurement, and Portfolio Operations teams, ensuring cohesiveness and alignment in project execution. Leads critical meetings and discussions, representing the project team in high-level strategic meetings and decision-making processes. Quality and Compliance Assurance: Ensures that all projects adhere to industry standards, legal regulations, and company policies. Implements and oversees quality control measures, consistently monitoring project progress and performance. Ensures Certified payroll for contractors is collected and properly certified for regulations. Risk Management and Mitigation: Identifies potential risks and challenges at the regional level, developing and implementing effective mitigation strategies. Holds ultimate accountability for resolving high-level issues and challenges that arise during project execution. Stakeholder Engagement and Communication: Maintains strong relationships with key stakeholders, including clients, vendors, partners, Utilities, Authorities Having Jurisdiction (AHJs), and other regulatory bodies. Ensures effective and transparent communication across all levels of the project team and external entities. Travel : 15-25% Travel to Project Sites Who You'll Work With Reports to Managing Director, Project Execution Manages multiple external parties as needed to complete projects successfully. Work Location & Schedule This is an onsite hybrid position. Candidates are expected to work from our New York City office four days per week, with one work-from-home day each week. Candidates who are not currently located within commuting distance of either office must be willing to relocate. Relocation assistance is not provided. What We're Looking For Bachelor’s degree in engineering or other quantitative educational background, or equivalent experience. A minimum of 6 years of relevant solar or energy storage project management experience (Solar PV, Energy Storage, or Electrical sectors) Superior oral and written communication skills, tailored for higher-level stakeholder engagement. Advanced ability to drive project teams and entities to success, ensuring deadlines and goals are met. Leadership in fostering a collaborative environment and proactive approach to seeking information and research. Expert in complex problem-solving abilities, including navigating challenging project scenarios and leading innovative solutions. Detail oriented while capable of seeing and understanding the full picture. Collaborate as part of a broader project management team to include, mentor, and develop others. description: At RES, we’re looking for purpose-driven individuals who are passionate about restoration and sustainability, and who want their work to make a lasting environmental impact. title: Solar Technician
description: Requisition ID  171624 Job Category: Maintenance / Construction / Operations Job Level: Individual Contributor Business Unit: Energy Delivery Work Type: Onsite Job Location: Moss Landing Department Summary / Facility Summary PG&E's Power Generation Department manages and operates the largest privately-owned hydroelectric system in the nation. These renewable electric generation resources, located mostly at high elevation in California's Sierra Nevada and southern Cascade mountains include 68 powerhouses, 184 miles of canals, 41 miles of flumes, 135 miles of tunnels, 19 miles of penstock pipes, 99 reservoirs, and 142,000 acres of watershed lands - all covered by 26 operating licenses issued by the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (FERC). In addition, the department is expanding its presence in renewable generation such as wind, photovoltaic (PV) solar, and fuel cells. The company recently received authorization to construct 250 MW of PV generation, most of which is expected to be located in the Central Valley of California. Additionally, the company also recently received authorization to construct a 200 kW Fuel Cell facility at SF State University and two 1.4 MW Fuel Cell facilities (one at SF State and one at CSU East Bay). Position Summary This is an IBEW Local 1245 represented classification, which has over 100 years of experience representing employees at PG&E. This job is subject to collective bargaining. The Solar Technician position is a journeyman level position. Required skills are those of a journeyman electrician or Power Plant Technician who has qualified in the Electrical skill block discipline. The successful candidate shall be able to perform work assignments, with or without direct supervision. Duties include the ability to inspect, evaluate, test, clean, calibrate, and maintain solar photovoltaic module systems, mounting hardware, combiner fuse boxes, inverters, switchgear, circuit breakers, transformers, batteries, data acquisition systems, relays, programmable logic controllers, revenue meters, weather stations, fuel cell equipment, and other AC and DC equipment. This position may involve frequent professional interaction with outside contract personnel and other site representatives. Employees will be required to travel between facilities located within their assigned geographic area as a part of their normal job responsibilities. PG&E is providing the hourly rate that the company in good faith believes it might pay for this position at the time of the job posting. This position is subject to collectively bargained hourly wage rates and increases. The starting wage rate for this position is $65.27 per hour. This wage rate is specific to the locality of the job. The wage rate is based on multiple factors, including, but not limited to, specific skills, education, licenses or certifications, experience, market value, geographic location, collective bargaining agreements, and internal equity. Responsibilities: Ability to apply safe work practices and perform facilities’ clearance and switching procedures per PG&E safety policies and procedures. Work safely and effectively with or without direct supervision while conducting safety tailboards with self and others as required. Review and understand technical documents such as OEM manuals, electrical single-line, wiring diagrams, schematics, relay settings, and other site-specific diagrams. Work safely in close proximity with energized electrical voltages up to 12 kV A.C. Troubleshoot and perform routine preventative and corrective electrical maintenance duties on site equipment such as batteries and chargers, wiring and terminations, ground systems, fuses, filters, inverters, transformers, monitoring equipment, circuit breakers, and switchgear. Familiarity with Computerized Maintenance Management Systems used to input data into the work management system including creating equipment job notifications, performing the work tasks, and closing out the jobs. Helps develop, review, and update operating and maintenance procedures to ensure they are complete and accurate. Monitor and Record routine operating data and keep Supervisor regularly informed of equipment status. Assist in ensuring regulatory compliance is maintained at all times and any identified deficiencies are addressed at once. Conduct all assigned activities in a professional, business-like manner Qualifications Minimum Qualifications: Must be at least 18 years of age Must possess a High School diploma or GED Must possess a valid State Driver's License with good driving record Must hold a state or PG&E certification as a Journeyman Electrician, IBEW/JATC-sanctioned Electrician apprenticeship OR have a minimum of 5 years experience operating and maintaining electrical equipment/utility solar generating facilities. Be able to work alone in isolated areas, outside under varying temperature extremes Willingness to work overtime as required Desired Qualifications: Successful completion of an accredited solar photovoltaic technical training program Experience in working on solar photovoltaic project sites, either in the construction or operations and maintenance phase Basic computer proficiency with Microsoft Office suite in a Windows environment SAP work management process experience Factory certifications to repair Satcon, Advanced Energy, or SMA inverters.

Utility, generation, or substation work — medium-voltage practice, switching, and grounding discipline map directly onto solar plant work. Develop and implement corrective action plans. Documentation Create and maintain comprehensive documentation of inspections, maintenance, and repairs. Strong analytical, problem-solving, and decision-making skills. Demonstrated ability to lead and mentor technicians in the field. Excellent communication and interpersonal skills. description: WORK ARRANGEMENT: ON-SITE, FIELD-BASED. THIS IS NOT A REMOTE OR WORK-FROM-HOME JOB. This role is performed in person, outdoors, on solar sites in and around Las Cruces, New Mexico. You must already live within commuting distance of Las Cruces, or be prepared to relocate there at your own expense before your start date. You may see this listed as "field-based." IT IS NOT REQUIRED. STRONG ELECTRICAL AND DIAGNOSTIC SKILLS ARE. Energy Support Services keeps solar and energy storage systems safe, reliable, and producing clean power. As a Field Service Technician II – Solar, you’ll work independently on advanced inspections, preventative maintenance, and system troubleshooting — operating safely in high-voltage environments without direct supervision, guiding junior technicians on site, and progressing along a defined pathway toward Technician III. If you have two or more years of serious hands-on technical work in any industry and you’re the person people bring the problem nobody else could figure out, we want your application. COMING FROM ANOTHER TRADE? THIS IS THE PART TO READ. We hire experienced technicians out of other industries at this level regularly, and we build the solar knowledge on top. Here’s how your background translates: Automotive, diesel, or heavy equipment — Root-cause diagnosis, circuit tracing, reading schematics, using a scan tool and DMM, working to torque spec, and writing up findings. You’ll trade flat-rate for a salary, and your tool box for ours. HVAC/R, especially commercial or light-industrial — Control circuits, contactors, VFDs, three-phase power, service calls run solo, and preventative maintenance on a schedule. Very close cousin to this work. Telecommunications, broadband, or utility line work — Working at height, terminations, test equipment, prints, and outdoor work in every kind of weather. Your safety habits are already right. Industrial maintenance, wind, or power generation — Lockout/tagout discipline, medium-voltage awareness, PM programs, and CMMS documentation all carry directly across. Military technical specialties — Power generation, electrical systems, avionics, and electronics maintenance transfer cleanly. The tools you’ll learn (and their equivalents you may already know) I/V curve tracer — measures the performance curve of a string of solar modules to find underperformance. Conceptually similar to putting a vehicle or motor on a load test. Megohmmeter ("Megger") / insulation resistance tester — finds insulation breakdown and ground faults. If you’ve used one in industrial or motor work, it’s the same instrument. Infrared thermography — thermal imaging to find hot spots in connections and modules. If you’ve used a thermal camera on bearings, panels, or refrigerant lines, you’re already there. Drone-based aerial thermal inspection — we pay for your FAA Part 107 and teach you the flight work. PAY $75,000 – $95,000 annually, depending on experience and qualifications. WHAT WE OFFER Tools and equipment: provided. Company truck, company fuel/credit card, and vehicle maintenance card. You will never spend your own money on tools here — no tool truck payment, no tool debt. Bonus: Up to an 8% performance bonus, paid annually. Apparel: Company-provided PPE and flame-resistant clothing kit (bibs, jackets, pants, shirts) at no cost to you. Health: Medical, dental, and vision. We pay 80% of your health insurance premiums. Retirement: 401(k) with up to a 7.5% company match. Time off: PTO accrued each pay period — 120 hours/year (years 0–2), 160 hours (years 3–9), 200 hours (10 years) — plus 11 paid holidays. Family: 8 weeks of paid parental leave. Insurance: Company-paid Life and AD&D insurance at 1x your annual salary. Certifications — we pay, you keep them: OSHA 10/30, NFPA 70E/70B, FAA Part 107 (drone), and our internal O&M Tech course series. These certifications stay with you for the rest of your career. Advancement: A published Field Tech Development Pathway with defined progression to Technician III. You move up on demonstrated capability, not on how long you’ve been here. Education: Tuition reimbursement up to $10,000 per year for approved programs. WHAT YOU'LL DO Safety Lead by example in promoting a safe working culture in the field. Perform approved hazardous electrical energy control procedures and select the exact PPE required for each task. Participate in and actively critique Pre-Job Briefs and Job Safety Analysis (JSA). Apply personal lockout/tagout as a worker, or serve as work leader once approved. Inspections and preventative maintenance Perform comprehensive electrical and mechanical inspections of solar energy systems. Conduct advanced preventative maintenance including infrared thermography, insulation resistance testing, and I/V curve tracing — all of which we train you on. Help build and implement preventative maintenance schedules for your assigned sites. Troubleshooting Independently diagnose and troubleshoot system and operational issues. Operate and troubleshoot safely in 600VAC and 1500VDC environments without direct supervision. Note: 1500VDC is a higher DC voltage than most trades encounter — this is exactly why our safety training is extensive, paid, and mandatory before you work unsupervised. Use specialized diagnostic tools and root-cause analysis to handle equipment repairs and replacements. Documentation Create and maintain detailed, accurate records of inspections, maintenance, and repairs with minimal oversight. Prepare clear technical reports and actionable equipment recommendations for the Team Lead. Knowledge sharing Stay current on industry best practices, safety updates, and emerging technology. Share your expertise and give supportive guidance to junior technicians on site. Help improve the quality, clarity, and safety content of our training materials. Support your teammates and take on other duties as assigned. WHAT YOU NEED High school diploma or equivalent. 2 years of hands-on technical, electrical, or mechanical work in any industry — solar, electrical, automotive, diesel, HVAC/R, telecommunications, wind, power generation, industrial maintenance, utilities, or a military technical specialty. Solid working understanding of electrical fundamentals — AC and DC theory, series and parallel circuits, grounding, and safe work practices around energized equipment. Confident with a multimeter and able to read, interpret, and work from electrical schematics or engineering drawings. Strong analytical, time management, and problem-solving skills, and a track record of working independently without someone checking on you. Strong communication skills and the patience to bring a junior technician along. Valid driver’s license and clean driving record. Helpful, but we’ll train and certify you Solar-specific or grid-tied PV system experience. FAA Part 107 drone certification — we pay for it. OSHA 30 and NFPA 70E — we pay for these as well. Hands-on time with I/V curve tracers, megohmmeters, or insulation testers — or comparable diagnostic instruments from another trade. Familiarity with Data Acquisition Systems (DAS) or SCADA — the monitoring systems that report site performance remotely. title: PV Solar Technician II
description: ACCIONA Energía is the biggest 100% renewable energy company with no fossil legacy in the world. With more than 30 years of experience and operations in 20 countries on five continents, ACCIONA Energía offers a wide portfolio of tailored energy solutions so that its corporate and institutional clients can meet their decarbonisation goals. This includes the development, engineering, construction, operation and maintenance of renewable power plants -mainly wind and photovoltaic technologies-, energy sales and management and marketing, energy services, self-consumption, electric mobility and new technologies such as storage and green hydrogen. ACCIONA Energía is governed by the most demanding environmental, social and corporate governance (ESG) criteria. ACCIONA Energía is seeking a PV Solar Technician to support operations at our Fort Bend Solar Farm located in East Bernard, TX. This role is responsible for maintaining and troubleshooting solar energy systems to ensure their safe, reliable, and efficient performance. Job Description Perform preventive and corrective maintenance on PV systems, inverters, and battery storage equipment. Troubleshoot electrical and mechanical issues while following strict safety protocols. Conduct site inspections, safety analyses, and participate in safety training and emergency drills. Support inventory control, documentation, and warranty tracking for replacement parts. Operate and maintain electrical equipment up to 345kV, including performing lock-out/tag-out procedures. Communicate effectively with the operations center and cross-functional teams to resolve issues. Assist with new installations, commissioning, and project-based site work. Other responsibilities as assigned. Required Skills and Competencies 2 years of directly related experience in solar, renewable energy, or equivalent electrical environments. Hands-on problem solver who thrives in fast-paced outdoor settings, demonstrating strong technical skills and an unwavering commitment to safety. Experience with electrical and mechanical systems, including knowledge of electrical theory, power electronics, substation equipment, and control systems. Proficient with hand and power tools, electrical test equipment, and capable of reading schematics, one-line, and wiring diagrams while working independently with high attention to detail. Capable of working in varying weather conditions, lifting up to 50 pounds, and performing physically demanding tasks in field environments. Hold a high school diploma or equivalent (technical degree or journeyman certification preferred), a valid driver’s license, and the ability to obtain a U.S. passport. Willingness to travel and work night shifts or extended hours as needed. Pay & Benefits: Base Pay: $28 – $38 (based on experience, education, and skillset) plus on-call pay. 5% Annual Performance Bonus (based on individual performance and company metrics) and 5% Availability Bonus. Benefits after 90 days: 401(k) with company match and immediate vesting, life insurance, disability coverage, paid parental leave, and other optional plans. 15 days of PTO (with 1 additional day per year of service), 9 public holidays, and 2 flexible holidays. $50 monthly reimbursement for health, wellness, or fitness-related memberships and equipment. Technician Progression Program: provides technical training in support of your career growth and compensation advancement as a technician. Working Conditions: All technicians are provided with the necessary tools and personal protective equipment (PPE) to work safely and efficiently. Uniform allowance to keep you equipped and comfortable on-site. GWO (Global Wind Organization) training and certifications to ensure compliance with international safety standards. title: Solar O&M Technician
description: Join one of Rochester's Top Workplaces! We would love to welcome you to the team! Our Mission: Loyal to People. Loyal to Planet. GreenSpark Solar creates fiercely local, cost-effective, clean energy options in the Greater Rochester Community. We feel a huge responsibility to succeed at GreenSpark. As a B Corporation, success is directly tied to honoring our triple bottom line of commitments to people (our employees and their families, our Customers and residents of the communities where we do business), planet (our local and the broader global environment) and profits (providing capital to grow, revenue to share among our employees, and a return to our investors). This is important work, and we have fun doing it. Our Core Values Believe in People Keep it Real Find Joy Be a Leader Work Together GreenSpark Solar is seeking an experienced Solar Operations & Maintenance (O&M) Technician to join our team! In this advanced field-based role, you'll be responsible for monitoring, troubleshooting, maintaining, and repairing residential and commercial renewable energy systems to ensure they operate safely and efficiently. This is a hands-on position that requires working in a variety of environmental conditions and is not a desk job. You'll diagnose and resolve technical issues both independently and collaboratively while delivering exceptional customer service during onsite interactions. Working closely with fellow field technicians and internal teams, you'll help maximize system performance while upholding GreenSpark's commitment to safety, quality, and operational excellence. Essential Job Functions & Key Responsibilities: Pre-Maintenance Preparation: Prepare for upcoming visits in the days prior by researching the case notes, adding pertinent data from customer build files, and obtaining necessary parts and supplies from warehouse stock. On-Site Maintenance & Repair : Perform maintenance, service, troubleshooting, and repair of solar photovoltaic systems and ancillary equipment (e.g., batteries, monitoring systems, EV chargers). Record Keeping : Update internal service records, time logs, and gather information for warranty claims. Keep accurate and detailed records of site visits. Customer Communication : Clearly communicate issues and resolutions to customers, office staff, and the operations team. Safety & Equipment Management : Adhere to safety policies, maintain tools, meters, truck stock, and spare parts inventory. Training & Reporting : Attend training sessions and create reports on system operability and major issues. PV Installation: During periods where there is no maintenance to perform: Install photovoltaic (PV) systems to include ballasted systems on flat roofs, pitched roofs and ground mounted systems. Work will include roof penetrations, mounting of racking systems, panels onto racking, inverter(s) and conduit between solar arrays and inverter(s), wire management, occasional trench work At all times, ensure personal, crew, and job site safety in accordance with Company and OSHA safety standards; General construction tasks, and operation of hand, and power tools, with occasional heavy machinery; Heavy lifting of modules, ballasts, and installation material to the location of the installation, typically via the use of ladders, cranes or lifts; Install to system design specifications that meet the highest quality standards, and in accordance with all applicable codes and standards; Support tool management and proper maintenance of personal and company tools and install vehicles; Practice the company core values in all daily activities; Follow daily instruction of your Crew Lead and Project Managers. Education & Qualifications: Education: High school diploma, GED, technical/trade school training, or equivalent combination of education and experience preferred. Experience: Two (2) or more years of experience in photovoltaic (PV) maintenance, including PV DC systems, AC medium-voltage systems, and network communications. Technical Skills: Experience with SCADA, DAS, UPS systems, and electrical testing equipment such as thermal imaging cameras, IV curve tracers, and megohm (megger) testers. Knowledge: Working knowledge of the National Electrical Code (NEC), industry design and construction practices, and the ability to read and interpret electrical drawings, diagrams, and schematics. Software: Proficiency with Microsoft Office and Google Workspace. Certifications: Valid driver's license required. OSHA 10-Hour Construction and NFPA 70E certifications are preferred but may be obtained after hire. Professional Skills: Strong troubleshooting, problem-solving, communication, and customer service skills with the ability to work independently and collaboratively. Work Environment, Physical Requirements & Travel Work Environment: Perform work indoors and outdoors in a variety of weather and environmental conditions, including commercial facilities, residential rooftops, elevated work areas, and uneven terrain. Physical Requirements: Ability to stand, walk, bend, kneel, climb ladders, and work at heights for extended periods. Must be able to lift, carry, push, and pull 50 pounds on a regular basis. Schedule: Primarily Monday–Friday with an early morning start (typically 7:00AM). Participation in an on-call rotation, including evenings and weekends, may be required. Travel: Ability to travel to project sites, including overnight travel as needed. Travel may account for approximately 50% of the role based on operational needs. A company vehicle may be available for business travel when applicable. Compensation & Benefits: Pay Range: $25.00–$40.00 per hour, depending on experience. Pay Schedule : Weekly pay. Prevailing Wage: Opportunities to earn prevailing wage compensation may be available when assigned to qualifying projects. Performance Bonus : Quarterly bonus potential based on company performance. 401(k) Plan : Profit-sharing plan to help you save for retirement. Medical, Dental & Vision Insurance: Comprehensive medical, dental, and vision coverage with company contributions toward employee and dependent coverage. Paid Time Off: Accrue up to three (3) weeks (120 hours) of paid time off (PTO) annually, with additional PTO available based on years of service. Paid Sick Leave: Paid sick leave in accordance with company policy. Paid Company Closure Days: Eight (8) paid company-wide closure days each year. Parental Bonding Leave: Paid parental bonding leave for eligible employees. Equipment Provision : Necessary tools, gear, and personal protective equipment (PPE) provided. Employee Support : Access to Employee Assistance Program (EAP) for confidential support and counseling services. Professional Growth : Opportunities for training and development programs. Team Building : Annual company retreat to strengthen collaboration and company culture. Pet-Friendly Workplace : Enjoy a work environment where pets are welcome. If you have roofing, electrical, and/or solar experience and want to work at an amazing company then apply today! We do not tolerate harassment or discrimination of any kind and seek to remove barriers and increase opportunities, access, and advancement for all people. Do not let historical barriers prevent you from jumping on this life-changing opportunity – reach out and ask questions if you have them – we are here!
