title: Senior Solar Project Engineer
description: Do you want to be a part of the clean energy movement? Are you passionate about improving our environment for this generation and those to follow? Are you ready to take on new challenges and collaborate with a future-focused team leading the way into new markets? Join Nexamp! This is where you can learn from industry leaders and become one yourself. It's fast-paced, mission-based work that challenges the status quo. Be on the team that's changing the world. What we’re looking for: Nexamp is seeking to hire a Senior Solar Project Engineer to join its Project Engineering team. In this role, you will lead engineering execution for complex solar and energy storage projects throughout the project lifecycle, ensuring technically sound, cost-effective, and constructible solutions. You will owns critical technical decisions, drives cross-functional alignment, and supports successful project delivery while advancing engineering standards, mentoring team members, and implementing continuous improvements. We are accepting candidates across our hub offices of Boston, MA, Chicago, IL, and Washington DC offices where you will be hybrid. You will report to the Manager, Project Engineering. What you’ll do: Lead engineering and design execution across the full project life cycle for complex PV and BESS assets. Coordinate internal teams and external engineers and vendors to deliver optimized engineering packages that meet project requirements and business objectives. Own project-level technical decision-making by identifying risks early, driving resolution of ambiguous design and construction issues. Constantly seek a balance between cost, schedule, constructability, and long-term asset performance. Direct cross-functional collaboration with Design, Development, Engineering, Estimation, Pre-Deployment, Deployment, Project Finance, and Grid Integration teams. Ensure that the basis of design and plan of record for project execution is understood by the entire project team. Lead development maintenance, and interpretation of plant performance models and related technical analyses for your assigned projects. Leverage models and analyses to evaluate project- and portfolio-level tradeoff decisions, value engineering opportunities, and focus areas for optimization. Review and approve key engineering deliverables, equipment selections, procurement inputs, RFIs, Submittals, construction drawing markups, and other project artifacts. Verify technical accuracy, constructability, and code compliance of all design specifications, and ensure that overall design spec will support project objectives. Mentor lower-level Project Engineering team members through technical coaching, design reviews, work shadowing, and direct practical feedback. Own department-level process improvement initiatives, standards updates, and tooling enhancements for Project Engineering. Partner with the Technical Strategy Team to evaluate, pilot, and deploy innovative technology and translate research into scalable solutions. Develop and manage relationships with a network of vendors and engineering consultants across the project life cycle. Perform site visits during construction for project assessment. Additional duties as assigned and/or directed. What you’ll bring: Bachelor’s Degree in Engineering. 5 years of solar or BESS design and/or project engineering experience. Experience leading engineering for complex PV or BESS projects across the full project life cyc le , including managing third-party engineering resources , reviewing design details, reviewing specs for critical equipment , and driving project-level decisions . Strong knowledge of PV and BESS engineering, design, and construction principles including power engineering fundamentals, major system components, constructability considerations, utility interconnection and acceptance processes, and performance optimization principles. Strong working knowledge of industry-standard PV and BESS design codes, engineering principles, and construction methods, including but not limited to NEC, IBC, and IFC. Demonstrated a bility to independently prioritize and manage multiple projects and tasks, identify critical path schedule items, and proactively anticipate and resolve construction challenges. Specific experience in roles where this is a core responsibility. Strong understanding of the DG and community solar market, including utility, state, and regional nuances, and how project execution differs from C&I and utility-scale PV. Proficiency reading and interpreting outputs from CAD and energy modeling tools, including AutoCAD and PVSYST or equivalent platforms, and using those outputs to support technical decision-making. Experience working with Microsoft Office and common collaboration tools used to manage engineering deliverables and cross-functional coordination. Demonstrated success leading engineering for utility-scale solar and BESS projects from early development through commissioning and operational handoff is a plus. Experience developing and managing contracts with engineering consulting partners and equipment suppliers is a plus. Experience creating and/or leading testing programs for implementation of new technology , product features, or proc ess launches is a plus. Having participated in formal workplace mentorship programs as a mentor or mentee is a plus. EIT Certification (PE License preferred), NABCEP Cert ification, and/or PMP certification. Commitment to Nexamp's mission and have a passion for solving tomorrow's climate crisis today. Demonstrated experience in effectively communicating information, ideas, and perspectives with people inside and beyond your organization. Experience in showcasing initiative to make improvements to current work, processes, products, and services across the organization. We value accountability and an ownership mentality. Ability to ask appropriate questions, analyze data, identify the root causes of problems, and present creative solutions. Expertise in building strong internal and external relationships with customers and stakeholders, instilling trust and loyalty across the industry. Eagerness to develop a fundamental understanding of how Nexamp operates and then apply that knowledge effectively to inform business decisions. If you don’t meet 100% of the above qualifications, but see yourself contributing, please apply. At Nexamp, our mission is to build the future of energy so it is clean, simple, and accessible for all. We are committed to providing a work environment free from discrimination. We are proud to be an equal opportunity employer. We do not discriminate against applicants on the basis of race, ethnicity, religion, sex, gender, sexual orientation, gender identity, disability status, veteran status, or any other basis protected by law. By encouraging a culture where ideas and decisions come from all people, we believe it will help us grow, innovate, and be a part of environmental and social change. You’ll love working here because: Not only will you get to take part in meaningful work and have the chance to change the world alongside innovative, dedicated, and motivated peers, but you will also have access to all the benefits that Nexamp offers! This include s our competitive compensation package; a 401(k) employer-match; health, dental, and vision insurance starting day one; flexible paid time off and holiday PTO ; c ommuter b enefits, and c ell p hone r eimbursement. We have headquarters in Boston, MA and Chicago, IL, in addition to growing offices nationwide. We provide healthy snacks, coffee, service days and other volunteer opportunities, company outings, and more! Compensation The reasonably estimated salary for this role at Nexamp ranges from $100,000 - $140,000. In addition to base salary, the competitive compensation package may include, depending on the role, participation in an incentive program linked to performance (for example, annual bonus programs based on individual and company performance, non-annual sales incentive plans, or other non-annual incentive plans). Additionally, you may be eligible to participate in the Company’s stock option plan. Actual base salary may vary based upon, but is not limited to, skills and qualifications, internal equity, performance, and geographic location. Any unsolicited resumes received will be deemed the property of Nexamp. We want to emphasize that Nexamp is not liable for any fees associated with unsolicited resumes.

title: Solar Project Manager - Champaign, Illinois
description: APPLICANTS ONLY - NO RECRUITERS PLEASE Harvest Solar, an equal opportunity employer, is a Michigan-based company that provides cost-effective renewable energy for agriculture, commercial, and utility customers yielding more energy independence by utilizing solar energy. We believe in energy independence and a sustainable future for our children and grandchildren. Our purpose is to empower people to create and use renewable energy by providing them with the best‐in‐class service, products, and experience. Salary The salary range for this role is $90,000.00 to 100,000.00 USD, salary commensurate with experience. An Annual Bonus Target representing 5% of your annual base salary/annual wages is paid based on meeting both organizational and individual targets. Purpose of Position Under the direction of the Director of Project Management and in full compliance with the employee handbook and all applicable laws, rules, and regulations, the Solar Project Manager (SPM) will perform all duties outlined in this position description. The ideal candidate will oversee multiple commercial photovoltaic (PV) projects, including supervision of the Installation work force to meet all schedule requirements, oversee and maintain a safe and clean work environment throughout the installation process and oversee and provide leadership for the Installation personnel. Support problem solving and continuous improvement activities and provide financial feedback and any other support required by the Vice President of Operations. Major Responsibilities of Position Lead by example in all areas of safety, quality, productivity, cost reduction and customer satisfaction. Enforce company rules and regulations, taking disciplinary action when necessary and coordinating with Human Resources. Instruct and assist employees to install in a safe and productive manner while adhering to quality requirements. Maintain a clean, safe work area and job site. Coordinate all sub-contractors, LV electrical, MV electrical, Surveyor, concrete, temporary labor, civil inspectors and Miss Dig. Assist in scheduling the work force and installation projects. Ensure that employees are properly trained to safely install quality solar arrays. Ensure all necessary materials are on hand to install in a productive manner. Document all accidents and file required reports. Assist in hiring/staffing employees as required to meet the needs of the installation schedule. Evaluate the new job packets for cost savings and process improvements. Ensure that customer and internal quality standards are achieved on new jobs and maintain properly documented evidence. Promote and maintain good customer and supplier relationships. Work with Purchasing to order material/supplies in a timely manner and maintain appropriate inventory levels. Initiate continuous improvement methodology with installation team members. Key contact person for any issues with customers or suppliers while on a jobsite. Schedule and perform routine maintenance requirements on company owned equipment. Duties, responsibilities and activities may change at any time with or without notice. Other duties as assigned. THE ABOVE STATEMENTS ARE INTENDED TO DESCRIBE THE GENERAL NATURE AND LEVEL OF WORK PERFORMED BY INDIVIDUALS ASSIGNED TO THIS POSITION. THEY ARE NOT INTENDED TO BE AN EXHAUSTIVE LIST OF ALL RESPONSIBILITIES, DUTIES AND REQUIREMENTS. Personal Competencies (Knowledge, Skills, Abilities, and Other Attributes) Ability to work in a team environment. Proven record of continuous improvement in Quality, Productivity, Safety and Housekeeping. Basic understanding of and the ability to operate all job-related equipment, company owned and rented. Excellent leadership, analytic, organizational and interpersonal skills. Ability to train, motivate and evaluate departmental personnel. Ability to handle and organize multi-task assignments with accuracy and in a timely manner Must have full range or mobility in upper and lower body; ability to work in various positions & environments, including, but not limited to, stooping, standing, bending, sitting, kneeling and squatting for extended periods of time. Professional appearance and excellent customer service. Educational and Certification Background Valid State Driver's License, required. Bachelor’s degree in construction management or directly related discipline required. Two years of directly related experience may substitute for one year of university degree. 3-5 years of Project Management experience, required. Experience dealing with utility scale projects of 5 Mega Watts or higher or behind the meter Commercial/Industrial projects, preferred. AC and DC electrical installation experience, preferred. MIOSHA 30 Certification, required. Training assistance is available. Work Environment Office Environment 50% of the time: Busy office with frequent interruptions and multi-tasking required; standard office equipment is available including Microsoft Office Day travel Required 50% of the time to support job sites and customers. Over Night Travel Required 25% of the time to support job sites and customers. Benefit Offerings Harvest Solar employees are eligible for the following benefits programs: Immediately After Hire Nine Paid Holidays per Year. Including: New Year’s Day, Memorial Day, Independence Day, Labor Day, Thanksgiving Day, Day after Thanksgiving, and Christmas Eve, Christmas Day, New Years Eve. Paid Vacation: Vacation time is accrued each week at a rate of 1.5384 to achieve 80 hours in the calendar year. Unused vacation can be paid out and/or up to 40 unused hours can be rolled over at year end. The First of the Month after the Date of Hire: Health Insurance. The premiums are a shared expense with 80% covered by Harvest Solar and 20% covered by the associate via a weekly payroll deduction. Premiums are based on level of coverage, (i.e., Associate only, Associate & Spouse, Associate & Child(ren), Family). Option 1: Priority Health, POS HSA 2000 Plan Members can seek care from in-network providers (Cigna provider network). Preventive care covered 100% when received in-network. HSA compatible health plan. An HSA is a tax-deductible savings account used in conjunction with the health plan. Contribution limits are determined by the IRS. Harvest Solar will make the following weekly deposit into your HSA account based on the coverage options: Associate: $10.64; Associate & Spouse: $27.25; Associate & Child(ren): $21.65; Family: $37.55 Option 2: Priority Health, Traditional POS 1000 Plan Members can seek care from in-network providers (Cigna provider network). Preventive care covered 100% when received in-network. Not an HSA compatible health plan. Dental Insurance The premiums are a shared expense with 80% covered by Harvest Solar and 20% covered by the associate via a weekly payroll deduction. Premiums are based on level of coverage, (i.e., Associate only, Associate & Spouse, Associate & Child(ren), Family). Vision Insurance: The premiums are a shared expense with 80% covered by Harvest Solar and 20% covered by the associate via a weekly payroll deduction. Premiums are based on level of coverage, (i.e., Associate only, Associate & Spouse, Associate & Child(ren), Family). Group Life Insurance: $50,000.00 of group life insurance, with and Accident Death clause. Premiums are covered by Harvest Solar Group Short Term Disability: 60% of your earnings, with a $1,000.00 weekly maximum, are available for injury or illness after a seven-day waiting period. Premiums are covered by Harvest Solar. Voluntary Supplemental Programs: Accident, Critical illness, and Hospital Indemnity are available at the associate’s expense. Plans are organized through Allstate and premiums are paid through payroll deduction. At 90 Days of Employment: Paid Time Off (PTO): 40 Hours are available each year on January 1. PTO Is available to assist you in managing your time off work for personal appointments. PTO does not rollover, nor is it paid out at the end of the year, unused PTO is forfeited. In the first year of employment available hours are prorated based on your date of hire. The First of the Month After 90-Days of Employment: Harvest Solar 401k Plan: Associates are auto enrolled at a 3% deferral rate. The plan is administered by Vestwell. Auto enrolled contribution is invested in a “Retire-On-Time” plan. Once enrolled, the associate may make changes that include: Increasing the Deferral Rate to the Applicable IRS Limits: A company match is available. When the associate defers 3%, Harvest Solar matches 3%. When the associate defers 4%, the Harvest Solar the first 3.5%. When the associate defers 5%, Harvest Solar matches the first 4%. Changing the Account Type: Both a pre-tax and Roth account is available. Changing the Investment Type: The plan offers standard plans to address risk or age of retirement, or the associate can customize their own investment.

title: Chief Electrician
description: Since our founding in 2016, we have been committed to helping build a more sustainable future by delivering innovative energy solutions that improve building performance, reduce energy costs, and support environmental responsibility. Our mission goes beyond business—we're dedicated to making a lasting, positive impact on the communities we serve and the future of energy. Our team provides a full range of services, including solar energy system design and installation, energy testing and verification, green building certifications, quality assurance, and regulatory compliance. We partner with builders, developers, municipalities, and businesses to ensure projects meet the highest standards of energy efficiency and sustainability. Through expert guidance, advanced technology, and a commitment to excellence, we help our clients achieve long-term performance, greater savings, and meaningful environmental impact. At 15 Lightyears, we're looking for passionate individuals who want to make a difference and help shape the future of clean energy. About the role 15 Lightyears is seeking an experienced Chief Electrician (EC Qualifier) to lead our growing commercial electrical division. This is a hands-on leadership role for a licensed electrical professional who enjoys mentoring others, providing technical guidance, and ensuring projects are completed safely, efficiently, and to the highest quality standards. As the Chief Electrician, you will serve as the company's Electrical Contractor (EC) Qualifier while providing technical leadership and oversight for our electrical field operations. Working closely with electricians, project managers, and company leadership, you will oversee daily operations, mentor field personnel, promote quality and safety, and support the successful execution of commercial electrical and solar projects. This position maintains a regular presence on active job sites throughout Central Florida, providing guidance, resolving technical challenges, performing quality inspections, and ensuring projects are completed to company standards. While the electrical team performs the majority of installation work, the Chief Electrician is expected to provide hands-on support when needed to ensure project success. What you'll do Serve as the company's Electrical Contractor (EC) Qualifier, ensuring compliance with all applicable licensing requirements, electrical codes, and industry standards. Lead, mentor, and develop a team of electricians and apprentices by providing technical guidance, coaching, and support. Maintain a consistent presence on active job sites to oversee field operations, monitor workmanship, and ensure projects are completed safely, efficiently, and to company quality standards. Provide technical direction and resolve complex electrical and construction-related issues that arise during project execution. Oversee commercial electrical and solar installations to ensure compliance with the National Electrical Code (NEC), local jurisdictions, and company standards. Review and interpret blueprints, electrical drawings, specifications, and project documents to guide field operations. Coordinate electrical layouts, project sequencing, material requirements, and installation activities with project managers and field personnel. Perform quality control inspections and verify completed work meets project specifications and company expectations. Collaborate with project managers, general contractors, inspectors, customers, and other trades to ensure successful project delivery. Promote and enforce OSHA regulations and company safety policies while fostering a culture of safety and accountability. Assist with estimating, project planning, scheduling, and material coordination as needed. Support recruiting, onboarding, training, and performance development of electrical personnel. Maintain accurate project documentation and communicate project status, risks, and recommendations to company leadership. Provide hands-on field support when necessary to assist the team and ensure successful project completion. Qualifications Active Florida EC License preferred. OR active Journeyman Electrician license with qualifications to obtain a Florida EC license. Minimum 5 years of supervisory or foreman experience on commercial electrical job sites. Extensive commercial electrical construction experience required. Strong knowledge of NEC codes, commercial electrical systems, and safe installation practices. Experience with switchgear, transformers, distribution panels, conduit installation, and commercial electrical infrastructure. Solar electrical experience is a plus. Ability to read and interpret blueprints, schematics, and construction documents. Strong leadership, communication, and problem-solving skills. Proficient with hand tools, power tools, and electrical testing equipment. Ability to work at heights, climb ladders, and lift up to 50 lbs. Basic computer skills preferred. Must pass a background check and pre-employment drug screening. Valid Florida Driver’s License with safe driving record required. PI59aca7e170be-26172-41153012

title: Solar Installation Instructor / Technical Trainer
description: About AOE International AOE International is a nonprofit organization focused on community support, workforce development and education. We partner with public agencies, employers and community organizations to expand access to career training, industry credentials and employment opportunities. Our workforce-development programs prepare participants for sustainable careers in construction, clean energy and related skilled trades. Position Summary AOE International is seeking an experienced Solar Installation Instructor / Technical Trainer to provide hands-on solar installation and construction-trades training to adult learners at the Vienna Correctional Center in Vienna, Illinois. The instructor will prepare students for entry-level employment in the solar and clean-energy industries by teaching the fundamentals of photovoltaic systems, jobsite safety, construction skills, tools, equipment and workplace expectations. The position combines classroom instruction, instructor-led demonstrations and supervised hands-on training. The ideal candidate is an experienced solar installer, lead installer, foreman, electrician, site supervisor or technical trainer who enjoys developing new workers and sharing practical industry knowledge. Formal classroom teaching experience is welcomed but is not required for candidates who have experience training apprentices, new installers or field crews. This position offers an opportunity for an experienced solar professional to transition from full-time field production, roof work or project travel into a stable training role while helping prepare the next generation of clean-energy workers. Key Responsibilities Solar Installation and Technical Instruction Deliver classroom and hands-on instruction covering the fundamentals of residential and commercial solar photovoltaic installation. Teach students how solar energy systems operate, including the basic functions of modules, racking systems, inverters, wiring, disconnects, batteries and balance-of-system components. Introduce students to the major career paths within the solar and clean-energy industries. Demonstrate proper methods for measuring, laying out, assembling and installing solar mounting and racking systems. Provide instruction in basic electrical concepts, including voltage, current, resistance, series and parallel circuits, grounding and electrical safety. Teach students how to identify and safely handle common solar installation tools, materials and equipment. Introduce students to system plans, electrical diagrams, equipment specifications, installation manuals and construction drawings. Explain basic site-assessment considerations, including roof condition, orientation, shading, structural limitations and equipment placement. Teach proper wire management, equipment labeling, system inspection and quality-control practices. Provide introductory instruction in system testing, commissioning, maintenance and troubleshooting. Connect technical instruction to current solar-industry practices, employer expectations and entry-level job opportunities. Construction and Credential-Based Training Deliver applicable NCCER Core curriculum, including basic safety, construction math, hand and power tools, construction drawings, communication, employability skills and material handling. Prepare students to complete required written assessments and hands-on performance profiles. Deliver or support OSHA-10 Construction or General Industry training in accordance with program and authorized-trainer requirements. Deliver or coordinate First Aid/CPR instruction and skills assessments leading to a recognized certification. Align lesson plans, hands-on activities and assessments with applicable credentialing standards and clean-energy workforce-program requirements. Prepare printed instructional packets and independent assignments to support continuity of learning during facility lockdowns or scheduling interruptions. Hands-On Laboratory Instruction Plan and supervise realistic solar installation exercises in a controlled training environment. Demonstrate proper use of personal protective equipment, fall-protection equipment, ladders, hand tools, power tools and electrical testing equipment. Guide students through simulated installations involving racking, modules, wiring, conduit, inverters and related components. Evaluate students through observation, skills demonstrations, written assignments and practical performance assessments. Maintain an appropriate instructor-to-student ratio during hands-on training. Ensure students understand both how to perform installation tasks and why each procedure is required. Safety, Security and Tool Control Maintain strict control and accountability for all tools, equipment, materials and instructional supplies. Complete daily tool and equipment inventories before and after instructional activities. Maintain secure storage areas, tool logs and equipment-issuance records in accordance with facility requirements. Enforce all AOE International, Illinois Department of Corrections and program safety procedures. Maintain an orderly, OSHA-conscious training environment. Model safe work practices and immediately correct unsafe student behavior. Ensure proper use of personal protective equipment and appropriate housekeeping practices. Report safety incidents, damaged tools, missing equipment and security concerns according to established procedures. Respond to emergencies and facility incidents in accordance with Vienna Correctional Center protocols. Learner Development and Support Provide supportive, respectful and structured instruction to justice-impacted adult learners. Use adult-learning, trauma-informed and strengths-based instructional practices. Break down technical concepts into clear, understandable and practical steps. Provide additional support with construction math, measurements, reading, terminology and technical documents when needed. Offer individualized coaching, tutoring, make-up instruction and reassessment opportunities. Monitor student attendance, participation, technical progress and credential attainment. Provide timely and constructive feedback regarding student performance. Develop individualized support plans for students who require additional assistance. Maintain professional boundaries and consistently apply classroom expectations. Employability and Career Preparation Integrate communication, teamwork, reliability, problem-solving, time management and workplace professionalism into daily instruction. Teach students about solar-industry jobsite expectations, workplace culture and advancement opportunities. Help students understand common solar-industry positions, including installer, lead installer, electrician, operations and maintenance technician, site assessor and project supervisor. Support resume development, interview preparation and job-readiness activities in partnership with program staff. Conduct mock interviews and provide practical feedback based on solar and construction employer expectations. Help students translate their training, credentials and hands-on experience into marketable employment qualifications. Contribute to transition planning and connections with employers, apprenticeship programs, workforce agencies and community partners. Program Coordination and Documentation Coordinate daily with facility personnel regarding schedules, participant movement, classroom access, room utilization and security procedures. Maintain a consistent instructor presence during scheduled instructional hours. Complete attendance records, lesson plans, assessment documentation, performance profiles and credentialing records accurately and on time. Maintain student-progress records and contribute information required for grant, contract and program-performance reporting. Communicate student progress, instructional needs, behavioral concerns and safety issues to appropriate program leadership. Participate in staff meetings, professional-development activities and technical-assistance sessions. Assist with curriculum improvement, equipment planning and instructional-material development. Maintain familiarity with developments in solar technology, installation methods, workforce standards and employer expectations. Requirements At least three years of professional experience in solar installation, electrical work, construction, renewable energy or a closely related skilled trade. Demonstrated knowledge of photovoltaic installation practices, jobsite safety, tools, equipment and construction methods. Experience as a solar installer, lead installer, foreman, site supervisor, electrician, technical trainer or comparable field professional. Experience training, coaching, supervising or mentoring apprentices, new employees, students or field crews. Ability to explain technical information clearly to individuals with different educational and experience levels. Ability to safely demonstrate solar installation and construction tasks in a hands-on training environment. Strong organizational, communication and classroom-management skills. Ability to maintain accurate records and comply with strict tool-control, safety and security requirements. Ability to work effectively with adult learners from diverse personal, educational and employment backgrounds. High school diploma or equivalent. Valid driver’s license and reliable transportation to the Vienna Correctional Center. Ability to successfully complete all required facility access, background-check, orientation and security-clearance procedures. Certification Requirements Candidates should possess, or be willing and eligible to obtain, applicable instructor and safety credentials. Depending on program requirements, these may include: NCCER Certified Craft Instructor certification NCCER Core certification OSHA Authorized Construction or General Industry Trainer status OSHA-10 or OSHA-30 certification First Aid/CPR Instructor certification through the American Heart Association, American Red Cross or an equivalent provider NABCEP PV Associate, PV Installation Professional or another recognized solar-industry credential AOE International may consider candidates who do not currently hold every instructor credential when they possess substantial solar field experience and can obtain required credentials within an established period following hire. Salary Description 75,000 - 80,000

title: Residential Service Crew Lead
description: About Namaste Solar Namaste Solar is an employee-owned cooperative, Certified B Corp, and Public Benefit Corporation on a mission to transform energy and transform business. After one month of employment, we offer a path for you to become a co-owner of Namaste Solar. As a co-owner, you can vote on critical company issues, run for Namaste Solar's Board of Directors, and participate in our annual profit-sharing program. We have fostered a thriving, inclusive organizational culture that offers flexible work schedules and prioritizes personal well-being and growth. We strive to incorporate diverse perspectives and ideas to challenge and improve how we do business in a rapidly changing and expanding industry. You will be part of a community committed to sustainability, equity, and positive impact. Overview This position is responsible for executing work duties that include, but are not limited to, PV system service inspections, de-installation and re-installation of PV systems, installation of retrofit storage projects, and responding to service calls to troubleshoot and repair residential PV and storage systems. This person needs to be self-driven and have strong troubleshooting skills to carry a project through to completion. The Residential Service Lead may also be asked to support other Residential Circle departments when needed, depending on team capacity and resource needs, including EPC, BNC, and DE/RE. Key Responsibilities • Troubleshoot and repair solar PV systems in an efficient and safe manner. • Lead quality PV and storage installations based on system design specifications, including de-installation and re-installation of existing solar PV systems. • Ensure layout, roof attachment, racking and module assembly, combiner box installation, homerun wiring, animal guard installation, and voltage testing meet expected quality standards. • Install Data Acquisition Systems, or DAS, for residential projects. • Lead equipment warranty and vendor RMA processes for customers. • Complete work orders through Site Capture and Salesforce/Field Service Lightning applications in a timely manner. • Provide feedback to operations teams to support best practice improvements. • Represent the company to customers in a way that builds trust, accountability, and customer satisfaction. • Educate customers on how solar PV and storage systems perform and operate. • Respond to customer emails and phone calls related to questions, service requests, and project coordination. • Work safely in a variety of conditions, including heights, ladders, live electricity, battery storage, and pitched roof surfaces. • Follow through on work delegated by the Project Manager, Installation Manager, and Department Director. • Operate in a lead role on assigned work orders to complete the full scope of work. • Maintain strong organizational skills, with the ability to multitask, set priorities, and meet deadlines. • Use Field Service Lightning to track and enter case and work order details, maintaining high-quality records with all information needed to close cases and work orders and report on work performed. • Effectively create, track, and process RMA work orders, including tracking necessary details to ensure customer satisfaction and OEM payment for work performed. Teamwork • Contribute and collaborate at departmental and company meetings. • Support other team members in the resolution and completion of work orders. • Provide transparency and ample notice for lengthy time-off requests to ensure the department can adequately cover required work during absences. • Provide feedback to installation, design, and sales teams about best practices and issues discovered in the field. Preferred • NABCEP certification. • Networking knowledge, such as TCP/IP, device addressing, and MODBUS protocols. • Understanding of data monitoring systems and related wiring and computer systems. • NFPA 70E certification. This includes tasks with repetitive motions and overhead work with hand tools, power tools, and materials. The employee is also required to reach with hands and arms, talk, and hear. The work environment may include extreme temperatures, both hot and cold, and the employee may be exposed to sunlight for multiple hours each day. title: Field Service Technician II – Solar
description: WORK ARRANGEMENT: ON-SITE, FIELD-BASED. THIS IS NOT A REMOTE OR WORK-FROM-HOME JOB. This role is performed in person, outdoors, on solar sites in and around St. Cloud, MN. You must already live within commuting distance of St. Cloud, or be prepared to relocate there at your own expense before your start date. You may see this listed as "field-based." That means you drive from your home to job sites rather than reporting to an office each morning. It does not mean you can work from another city or state. Applications from candidates who are not located in — or actively relocating to — the St. Cloud area cannot be considered for this posting. Territory: [30–90 minutes typical, rarely over 3 hours]. Overnight travel: [under 10%]. Schedule: [M–F, 7am–3pm or 8am–4pm]. On-call: [rotational Saturday 8am–12pm]. Overtime: [paid biweekly; 40–45 hours typical; 1.5x over 40]. SOLAR EXPERIENCE HELPS. IT IS NOT REQUIRED. STRONG ELECTRICAL AND DIAGNOSTIC SKILLS ARE. Energy Support Services keeps solar and energy storage systems safe, reliable, and producing clean power. As a Field Service Technician II – Solar, you’ll work independently on advanced inspections, preventative maintenance, and system troubleshooting — operating safely in high-voltage environments without direct supervision, guiding junior technicians on site, and progressing along a defined pathway toward Technician III. If you have two or more years of serious hands-on technical work in any industry and you’re the person people bring the problem nobody else could figure out, we want your application. COMING FROM ANOTHER TRADE? THIS IS THE PART TO READ. We hire experienced technicians out of other industries at this level regularly, and we build the solar knowledge on top. Here’s how your background translates: Automotive, diesel, or heavy equipment — Root-cause diagnosis, circuit tracing, reading schematics, using a scan tool and DMM, working to torque spec, and writing up findings. You’ll trade flat-rate for a salary, and your tool box for ours. HVAC/R, especially commercial or light-industrial — Control circuits, contactors, VFDs, three-phase power, service calls run solo, and preventative maintenance on a schedule. Very close cousin to this work. Telecommunications, broadband, or utility line work — Working at height, terminations, test equipment, prints, and outdoor work in every kind of weather. Your safety habits are already right. Industrial maintenance, wind, or power generation — Lockout/tagout discipline, medium-voltage awareness, PM programs, and CMMS documentation all carry directly across. Military technical specialties — Power generation, electrical systems, avionics, and electronics maintenance transfer cleanly. The tools you’ll learn (and their equivalents you may already know) I/V curve tracer — measures the performance curve of a string of solar modules to find underperformance. Conceptually similar to putting a vehicle or motor on a load test. Megohmmeter ("Megger") / insulation resistance tester — finds insulation breakdown and ground faults. If you’ve used one in industrial or motor work, it’s the same instrument. Infrared thermography — thermal imaging to find hot spots in connections and modules. If you’ve used a thermal camera on bearings, panels, or refrigerant lines, you’re already there. Drone-based aerial thermal inspection — we pay for your FAA Part 107 and teach you the flight work. PAY $75,000 – $95,000 annually, depending on experience and qualifications. WHAT WE OFFER Tools and equipment: provided. Company truck, company fuel/credit card, and vehicle maintenance card. You will never spend your own money on tools here — no tool truck payment, no tool debt. Bonus: Up to an 8% performance bonus, paid annually. Apparel: Company-provided PPE and flame-resistant clothing kit (bibs, jackets, pants, shirts) at no cost to you. Health: Medical, dental, and vision. We pay 80% of your health insurance premiums. Retirement: 401(k) with up to a 7.5% company match. Time off: PTO accrued each pay period — 120 hours/year (years 0–2), 160 hours (years 3–9), 200 hours (10 years) — plus 11 paid holidays. Family: 8 weeks of paid parental leave. Insurance: Company-paid Life and AD&D insurance at 1x your annual salary. Certifications — we pay, you keep them: OSHA 10/30, NFPA 70E/70B, FAA Part 107 (drone), and our internal O&M Tech course series. These certifications stay with you for the rest of your career. Advancement: A published Field Tech Development Pathway with defined progression to Technician III. You move up on demonstrated capability, not on how long you’ve been here. Education: Tuition reimbursement up to $10,000 per year for approved programs. WHAT YOU'LL DO Safety Lead by example in promoting a safe working culture in the field. Perform approved hazardous electrical energy control procedures and select the exact PPE required for each task. Participate in and actively critique Pre-Job Briefs and Job Safety Analysis (JSA). Apply personal lockout/tagout as a worker, or serve as work leader once approved. Inspections and preventative maintenance Perform comprehensive electrical and mechanical inspections of solar energy systems. Conduct advanced preventative maintenance including infrared thermography, insulation resistance testing, and I/V curve tracing — all of which we train you on. Help build and implement preventative maintenance schedules for your assigned sites. Troubleshooting Independently diagnose and troubleshoot system and operational issues. Operate and troubleshoot safely in 600VAC and 1500VDC environments without direct supervision. Note: 1500VDC is a higher DC voltage than most trades encounter — this is exactly why our safety training is extensive, paid, and mandatory before you work unsupervised. Use specialized diagnostic tools and root-cause analysis to handle equipment repairs and replacements. Documentation Create and maintain detailed, accurate records of inspections, maintenance, and repairs with minimal oversight. Prepare clear technical reports and actionable equipment recommendations for the Team Lead. Knowledge sharing Stay current on industry best practices, safety updates, and emerging technology. Share your expertise and give supportive guidance to junior technicians on site. Help improve the quality, clarity, and safety content of our training materials. Support your teammates and take on other duties as assigned. WHAT YOU NEED High school diploma or equivalent. 2 years of hands-on technical, electrical, or mechanical work in any industry — solar, electrical, automotive, diesel, HVAC/R, telecommunications, wind, power generation, industrial maintenance, utilities, or a military technical specialty. Solid working understanding of electrical fundamentals — AC and DC theory, series and parallel circuits, grounding, and safe work practices around energized equipment. Confident with a multimeter and able to read, interpret, and work from electrical schematics or engineering drawings. Strong analytical, time management, and problem-solving skills, and a track record of working independently without someone checking on you. Strong communication skills and the patience to bring a junior technician along. Valid driver’s license and clean driving record. Helpful, but we’ll train and certify you Solar-specific or grid-tied PV system experience. FAA Part 107 drone certification — we pay for it. OSHA 30 and NFPA 70E — we pay for these as well. Hands-on time with I/V curve tracers, megohmmeters, or insulation testers — or comparable diagnostic instruments from another trade. Familiarity with Data Acquisition Systems (DAS) or SCADA — the monitoring systems that report site performance remotely. PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS Drive a vehicle confidently and with a high degree of safety. Stand for long periods and walk distances up to three miles per day. Navigate ladders, stairs, scaffolding, and ramps while maintaining three points of contact. Have visual acuity for depth perception, no field-of-vision issues, and the ability to distinguish between colors. Work comfortably in a range of climate conditions, including extreme heat (above 100°F) or extreme cold (below 32°F), for periods of more than one hour. Exert up to 50 pounds of force occasionally, up to 30 pounds frequently, and up to 10 pounds constantly to move objects. description: About Us Solar Landscape is the leading commercial rooftop solar developer in the U.S. Only 4% of commercial rooftops host solar today — we’re changing that, fast. At the same time, we’re collaborative by default, and believe the best work happens when people enjoy working together. This role includes managing project planning, budgeting, procurement, construction, scheduling, reporting, and risk mitigation. Responsibilities Plan, budget, manage, and complete PV projects of moderate complexity, or multiple projects of lesser complexity simultaneously. Coordinate design and permitting activities with engineering team and local authorities. Work with Safety Manager to develop Site Specific Health and Safety Plans and implement safety procedures. Drive completion of all job closeout procedures including AHJ inspections, interconnection, testing, documentation, Owner’s Engineer reviews, Independent Engineer reviews. Manage, train, and supervise project team; act as mentor to younger employees to encourage professional growth and career development. Support sales activities with estimates, contract review, and client communication. Build trust and rapport with all Solar Landscape departments. Qualifications Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Project Management or Construction Management preferred. 5 years of experience in field construction management. 2 years of experience in C&I solar project management. Strong leadership abilities. Proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite, Dynamics 365 (or other construction management software), and Microsoft Project. Deep understanding of rooftop, ground-mount, and carport commercial PV construction methods. Knowledge of behind-the-meter and utility interconnections. Familiarity with Purchase Orders, Subcontracts, PPA, EPC Contracts, and project accounting. Excellent organizational and communication skills. Detail-oriented and self-motivated. Knowledge of construction safety requirements; OSHA 10 or 30 certification preferred. Valid driver’s license with willingness to travel to various job sites. Ability to climb ladders and access building roofs. title: Solar Technician
description: Job Description We are seeking a Solar Technician to join our Site Team at our utility-scale solar site in Bellevue, OH (Wheatsborough Solar) . This position is responsible for performing testing, troubleshooting, and the repair of solar inverters at the site to meet maintenance schedules and performance standards such as Mean Time To Repair (MTTR). Focus will be placed on ensuring a safe, efficient, and environmentally sound plant operation through inspection of watch, electrical, mechanical, and electronic troubleshooting. Inspection will be performed daily for mechanical component breakage or misalignment and electrical component failures preventing a collector or group of collectors from tracking. Reporting to the Facility Manager on site, you will receive instructions on forward-looking assignments typically on a weekly cadence. Duties and tasks are standardized, but what is performed will vary day to day. Primary Responsibilities Ensure proper operation, inspection, and maintenance of solar field equipment and associated solar components, including inverters, tracker systems, transformers and substations, SCADA systems, road maintenance, vegetation assessments, general building maintenance, etc., and perform QA/QC inspections in accordance with applicable SOPs. Proactively look for improvement opportunities to improve appropriate processes and procedures Read schematics to troubleshoot complicated mechanical and electrical problems with inverters, tracker control systems, PV panels, and components. Effectively gather information regarding solar performance issues associated with solar field equipment, met towers, metering, etc. May diagnose, recommend, and implement solutions up to intermediate routine issues. Seeks assistance when encountering issues outside trained skill level to ensure success in resolution. Comply with all pertinent environmental health and safety programs. Act as a safety role model by encouraging and recognizing others completing safe acts and intervening when unsafe acts are being practiced. Identify gaps in safety standards and safety risks in the work environment and provide recommendations to higher-level technical staff and management. Perform a variety of administrative duties satisfying both internal and external reporting requirements. Administrative responsibilities include but are not limited to: plan of the day (POD) reports, reviewing work orders, SAP processing, fault reports, offline inverter reports, and engineering cases. Demonstrate and promote integrity, strong initiative, and a no-compromise focus on safety and quality of work on a continuous basis. Review completed service checklists for accuracy and maintain a punch list for future work activities Engage appropriate internal and external resources to correct performance issues. Ensure that reliable electronic communication is maintained between the solar field, substations, site office, and home office. Responsible for facilitating training requirements as related to areas of safety and compliance training. Work closely with equipment suppliers and service entities as needed Works on assignments that are semi-routine in nature where the ability to recognize nonconformities and develop solutions is required. Demonstrates superior workmanship and quality in all work areas. May act as the technical interface with the customer and with other Apex departments. Professional appearance and courteous behavior are required at all times. Models a professional and positive work ethic. Ability to effectively work both independently and in a team environment.

title: Commercial Solar Technician
description: Role: Solar Technician, Operations & Maintenance (O&M) Location: Illinois and Wisconsin. Field-based, home-deployed. Ideal home base is the Chicago-to-Rockford-to-Milwaukee corridor. Company vehicle provided. Reports to: Kyle, Director of Operations & Maintenance, who reports to the Chief Operating Officer. Team size: Small and rebuilding. Two technicians and an operations coordinator today, growing to five-plus technicians over the next 12 months. Why it exists now: The O&M line is behind on a growing site backlog and is being rebuilt to stand on its own. Kyle needs working technicians who can restore downed sites and grow with the operation. Video Job Description - See the Leader Before You Apply: https://youtu.be/YQBHS7Nv41U Why This Role Matters "If I got two quality techs, that would just dig us out fast and we would start really generating some real growth." Rethink Electric maintains commercial, distributed-generation, and light-utility solar across Illinois and Wisconsin. The portfolio runs from warehouses, churches, and high schools to industrial sites like the Harley-Davidson plant in Milwaukee and ground-mount utility fields. The O&M line is in a deliberate rebuild. Kyle inherited a team that looked good on paper and did not produce, and he cleared it. He is now hiring for output, not pedigree. Every day a site sits down is a day it does not make money, so the person in this seat directly protects revenue and customer trust. There is a real fork in the road that Kyle named plainly. Hire well, and the line grows into an independent business with its own external clients. Fail to hire, and the operation contracts into a SunVest-only shop. This hire helps decide which way it goes. The Mission In the first year, become the technician Kyle can send to a broken site and trust to figure it out. He is not looking for the person swinging for the grandstands. In his words, he wants "the guy who gets on base reliably," because when you put people on base you bring runs home. That means showing up to a site where something is down, diagnosing what is actually wrong, restoring production safely and efficiently, and moving to the next job without needing the answer handed to you. You will start with a guide and support on the phone. You will grow into someone who works the fault with your own troubleshooting mind. Performance Objectives Restore downed C&I, distributed-generation, and light-utility sites to production safely and efficiently, minimizing revenue lost to downtime. Measured by dispatch-to-restoration time and repeat-dispatch rate. Diagnose faults across a mixed inverter fleet spanning multiple OEM platforms, using HMI diagnostics, insulation-resistance testing, DC string isolation, and voltage and current analysis. Reach independent Level 1 troubleshooting within the first 90 days. Deploy from home as a self-directed operator, out the door between 7:00 and 7:30, running your own day with minimal oversight. Reduce unnecessary truck rolls by restoring sites remotely where the site allows, before driving out. Progress from Level 1 to Level 2 technician within 12 months, taking more sites solo and helping dig the O&M line out of its backlog as the team scales. Carry a share of the weekend on-call rotation once the team reaches roughly five technicians, restoring remotely wherever possible. Fit Traits Troubleshooting Mind. Signal: "They can start using their own troubleshooting mindset, their own curious mind to find the solution." Kyle can teach solar. He cannot teach curiosity. The hire has to want to solve the broken thing. Self-Starter. Signal: "The guys deploy out of their houses, so they gotta be self-starters," and, "If you're still waiting for the reveille bell every morning, this ain't the job for you." Nobody is watching you leave the driveway. Maturity. Signal: "The majority coming out, I think that would be our number one thing is maturity." This is the filter Kyle named first. You manage your own day, your own truck, and your own travel. Urgency About Downtime. Signal: "When the site's down, you're not making money. That's bad." Kyle wants people who feel the clock the way an aviation electrician's mate does. If it is not running, we are losing. Coachable Without Ego. Signal: "Anybody who asks for help, help will be given here." Kyle respects the tech who calls when stuck. He has no patience for the one who twiddles their thumbs for an hour, says "I did what I could," and drives home. Who You'll Work For Kyle is a Navy veteran, a nuclear electrician who served nine years before moving into wind, then solar. He came up on the tools, not from a corner office, and he now runs Rethink's O&M line as a director reporting to the COO with real autonomy. He describes a hands-off style built on trust and communication. He tries to give a consistent workday, he communicates travel a couple of weeks out, and he does not nickel-and-dime his people. He was shaped by his own time in uniform, by good leaders and bad ones, and he hires accordingly. "Anybody who asks for help, help will be given here." Why Veterans Succeed Here If you ran advanced electronics or electrical systems in the Navy as an EM, ET, AE, FC, IC, STG, or gas-turbine electrical technician, you already have the core of this job. You have stood in front of a system that was down, with pressure on and no one to hand you the answer, and you got it back. Kyle named exactly those ratings on the intake, and he named the mindset that goes with them. The aviation electrician's mate who knows that if the aircraft is not flying, people are in danger, translated here to "if the site is down, we are not making money." That sense of urgency is a deployment habit, not a training module. This operation runs the way a good shop in uniform ran. Early starts, direct communication, autonomy with accountability, and a leader who came up on the tools and expects you to own your day. The corporate layer exists above Rethink through SunVest, but it does not drive the truck. Kyle does. VHS matched this role because the performance objectives, the leadership style, and the operational tempo line up cleanly with mature transitioning sailors from the advanced-electronics community, and because Kyle is a veteran who hires veterans on purpose. LI-BN1 Requirements Hands-on electrical or electronic troubleshooting experience. | Military equivalent: EM (Electrician's Mate), ET (Electronics Technician), AE (Aviation Electrician's Mate), FC (Fire Controlman), IC (Interior Communications Electrician), STG (Sonar Technician), GS and GSE (Gas Turbine Systems electrical). | Maps to: Objectives 1 and 2. Note that heavy solar experience is not required and is not the primary filter. Comfort with standard electrical test equipment, specifically a multimeter and a clamp or amp meter. Insulation-resistance (megger) testing is learnable on the job. | Military equivalent: any advanced-electronics rating uses these tools daily on energized and de-energized systems. | Maps to: Objective 2. Self-directed work habits and personal reliability. | Military equivalent: any NCO or senior technician who ran their own maintenance actions without daily supervision. | Maps to: Objective 3. Maturity and sound judgment. | Military equivalent: Kyle would generally pass on a four-year, first-term junior unless the maturity is unmistakable. Most advanced-electronics veterans signed six-year contracts and carry that maturity out with them. | Maps to: Fit Traits. Valid driver's license and a genuine willingness to accept significant windshield time, with occasional overnight travel to Wisconsin. | Military equivalent: comfort operating independently in the field away from a home station. | Maps to: Objective 3 and Honest Notes. Willingness to learn on the job. Training is largely OJT with limited formal instruction. | Maps to: Objective 2. Not a fit: rooftop residential installation experience alone, with no troubleshooting or maintenance background. Benefits Base pay is hourly. Kyle set a floor of $35 per hour for the standard Level 1 hire, moving to $39 or $40 for a candidate he is sold on. For a veteran who already brings genuine solar or strong troubleshooting experience and is a clear standout, Kyle said he would pay $45 per hour, possibly a little north of that. Annualized at a standard 40-hour week, that range runs roughly $72,800 to $93,600 and above. Drive time is paid at the regular wage. Kyle was explicit that drive time is not free and not docked. As soon as you are in the truck, you are on the clock. Company vehicle is provided. You launch from home. On-call is a planned weekend rotation as the team grows, roughly one weekend in five at full staffing. Kyle's stated intent is a one-hour minimum payout even for a five-minute remote restore, so the interruption is compensated fairly. Schedule is Monday through Friday, targeting out the door between 7:00 and 7:30 and home by 5:00, earlier in summer when the work allows. Benefits include 401(k), medical, dental, vision, and paid time off, per the company benefits summary.

SolAmerica is committed to advancing diversity, equity, and inclusion and believes in attracting, retaining, and advancing employees who will best serve and represent its customers, partners, and communities. We promote fostering a work culture of mutual respect and teamwork, ensuring that everyone can grow and contribute at their greatest potential. For additional information about SolAmerica, visit www.solamericaenergy.com . Requirements SolAmerica is seeking a highly skilled Project Manager to oversee the complete lifecycle—from planning through execution and completion—of our solar and energy storage portfolio. As a growing Independent Power Producer (IPP), we rely on this pivotal role to ensure the successful, profitable implementation of our projects. The ideal candidate will bring a strong blend of leadership, technical expertise, and rigorous project management skills. You will be responsible for directing projects for Distributed Generation (DG) ground-mount solar. By leading a cross-functional team to meet strict budget and timeline goals, the Project Manager will maximize both the environmental and financial returns of our portfolio. PRIMARY DUTIES & RESPONSIBILITIES Manage project preconstruction including EPC bids and supervision of engineering design Responsible for the overall delivery of the project within budget, schedule, and quality requirements; while maintaining relationships with clients, stakeholders, and vendors Coordinate with internal teams, contractors, suppliers, and other stakeholders to ensure seamless project execution Manage project resources and allocate tasks to team members Conduct regular project meetings to identify and address any issues or risks Manage engineering and procurement teams to ensure the timely delivery of equipment and materials Review and take ownership of critical path project schedules for construction; along with aligning with company and financing requirements Create detailed project budgets, managing cash flow, analyzing costs vs. benefits, and ensuring the project meets financial goals set forth by Stage Gate approval process Produce project level reporting deliverables at required intervals as set forth by management. Assist in the negotiation of EPC contract amounts and contract terms Oversee the installation and commissioning of solar systems by turn-key EPC, ensuring adherence to safety, health and environmental standards Communicate project status updates, milestones, and key deliverables to internal teams, management, and financing partners Manage Utility interconnection processes after execution of Interconnection Agreement to align with project requirements Coordinate with financing parties, including Independent or third-party engineering needs and deliverables EXPERIENCE Bachelor's degree in engineering, construction management, or related STEM field. Advanced degree or professional certification in project management is preferred (may consider demonstratable experience in relevant industries); Demonstrated experience achieving positive renewable energy project construction results; Deep understanding of the solar industry; Experience with solar electrical equipment engineering and/or electrical engineering; Experience with solar racking design and engineering process (geotechnical studies, pile load testing, etc.); Experience in the field is preferred; Familiarity with utility interconnection processes and testing requirements; Proficient with MS Project or other Critical Path Scheduling Tools; PMP, PE, NABCEP, OSHA 10 (or 30) or other Certifications. KEY SKILLS & COMPETENCIES Proven experience in project management, preferably in the solar energy industry; Strong understanding of solar photovoltaic systems and installation practices; Excellent organizational and time management skills; Ability to read and comprehend plans, drawings, specifications, bid materials, contracts and related construction documents. Additional training in these skills will be provided; Ability to be self-motivated and work in a team environment where the focus is on the goals and objectives that determine the success of the projects; Excellent written and verbal communication skills with strong attention to detail; Ability to exercise judgment to appropriately balance risks with business objectives; Intellectual curiosity and a desire to constantly learn and improve; Self-starter with a strong work ethic and ability to manage multiple competing priorities; Ability to work both independently and as part of a close-knit team; Knowledge of project management software and tools; Excellent communication and interpersonal skills; Ability to manage multiple projects simultaneously; Understanding or regulatory requirements related to solar energy projects Benefits Compensation and Benefits At SolAmerica Energy, we provide a compelling salary along with a comprehensive benefits package that includes equity-based compensation and opportunities for performance bonuses. Our total rewards philosophy is structured to empower our employees to excel both professionally and personally, fostering a culture that values work/life balance as we strive toward our shared business objectives. In addition, we offer a monthly stipend for communication expenses, and all our health insurance benefits activate on Day 1. Now is an exciting time to become a part of SolAmerica Energy! We do not accept unsolicited applications from third-party agencies, as we prefer to manage our hiring internally. We are not obligated to compensate third parties for candidates introduced outside our official channels. Thank you for your understanding.

title: Solar Field Technician - Raleigh, NC
description: As a Solar Field Technician at QE Solar, you are responsible for providing ongoing field services support to multiple solar, battery storage (BESS) or other renewable energy systems on a continual/on-demand basis in order to optimize equipment performance, troubleshoot/resolve equipment issues, support emergency repairs and other provide ongoing O&M compliance support. In this role you will assist with all routine site inspections, maintenance projects, equipment & system testing, and other project compliance, troubleshoot or restoration matters. Field Service Technicians regularly participate in field support, training and project safety orientations/classes in order to develop skills and technical expertise in one or multiple disciplines including PV array, inverter, medium voltage, BESS and other solar services. Operations Leads, Solar Engineers and other management will provide regular coaching and training and will qualify technicians for field operations. Essential Duties: Diagnose and repair systems failures as existing solar sites, identify and correct potential issues that may impact site performance in the future. Assist and support field teams with real-time solutions to site operations issues and execute the same. Diagnose/troubleshoot equipment failures and perform regular preventative maintenance on a variety of solar, BESS and other project equipment. Support field teams and clients via oversight/support of warranty matters regarding equipment and systems for use or replacement. Installs, removes, troubleshoots and the maintenance of solar, BESS and other related electrical equipment. Ensure a safe, event-free work environment through strict adherence to company and client protocols, safety procedures and regulations. Ensure compliance with all safety requirements and safe best practices (e.g. lock-out/tag-out compliance, JHA completion, LDL testing, and compliance with all company safety policies or procedures and work practices). Prepare service tickets and reports for site visits, emergency repairs, equipment modifications and equipment improvement investigations. Provide reports, written and oral communication in a timely and complete fashion. Communicate with technical leads, project leads/managers, and third-party sub-contractors to ensure timely resolution to all required activities; Support recommended performance improvements and at address site safety and compliance concerns; Other responsibilities as directed by manager. Education Required: High School or Technical School Degree, Or, equivalent combination of education and experience; Veterans or military experienced candidates are strongly encouraged to apply Experience Required: 0-2 years of specialist, technical experience with solar projects, BESS, or other renewable systems; Experience with data acquisition systems. Experience Preferred: Experience working with 600v-1500v systems; Strong knowledge of NEC, IEEE and current NFPA-70e requirements; Proficient with technology and computing programs/platforms; C&I/Utility Scale solar work experience; Experience with operations of solar sites and/or project maintenance and compliance. Specialized or Technical Knowledge Licenses, Certifications Preferred: Inverter and/or BESS manufacturers’ certifications (e.g SunGrow, Power Electronics, Solectria, BYD, etc) a plus Thermography certifications (Level 1) IT/networking skills: Familiarity with RS485, Modbus, tcp/ip, etc. NABCEP PV Installer Certification Minimum OSHA 10/30 Certification Completion of NFPA 70E courses CPR/First Aid Travel Requirements: Extensive travel regionally and occasionally nationally, to meet client field operation’s needs. This role is performed primarily in field, construction, or industrial environments. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable qualified individuals with disabilities to perform these essential functions. title: Maintenance Technician I
description: Description DEFINITION Under general supervision, performs a variety of work in the construction, maintenance, and repair of District buildings, facilities, grounds, trees, and water system equipment; cleans and maintains District premises and equipment; uses and operates a variety of hand and power tools and light equipment; and performs related duties as required. SUPERVISION RECEIVED AND EXERCISED Receives general supervision from assigned supervisory or management staff. Exercises no direct supervision over staff. CLASS CHARACTERISTICS This is an entry-level in the Maintenance Technician series responsible for performing maintenance and repair of District facilities and grounds. Incumbent is expected to work independently with minimal supervision; work is routinely checked and/or supervised while in progress and fits an established structure or pattern. Exceptions or changes in procedures are explained as they arise. Examples of Duties EXAMPLES OF TYPICAL JOB FUNCTIONS (Illustrative Only) The duties and responsibilities listed below are intended to provide a representative list of the various types of work that may be performed. Specifications are not intended to reflect all duties performed within the job class, and incumbents may expect to perform other related similar duties. Some of the duties include, but are not limited to, the following. Performs a variety of maintenance, repair, and construction tasks for District infrastructure, including well buildings, booster stations, drainage stations, and related facilities. Conducts electrical work in all of District-owned facilities, including system installations, rewiring, troubleshooting, and solar panel installations. Performs welding, fabrication, and structural installations, including custom sign creation for District use. Conducts preventive maintenance, troubleshooting, and minor repair of motors, pumps, valves, and related water production and distribution systems. Performs general facilities and landscape maintenance, including clearing debris, felling trees, repairing fences, and maintaining exterior structures. Conduct minor and preventive maintenance on District vehicles, equipment, and tools, including oil changes and minor repairs. Assists in construction, installation, and servicing of mechanical and electrical systems for water distribution and production facilities. Operates air compressors, pneumatic/electric tools, and receive training in heavy equipment operation. Reads and interprets manuals, blueprints, and diagrams for repairs and installations. Cleans and paints District-owned structures, buildings, and piping; haul debris and maintain site cleanliness. Maintains inventory, stock levels, and records for maintenance supplies and equipment. Inspects District facilities and grounds for safety issues and coordinate with vendors for complex repairs. Drives vehicles to transport materials, tools, and equipment as needed. Utilizes software for recordkeeping, maintenance tracking, and reporting on work orders. Works on a computer; uses software to create and maintain a variety of records and reports; maintains operating logs and records; updates a computer-based work ticket system. Assists other divisions under the Department of Operations as needed, including leak repairs, well reads, and chlorine deliveries. Performs other related duties as assigned. Typical Qualifications QUALIFICATIONS Knowledge of: General knowledge of principles and practices of maintenance construction and repair, including principles of carpentry, plumbing, electrical work, and painting. The operation and minor maintenance of a variety of hand and power tools, vehicles, and light power equipment. Principles and practices of landscaping and tree trimming. Safe work practices and safety equipment. Techniques for providing a high level of customer service by effectively dealing with the public, vendors, contractors, and District staff. The structure and content of the English language, including the meaning and spelling of words, rules of composition, and grammar. Modern equipment and communication tools used for business functions and program, project, and task coordination, including computers, tablets, smartphones, and software programs relevant to work performed. Ability to: Safely and effectively operate and maintain a variety of hand tools, mechanical equipment, power tools, pneumatic tools, and light to heavy equipment required for the work performed. Regularly and predictably attend work. Independently organize work, set priorities, meet critical deadlines, and follow-up on assignments. Perform confined space entry with appropriate safety equipment and safe work practices. Use tact, initiative, prudence, and independent judgment within general policy and procedural guidelines. Effectively use computer systems, software applications relevant to work performed, and modern business equipment to perform a variety of work tasks. Accurately read meters, gauges, blueprints, and schematic drawings. Maintain records. Follow and apply written and oral work instructions. Research repair options and contact manufacturer to determine proper repair procedures for a variety of equipment. Communicate clearly and concisely, both orally and in writing, using appropriate English grammar and syntax. Establish, maintain, and foster positive and effective working relationships with those contacted in the course of work. Education and Experience: Any combination of training and experience that would provide the required knowledge, skills, and abilities is qualifying. A typical way to obtain the required qualifications would be: High school graduation or equivalent; and One (1) to Three (3) years of responsible general construction and maintenance work experience, preferably in a water district or related environment. Licenses and Certifications: Possession of and ability to maintain a California Class C driver’s license. Supplemental Information PHYSICAL DEMANDS Must possess mobility to work in the field; strength, stamina, and mobility to perform medium to heavy physical work; to sit, stand, and walk on level, uneven, or slippery surfaces; frequently reach, twist, turn, kneel, bend, stoop, squat, crouch, grasp and make repetitive hand movement in the performance of daily duties; possible entry into confined spaces and the use of confined entry equipment, to climb and descend ladders, to operate varied hand, pneumatic and power tools and construction equipment, and to operate a motor vehicle and visit various District sites; and vision to inspect and operate equipment. Finger dexterity is needed to operate and repair tools and equipment. Employees must possess the ability to lift, carry, push, and pull materials and objects averaging a weight of 60 pounds or heavier weights, in all cases with the use of proper equipment and/or assistance from other staff. Employees must wear and use the proper Personal Protective Equipment (PPE). ENVIRONMENTAL CONDITIONS Employee works in the field and are exposed to loud noise levels, cold and hot temperatures, inclement weather conditions, road hazards, vibration, confining workspace, chemicals, mechanical and/or electrical hazards, hazardous physical substances and fumes, dust, and air contaminants. Employees may interact with upset staff and/or public and private representatives in interpreting and enforcing District policies and procedures.

description: About Sungrow: Sungrow North America is a leading provider of renewable energy solutions, specializing in the development and manufacturing of photovoltaic inverters and energy storage systems. The company offers a comprehensive range of products and services designed to optimize the performance and efficiency of solar power installations.
