title: Assistant Project Manager
description: About Us Solar Landscape is the leading commercial rooftop solar developer in the U.S. Only 4% of commercial rooftops host solar today — we’re changing that, fast. Commercial rooftop solar is the fastest, smartest way to build new clean power — delivering megawatts of generation in months, not years, and powering America’s energy and future right where it’s needed most. By turning rooftops into local power plants, we’re reshaping how — and how fast — energy gets built in the U.S. Recognized as the 1 Distributed Generation Developer by New Project Media, the 1 National Commercial Rooftop Solar Developer by Solar Power World, and winner of the U.S. Department of Energy’s Grand Prize for Clean Energy, Solar Landscape is defining the future of energy generation in America. Headquartered in Asbury Park, New Jersey, Solar Landscape has offices in Chicago, Baltimore, and New York City and operates in over a dozen states nationwide. We move fast, solve hard problems, and take our work seriously — but never ourselves. We value clear thinking, accountability, and execution. At the same time, we’re collaborative by default, and believe the best work happens when people enjoy working together. Our team is made up of smart, grounded people who show up for each other — whether that’s troubleshooting a system design or catching up over lunch. If you’re looking to do meaningful work in a high-performance environment — and be part of the team reshaping how energy gets built in the U.S. — we’d love to meet you. About The Role We are currently seeking an Assistant Project Manager to support the successful execution of solar projects. The Assistant Project Manager will work closely with the Project Management team and be responsible for assisting with all aspects of project delivery, including project planning, budgeting, procurement, construction management, project controls and reporting, scheduling, and risk management. This role is based in Illinois (Greater Chicago area). Responsibilities Assist with planning, budgeting, management, and completion of PV projects. Coordinate design and permitting activities with engineering team and local authorities. Follow Solar Landscape Safety and Quality standards and make sure others are adhering to policies. Provide input on construction schedules for assigned projects. Solicit, negotiate, and execute subcontracts and purchase orders with timely delivery to support the project schedule. Schedule and manage deliveries of materials and equipment. Maintain accurate receiving records and provide timely follow up to missing items, damaged goods, backorders, etc. Assist with planning and execution of self-performed work and managing labor crews and subcontractors. Plan sequencing, crew-sizes, productivity goals, and monthly labor spend. Execute work and track actual results, adjusting and refining forecasts to reflect actual production. Help complete all job closeout procedures including AHJ inspections, interconnection, testing, documentation, Owner’s Engineer revies, Independent Engineer reviews. Build trust and rapport with all Solar Landscape departments. Qualifications Bachelor’s degree in Engineering or Construction Management preferred. Proficient in Microsoft Office Suite, Microsoft Project, and construction management software such as Dynamics 365. 2 years of experience in the solar industry, preferably in a project coordination or project support role. Strong understanding of commercial PV construction, including rooftop, ground-mount, and carport installations. Knowledge of behind-the-meter and utility interconnection processes. Excellent organizational and communication skills. Detail-oriented and self-motivated with the ability to work independently. Familiarity with construction safety standards; OSHA 10 or 30 certification preferred. Valid driver’s license with willingness to travel to job sites as needed. Ability to climb ladders and access building rooftops. Authorized to work in the United States on a full-time basis. $70,000 - $90,000 a year Salary will vary depending on your location and job-related skills and experience. This is an incentive-based position with the potential to earn more. For part-time roles, your compensation will be adjusted to reflect your hours. title: Site Surveyor
description: Empower Solar is a full service, residential solar installer looking experienced and driven individuals to join our ever-expanding team. We are currently looking for a full-time Solar Site Surveyor to assist documenting site information in order to design a photovoltaic system to meet the needs of our customer. Position Overview: The Site surveyor position is a very critical part our organizations internal team. Our site surveyors are the first person with boots on the ground at the jobsite representing our company. You will work closely with our Design and Engineering team along with fellow site surveyors. This position is responsible for gathering all information needed from a homeowner’s residence to ensure the design team can properly prepare permits needed to facilitate installation of photovoltaic systems. With the utilization of a drones & iPad, this position requires you to get aerial imagery of the home/property and take photos of the electrical panel, meter, obstructions, and general property info but not limited to taking physical measurements and documentation. Responsibilities and Duties: Assess job site conditions upon arrival such as roof tops and electrical panels Utilize Drones to capture aerial imagery Measure roof planes, vents, dormers, and chimneys as needed Measure and access attic structure and conditions Capture shade reading reports for designers and financing platforms Draw, document, and photograph roofs, Attic space and Electrical panels, including pre-existing damages Upload photos and site assessment documentation into Site Capture Inspect roofs for structural integrity Properly use Personal Protective Equipment Perform other tasks and duties as required Qualifications: 1-2 years of experience in the construction industry Solar installation experience is preferred but not required Ability to read, write, understand solar plans and designs as well as obtain excellent verbal communication Ability to work in challenging environments (hot sun, cold, wind, tight spaces, etc.) Capable of standing for long stretches of time and working at heights (on rooftops, climb ladders and stairs) Must be willing to travel Ability to establish and maintain cooperative working relationships with those contacted during work, including but not limited to peers and customers Ability to operate a computer, drone and smart phone for communication and uploading documents / photos Must be open to working different schedules Mon-Sun Current Driver’s license, and clean drivers abstract Benefits: We offer employees working full-time comprehensive benefits, including health coverage (medical, dental and vision), 401K, paid Holidays off, and Sick Leave. Physical Demands: While performing the duties of this job, the employee is frequently required to walk, climb, crawl, push, pull, reach, sit, stand, climb ladders, and work with various tools and equipment. Must be able to operate a pallet jack and forklift. Have to ability to listen, understand, and communicate in writing and verbally. The employee will frequently be required to lift objects up to 75 pounds. Requirements Clean driving and background record Valid CA Driver's License The ability to travel within California on a Weekly basis based on project location. Must be able to successfully pass pre-employment screening requirements

title: Solar Maintenance Technician II – Field Operations (Memphis, TN site)
description: Silicon Ranch is a fully integrated provider of customized renewable energy, carbon, and battery storage solutions for a diverse set of partners across North America. We are known for putting community partnerships first, and are the only renewable energy company in the U.S. that owns and operates all of its solar ranches and has a 100% track record for successful delivery. We have the largest utility scale agrivoltaics portfolio in the country under Regenerative Energy®, our nationally recognized holistic approach to project design, construction, and land management. Our model incorporates regenerative ranching and other regenerative land management practices to restore livelihoods and soil health, biodiversity, and water quality. Through our subsidiary, Clearloop, we are able to help businesses of all sizes reclaim their carbon footprint with a direct investment in building new solar projects while also helping bring renewable energy and economic development to distressed communities. By joining Silicon Ranch, you will be joining a team of experienced and dedicated individuals who have proven time and again that it is indeed possible to not only “make solar do more”, but to make the promise of carbon-free, renewable energy that benefits people right where it comes from a tangible, measurable, and replicable reality. Silicon Ranch is committed to creating a diverse and inclusive workplace that is reflective of the communities in which we work and serve. We are an equal opportunity employer and will consider all qualified applicants without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability, veteran status, and other legally protected characteristics. Job Description Position: Solar Maintenance Technician II – Field Operations Location: On-site, primarily in Memphis, TN. Overview: This position is responsible for the performance of corrective and preventative maintenance tasks within a defined set of facilities. These tasks include the inspection, troubleshooting, diagnosis, and remedy of issues impacting the production of the solar PV facility. This includes repair and/or replacement of electrical and mechanical components and subcomponents such as contactors, breakers, motors, bearings, PV modules, PLCs, transformers, etc. This position may also act as a safety second and assist more senior technicians as needed. The ideal candidate is a self-starter with a strong mechanical inclination and verifiable experience performing in the electrical trade, electrical or multicraft maintenance, or solar operations and maintenance. Experience performing maintenance tasks on DC, AC, and MV systems, communications equipment, and mechanical systems will translate well to this position. No direct solar PV experience is required. Main Responsibilities: Perform scheduled preventive maintenance tasks at each facility, including the full PV system, UPS, SCADA, substation, and MV/HV/OHE systems. Perform corrective maintenance tasks, both scheduled and unscheduled, at each facility, including the full PV system, UPS, SCADA, substation, and MV/HV/OHE systems. Respond to directives for emergency dispatches for critical systems as directed. Log all work performed via the Silicon Ranch CMMS platform. Perform electrical testing using IV Curve Tracers, Power Quality Meters, Insulation Resistance Testers, Multimeters, and other testing equipment as needed. Assist management with field investigations to support predictive analytics, root cause analysis, and serial defect reports. Provide site access to third party contractors and as directed. Assist with other site tasks, including land management, module washing, and vegetation management as directed. Attend internal and external training sessions as directed. Must be able to communicate effectively, collaboratively and responsibly with team members and management. Must be able to work alone as a self-starter and work within a team driving towards a common goal. Must be able to stand for long periods of time. Must be able to work outside in most weather conditions. Must be able to lift 50 pounds. Qualifications: Intermediate skills with computers and electronic equipment required Intermediate skills with Microsoft Office and Adobe Acrobat required Working knowledge of NEC, NFPA70E, and OSHA standards Valid Driver’s License Required OSHA 30 (must be obtained within 4 weeks of employment) CPR/BLS (must be obtained within 4 weeks of employment) State electrical license or NABCEP certification desired Ability to perform localized travel of up to 2 hours each way. Note: The first hour and Last hour of daily driving/travel is not paid. It is considered normal commute time. Education: High School Diploma or GED Experience: 3 years of experience in the electrical trade, electrical maintenance, multicraft maintenance, or the completion of a recognized apprenticeship program required. Solar installation, commissioning, or operations and maintenance experience highly desired. Experience with MV/HV systems, IT systems, inverters, T&D systems, substations, or other specialized electrical systems desired. Our interview process: A typical interview process at Silicon Ranch might include the below stages. Please note that we may make changes to these steps as needed, and details will be provided to you early on in the process. Introductory Interview with our recruiter Hiring Manager Interview to dive into technical skills and behavioral questions Panel Interview to assess cross-functional skills and dive deeper into technical skills Executive Interview to answer high-level questions about SRC and the team

Performs/assists with technical and administrative duties associated with operating and maintaining a power plant. May assist with site vegetation management plans, including running tractors, riding mowers, and other vegetation maintenance equipment as needed. Writes/assists with Plant Orders, Plant Procedures, Operating Instructions, and other documents assigned. Ensures work follows Environmental and Safety requirements and is appropriately documented. title: Solar Installer
description: About the role The Residential Roof Installer will assemble, install, or maintain solar photovoltaic (PV) systems on roofs or other structures in compliance with site assessment and schematics. title: PV Solar Technician
description: ACCIONA Energía is the biggest 100% renewable energy company with no fossil legacy in the world. Troubleshoot electrical and mechanical issues while following strict safety protocols. Conduct site inspections, safety analyses, and participate in safety training and emergency drills. Other responsibilities as assigned. Required Skills and Competencies Qualifications : 2 years of directly related experience in solar, renewable energy, or equivalent electrical environments. Capable of working in varying weather conditions, lifting up to 50 pounds, and performing physically demanding tasks in field environments. Willingness to travel and work night shifts or extended hours as needed. Benefits after 90 days : 401(k) with company match and immediate vesting, life insurance, disability coverage, paid parental leave, and other optional plans. 15 days of PTO (with 1 additional day per year of service), 9 public holidays, and 2 flexible holidays. $50 monthly reimbursement for health, wellness, or fitness-related memberships and equipment. title: Design Engineer
description: Inman Solar is a full-service solar company specializing in utility-scale and community solar. As a developer and EPC (Engineering, Procurement and Construction) contractor, we design and build solar farms as turn-key delivery. Founded in 2009, Inman Solar has established itself as the top contractor serving the eastern US. We are a team of highly skilled engineers and professionals passionate about the work and the impact we make. We value smart, proactive and results-driven people and are looking to grow our team to meet the continuously increasing demand for solar power. At Inman Solar every employee has a direct impact on the projects under design and construction. The project team works tightly with seamless coordination between the different disciplines, providing the candidates with an exceptional view to the fast-growing solar industry. Description: Inman Solar is seeking a motivated engineer for the position of Design Engineer. Working as an integral part of a knowledgeable and experienced team, the candidate will be involved in all aspects of solar project design and engineering and will see projects from conceptual design to final completion. The candidate will be responsible for creating design drawings and coordinating between design, procurement and construction. The role will require a strong understanding of the electrical and physical considerations of PV systems. A high level of project management and communication skills will be valuable to ensure a quality project is delivered on time and on budget. The Design Engineer will work under direct supervision of a Professional Engineer. Qualifications: • Educational background or industry experience in mechanical, electrical, or civil engineering • 2 years of relevant work experience • AutoCAD and Civil 3D experience preferred; CAD experience required • Microsoft Excel proficiency • Interest in sustainability and solar energy • High level of attention to detail, time management, and organization • Good communication skills Responsibilities: • Manage a team of external engineers and technicians to ensure the successful execution of solar project designs. • Integral contributor to the design of PV systems producing construction quality drawings (physical layout, electrical design, installation details, etc.) • Specify equipment and materials selection and lead procurement • Coordinate with installers to ensure correct and efficient installation • Travel to site to engage with constructors and support installation – expect roughly 10% travel • Perform PV Production modeling and performance testing • Stay up to date with code requirements and industry standards • Review environmental studies (e.g. geotechnical reports, wetlands & wildlife studies) and translate site-specific requirements to design.

Desired Skills, Expertise and Proficiencies : · Understands and promotes general workplace safety and the ability to follow safety standards as well as help the company improve upon the standards in place. · Experience with electrical systems and familiarity of basic safety principles to include LOTO and Electrical Safety. · Must have experience in operating personal computer with technical proficiency of standard business software. Experience with SCADA and Computerized Maintenance Management Systems is highly recommended. · Ability to excel in a collaborative, cross-functional and geographically diverse organization. · Integrity and excellent communication skills, both verbally and in writing with leaders and colleagues. · Promotes the site team; strong teammate and willing to assist others when necessary and appropriate. · High-energy, developed interpersonal skills and a strong work ethic. · Meticulous, with an ability to synthesize complex analysis, approach new challenges with creativity and summarize information in a manner that supports key decision makers. · Excellent hands-on abilities with strong technical skills. · Ability to read, write and understand English. · Ability to speak and understand Spanish and Portuguese is a plus. · Knowledge of applicable safety and environmental regulations · Demonstrates proactive enthusiasm for solving problems and adding value to the company. · Maintains a current level of professional knowledge. · Focuses on personal growth and development by actively seeking feedback and responding with action. · Ability to establish and maintain a positive and professional working relationship with all individuals. · Communicates openly and honestly, does not engage in gossip. · Models’ professional behaviors of conduct and decorum. Education / Experience: · Possess a high school diploma or GED. · One (1) or more years’ experience as a PV O&M solar technician or Three (3) or more years’ experience in a power plant. Experience in utility-scale projects is a plus. · Demonstrate knowledge of electrical and/or mechanical fundamentals (single craft journeyman skills) such as electrical measurements, control circuits, and solid-state theory application, and/or basic knowledge of operational characteristics of equipment and associated control devices installed in power facilities. · Ability to understand engineering, electrical single line and schematic drawings. · Understanding of the NEC codes and knowledge of NFPA 70E practices. title: Solar/BESS Operations Engineer
description: What The Role Is The Solar/BESS Operations Engineer is responsible for supporting the ongoing operations, maintenance, and performance optimization of utility-scale and commercial solar photovoltaic (PV) and Battery Energy Storage System (BESS) assets. This role focuses on troubleshooting, reliability improvement, root cause analysis, and the implementation of best practices to ensure safe, efficient, and cost-effective operation of solar and storage facilities. This hybrid position is located in Scottsdale, AZ. If you don’t meet 100% of the qualifications but see yourself contributing, please submit your resume. What You'll Be Doing Provide responsive engineering technical support for the Clearway Solar and BESS operating fleet. Recommend and drive solutions that maximize the reliability and operation of Solar and BESS equipment. Provide internal subject matter expertise for Solar modules, inverters, and BESS. Contribute to the development and updating of engineering specifications and operational procedures, leveraging lessons learned from operating plants. Support the O&M team during new project construction and acquisition, ensuring readiness for operation to Clearway standards. Review and evaluate BESS capacity testing. Support training programs for site personnel, sharing technical knowledge and promoting best practices. Evaluate equipment obsolescence and repowering opportunities or augmentation for existing Solar and BESS plants. Provide technical support for warranties and insurance claims. Support the Operations Engineering team more generally to solve complex problems associated with renewable energy equipment. What You'll Bring B.S. in an Engineering field related to Energy Systems or Technology. 3 years of experience. Ability to identify and implement detailed solutions to complex technical problems. Capable of managing small projects or tasks on a larger-scale project, and the ability to mentor less experienced technicians. Excellent written and oral communication skills to effectively communicate both internally and externally. Minimum of two years of experience with data historians and building performance monitoring tools. Advanced knowledge of battery operation and maintenance requirements. Experienced understanding of electrical power generation, operation, and maintenance. Able to read and interpret electrical drawings, technical manuals, and test reports. Must successfully function as a member of a team. Must be able to maintain a professional and positive company image and positive relationships with owners, customers, internal contractors, and external contractors. May be required to work flexible work hours at times. Ability to travel up to 20%. What Would Be Nice A minimum of three years of experience related to energy systems design, power distribution, renewable energy, or related industry. Knowledge of relay coordination, protection, and grounding schemes. Experience with power plant controllers for AC and/or DC-coupled ESS  PV. Knowledgeable in technical standards such as UL1703, UL1741, UL9540, UL9540A, NFPA 68, NFPA 69, NFPA 70, NFPA 72, & NFPA 855. No visa sponsorship or any kind of sponsorship for employment authorization is available for this role, now or in the future. LI-Hybrid The pay rate for the successful candidate will depend on geographic location, skills, relevant and demonstrated experience, education, training and certifications, and other factors permitted by law. This role is eligible to earn an annual cash bonus, subject to personal and company performance goals. Along with our public affiliate Clearway Energy, Inc., our portfolio comprises approximately 11.6 GW of gross generating capacity in 26 states, including 9.1 GW of wind, solar, and battery energy storage assets, and over 2.5 GW of conventional dispatchable power generation providing critical grid reliability services. Operation of relays, pad mounted switchgear, PV modules, PV arrays, inverters, and battery storage containers. Maturity, professionalism, and excellent communication skills both verbally and in writing; developed interpersonal skills and a strong work ethic. Demonstrated ability to research and interpret technical documents and data; Must be results oriented, a “fixer of things”, with a “Do what I do” leadership philosophy. Demonstrates enthusiasm for solving problems, maintain a current level of knowledge, and work in increase knowledge base and teach others on the team. Demonstrated knowledge of electrical or mechanical fundamentals (single craft journeyman skills) such as electrical measurements, control circuits, and electrical theory application. Basic knowledge of operational characteristics of equipment and associated control devices installed in power plants. Competence with relevant computer systems including but not limited to CMMS, DAS/SCADA, equipment-specific maintenance programs, and Microsoft Office programs. High degree of commitment to a quality safety culture and an incident-free work environment. Safety must be part of your DNA and be part of all that you do. NFPA 70E and OSHA 30 Certification. Candidates considered will have to provide documentation for college degrees and certification. This will be performed by an outside company that works with AES Clean Energy. Employees will be required to get a TWIC card. Ability to read and interpret equipment/facility schematics, maintenance instructions, procedures/manuals, process/procedure documents. Personal values consistent with those of the AES: Safety First, Highest Standards, and All Together. Ability to excel in a collaborative, cross-functional and geographically diverse organization. Excellent English written and verbal communication skills. Positive, professional, and collaborative work ethic. Detail oriented, high-energy, adept at problem solving and time management in sometimes high stress situations, highly organized. Must be able to lift 35 lbs. (OSHA) without assisted lift device or another employee. Must have eyesight corrected to 20/20, must have good hearing. Candidates cannot be color blind. Design and conduct process qualifications using design of experiments and statistical process control Work seamlessly with supply chain and production partners to complete design for manufacturing (DFM) changes necessary to meet factory rates and costs. title: Process Engineer

At Blue Origin, we envision millions of people living and working in space for the benefit of Earth. We’re working to develop reusable, safe, and low-cost space vehicles and systems within a culture of safety, collaboration, and inclusion. Join our team of problem solvers as we add new chapters to the history of spaceflight! This role is part of Advanced Concepts and Enterprise Engineering (ACE), supporting Blue Origin’s mission of millions of people living and working in space for the benefit of Earth. The team fosters innovation and drives engineering workflows of the future, shared solutions and standards, simplicity and lower costs, and manufacturable design. As part of a hardworking team of specialists, technicians, and engineers, you will own end-to-end integration verification for the New Product Introduction (NPI) lines that bring next-generation spacecraft solar arrays into production at unprecedented rates and reliability . This is an architecture-level opportunity for green-field design and process integration - the equipment is still being specified, the flow has not been locked, and the architecture is still a set of open decisions. You will work on a team of manufacturing, process, and ground support equipment engineers owning their individual process areas - cell interconnection, lamination and bonding, mechanism assembly, tooling, fixturing, automation. You own the interfaces between them and the overall performance of the manufacturing system as a whole . Your object is the value stream as a system, raw material intake through wing integration, verified end to end as scalable and stable for high volume production. You will use data to make enhancements to the solar array design with design engineers vertically integrated within the organization. You will not only ensure that each process works , but more importantly you will be responsible for making the i ntegrated system scalable. That is a claim about distributions and resource envelopes: process capability, equipment availability, yield, test throughput, and lot-to-lot variation. You will build the models that determine whether it closes, instrument the line to find out what it actually does , and generate the verification evidence the program's scalability claim rests on. You will partner with Operations to define the architecture the full-rate line s are built to, ensuring the lines inherit proven designs instead of new discovery, enabling a rapid ramp up to rate production. This is a hands-on building role. You will write the models yourself and be on the floor with the machines and instrumentation. You'll play a front seat role in architecting high volume production lines powering the next generation of space vehicles. We are primarily seeking a senior-level engineer to help establish and scale this capability, but are open to exceptional candidates at adjacent career levels whose manufacturing, industrialization, NPI, and cross-functional execution experience align with the needs of the role. We are tackling one of humanity’s most complex engineering challenges with a world-class team dedicated to delivering a revolutionary power platform. Cowboy Space Corporation is transforming how civilization powers, computes and connects - from orbit to Earth. Background Cowboy Space Corporation is building the infrastructure to power and connect the orbital economy. Our modular, scalable satellites collect sunlight in Low Earth Orbit to enable multiple integrated applications: transmitting energy via infrared lasers (space-to-earth and space-to-space), powering on-orbit high-performance computing clusters (GPU/TPU), and providing secure, high bandwidth optical data transport. Current energy and data systems rely on complex logistics and outdated infrastructure. Cowboy Space Corporation overcomes these challenges by enabling direct, on-demand, secure, and scalable energy distribution and data processing from space. This will revolutionize how we operate in orbit and on Earth, supporting the rapidly expanding space industrial base, ISAM (In-Space Servicing, Assembly, and Manufacturing) operations, remote regions, and military bases. Baiju Bhatt founded Cowboy Space Corporation in 2024. Inspired by his father’s work with NASA Langley Research Center, Baiju earned his B.S. in Physics and M.S. in Mathematics at Stanford before co-founding Robinhood, now a public company that has helped over 20 million Americans access the financial system. Cowboy Space Corporation has raised ~$365 million from Index Ventures, Interlagos, Construct Ventures, Breakthrough Energy Ventures, Andreessen Horowitz, NEA, and others. This is an ambitious mission that demands extraordinary talent. Cowboy Space Corporation ’s team has worked at places like SpaceX, Blue Origin, Stoke Space, Astranis and NASA, and is based in San Carlos, CA. If you're ready to solve complex technical challenges and help build the most important energy company in the world, we want to hear from you. The Role As a Mechanical Engineer – Solar Array Deployable Structures, you will be the responsible engineer for the large deployable structure that supports and positions our solar array. This is a mechanisms-first, hands-on role: you will architect and own the deployment mechanism along with its actuation, latching, and stowage, and the structural design that makes a very large deployed structure stiff, light, and reliable. You will own this hardware end to end, from concept and analysis through the ground testbeds used to prove it out, qualification, and on-orbit deployment. Deploying a very large structure reliably is the central challenge of the role. You will work closely with structures, manufacturing, GN&C, power, avionics, propulsion, and software teams to deliver an integrated array. We’re looking for a strong deployable-mechanism background paired with solid structural analysis skills—someone who can move quickly, iterate often, and take full ownership of hardware that directly determines whether our spacecraft gets the power it needs on orbit. Responsibilities Own the design of the deployable structure’s mechanism from concept through flight, including actuation, deployment sequencing, latching and locking at full extension, and stowage and launch restraint. Design and analyze the deployment kinematics, actuation, synchronization, and end-of-travel latching, and quantify deployment reliability, force/torque margin, and jam resistance. Design mechanism details—bearings, guides, drives, dampers, and release devices—with attention to tribology, space-rated lubrication, and repeatable, low-shock deployment. Perform structural analysis of the deployed and stowed structure—deployed stiffness and fundamental frequency, buckling and stability, strength, and thermal distortion—and design to meet stiffness and pointing requirements. Design the interfaces to the solar array and its supporting hardware, balancing structural stiffness against operational loads and dynamics. Design, build, and operate ground testbeds and dev rigs, including gravity-offload deployment fixtures for a very large structure, to characterize the mechanism, validate deployment, and de-risk the flight design. Develop and execute deployment, life/cycle, structural static/modal, vibration, thermal-vacuum, and qualification/acceptance test programs to verify flight-worthiness. Drive design-for-manufacturing of long, precision structural elements—tolerances, straightness, and repeatability—and work with suppliers to ensure high-quality, scalable production. Author and maintain drawings, interface control documents, analysis reports, test procedures, and release/configuration records. Diagnose and resolve mechanism and structural anomalies during integration and test, applying root-cause analysis and implementing corrective actions. Partner with structures, GN&C, power, avionics, propulsion, and software teams to ensure the array integrates seamlessly within the overall spacecraft architecture, including low-frequency flexible-body dynamics. Embrace a fast-paced development environment, driving quick design cycles, hardware builds, and test campaigns to accelerate the program schedule. Basic Qualifications BS or MS in Mechanical Engineering, Aerospace Engineering, or a related field 3 years of experience designing and analyzing deployable mechanisms and/or precision mechanical hardware in aerospace or other high-performance environments Strong mechanism fundamentals: kinematics, actuation, springs and stored energy, motors and drives, bearings, latches, tribology, and deployment reliability Solid structural fundamentals: stiffness, buckling and stability, strength, and structural dynamics of slender or lightweight structures Hands-on experience building and testing mechanisms, including deployment testing Experience taking hardware from concept through build and test, with hands-on integration and test experience Proficiency with CAD (e.g., NX, SolidWorks, or similar) Experience working in fast-paced, hardware-focused development environments Preferred Qualifications Direct experience designing deployable booms, masts, or large deployable structures for solar arrays, antennas, or similar Experience with composite structures—design, analysis, layup, bonding, and joint design—and composite fabrication and test Experience with large or flexible-blanket solar arrays, including deployment, tensioning, and stowage Experience designing and operating gravity-offload or deployment test rigs for large or long structures Experience designing for space environments (thermal, vibration, vacuum) and background in spacecraft mechanisms, structures, or deployables Familiarity with structural dynamics of large flexible structures and their interaction with GN&C (low-frequency modes, pointing, jitter) Experience with space-rated lubrication, tribology, and mechanism qualification Knowledge of aerospace standards (MIL-SPEC, NASA-STD, ECSS) and spaceflight hardware qualification and acceptance margins Startup or early-stage hardware experience; comfort operating with significant technical ambiguity Compensation and Benefits The salary range for this position is $100,000 – $300,000 annually. The actual base salary offered will depend on factors such as job-related skills, experience, qualifications, and internal equity. Equity in Cowboy Space Corp. Employees and their eligible dependents may enroll in medical, dental, and vision insurance 401(k) retirement savings plan Paid time off 10 paid holidays per calendar year Paid parental leave Relocation assistance if applicable Daily lunch in the office and a fully stocked kitchen with beverages and snacks ITAR Requirements Export Control Requirement: To conform to U.S. Government space technology export regulations, including the International Traffic in Arms Regulations (ITAR), applicants must be a U.S. citizen, lawful permanent resident of the U.S., protected individual as defined by 8 U.S.C. 1324b(a)(3), or eligible to obtain the required authorizations from the U.S. Department of State. Learn more about ITAR here. Disclaimer This job description is a summary of the primary duties and responsibilities of the job and position. title: Solar Technician

title: Manufacturing Engineer - Solar Module Manufacturing
description: The Company: Solestial is pioneering the future of space-based solar power by developing advanced solar technologies optimized for the harsh conditions of space. Our innovative, low-cost, and scalable solar arrays are engineered for next-generation satellites, spacecraft, and orbital infrastructure. We are driven by a mission to power the space economy and unlock limitless opportunities in orbit and beyond. The Role: As a Manufacturing Engineer – Solar Module Manufacturing , you will develop, optimize, and implement the materials and manufacturing processes used to build Solestial’s solar modules. You will work closely with Product/ Process Engineering, Manufacturing, Equipment, and Quality teams to translate module designs into reliable, repeatable, and scalable production processes. Your Mission: Develop, optimize, and create manufacturing processes & documentation for solar module assembly and integration. Collaborate with design engineering in the evaluation and selection of materials, including polymers, adhesives, thermal interface materials, and electrical insulation materials. Translate product and design requirements into practical manufacturing processes, work instructions, and process specifications. Plan and execute process trials, experiments, and qualification activities to improve yield, quality, reliability, and manufacturability. Coordinate materials characterization, process validation, design verification, and hardware qualification testing. Troubleshoot materials, process, and integration issues in partnership with Manufacturing, Product, Equipment, and Quality teams. Support the transfer of new module designs and processes from development into production. Develop process controls, acceptance criteria, and standard methodologies that ensure consistent, high-quality module production. Support supplier selection, material qualification, and ongoing supplier improvement efforts. Identify opportunities to improve process capability, cycle time, cost, and scalability as production grows. Create and source customer packaging designs. What You Bring: Bachelor’s degree in Materials Science, Chemical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Manufacturing Engineering, or a related field. At least 5 years of experience in process engineering, materials engineering, or manufacturing engineering, preferably within the solar, semiconductor, aerospace, or advanced manufacturing industries. Hands-on experience developing, optimizing, and implementing manufacturing processes for complex hardware or assemblies. Strong knowledge of materials selection, characterization, and testing, particularly polymers, adhesives, thermal interface materials, and electrical insulation materials. Experience translating product requirements into manufacturing processes, material specifications, process specifications, and work instructions. Experience with process validation, qualification testing, troubleshooting, root-cause analysis, and continuous improvement. Ability to use structured process-development tools such as DOE, SPC, process capability analysis, and PFMEA. Experience supporting the transfer of new products or processes from development into manufacturing. Familiarity with supplier selection, material qualification, supplier development, and ongoing performance evaluation. Strong cross-functional communication skills and the ability to work effectively with Product, Manufacturing, Equipment, and Quality teams. What Gives You an Edge: Experience with solar cell or solar module manufacturing, assembly, and integration. Background in semiconductor, photovoltaic, aerospace, or other high-reliability manufacturing environments. Hands-on experience with module integration processes such as bonding, lamination, encapsulation, interconnection, thermal management, or insulation. Experience scaling new materials and processes from development through qualification and production. Familiarity with spaceflight hardware requirements, environmental testing, and qualification standards. A practical, hands-on approach to troubleshooting and a willingness to work directly with equipment, materials, and production teams. Comfort operating in a fast-paced environment where processes are still being developed and priorities evolve. Our Benefits: Competitive salary Generous, high-quality medical, dental, and vision coverage on day one of employment 15 vacation days, 5 sick days, and 10 paid holidays annually - with an extended holiday break at year’s end 401K with employer match up to 4% of salary Employer-paid short-term and long-term disability and employer-sponsored life insurance Your work will literally go to space!

title: Project Manager - Solar & Storage
description: Job Description Senior Project Manager | San Diego or Los Angeles, CA (Hybrid) Ever managed a project that touched solar, storage, EV charging and a microgrid, all under one contract? You won't be siloed into a single technology here. This Senior Project Manager role owns projects end to end, from contract signature through construction to handover, across solar PV, battery storage and EV charging on the same portfolio. If you want your next role to stretch further than the last one, this is the shape of that. title: Field Service Technician - BESS
description: About Sungrow: Sungrow North America is a leading provider of renewable energy solutions, specializing in the development and manufacturing of photovoltaic inverters and energy storage systems. The company offers a comprehensive range of products and services designed to optimize the performance and efficiency of solar power installations. Sungrow North America is known for its commitment to innovation, high-quality standards, and exceptional customer service, aiming to provide sustainable and reliable energy solutions to meet the growing demand for clean power. The Position: This role supports areas of field Service operation within Sungrow USA related to commissioning, warranty, and Operations and Maintenance (O&M) of the expanding installed sites in the region. Reporting to the regional field service supervisor, this position is responsible for troubleshooting, repairing, maintaining, and commissioning support of PV inverters and ancillary equipment/ systems, usually at the customer’s site or at a staging yard/warehouse. This position will comply with the Safety Mandate, “ZERO HARM,” to ensure safe and efficient work and operation of the facility for all personnel and equipment. Ensures that personnel and safety issues are given priority to maintaining a safe and efficient working environment. Implements and enforces safety management policy and procedures regarding the facility: safety information, hazard analysis, safe operations/Maintenance Training, subcontractor compliance, plant integrity, work permits, emergency planning, and response. Duties and Responsibilities: Perform a variety of technical assignments involving the installation, operation, testing, and maintenance of string and central solar inverter and/or BESS Systems, PCS, batteries, and ancillary equipment. Perform general troubleshooting and diagnosis under Sungrow’s maintenance and repair guidelines. As needed, support and perform pre-commissioning (with and without grid emulator) and commissioning of solar inverters and BESS systems within schedule and work plans Additionally, for those on O&M capacity, perform Preventive Maintenance and other Long Term Service Agreement (LTSA) activities per the contract Investigate solar plant issues such as DC array grid faults, inverter design issues, and utility grid transients. For BESS positions, these investigations may also involve SOC checks and module /component-level troubleshooting, replacement of electrical/electronic parts, SW version updates, etc. Provide feedback to the engineering and project team on possible mechanical and electrical design improvements. Lead upgrade/rework projects (software and hardware) in the field and interact with customers to explain the project's technical scope and manage work schedule and commitments. Work with customer SCADA engineers to set up systems communication and parameters involving Sungrow’s controllers and F&G systems as needed. Accurately describes troubleshooting sequences and procedures which they have observed Identifies and documents basic mechanical and electrical issues and problems Performs basic corrective maintenance Create/modify Field Service procedures for safety troubleshooting and maintenance if required. When using contractors on sites, act as the Lead to ensure the contractors submit daily activity reports and JSA reports and work follows Sungrow standards and expectations. Prepare and submit own Daily Activity Reports and Daily JSA Reports. Work independently in the field and with Design Engineers to resolve high-level technical issues, support the investigation of the root cause for technology applications for complex projects Coordinate and work closely with other engineering, logistic, financial, and program management disciplines to maintain the solar plant operations. Verify and comply with engineering documentation standards and test procedures. C ompletes documentation in a timely and organized fashion Follow level-appropriate standard operating procedures. Own creation and submission of all field paperwork and documentation for full compliance with site documentation and project requirement Serve as a safety second if needed. Education or Desired License and Certificates: Associate’s Degree in an Engineering or Computer Science Discipline from an accredited university or college Renewable industry experience is desired Power Electronics experience is desired OSHA 10 certificate within 12 months of date of hire NFPA 70e certificate within 12 months of date of hire Competencies: Perform essential job functions using proper techniques that may include lifting, carrying, pushing, and pulling tools, equipment, and materials. Lift and carry items weighing up to 50 pounds, with or without reasonable accommodation. Engage in frequent standing, walking, bending, stooping, kneeling, crouching, and reaching during field assignments. Work in a variety of field environments, including confined spaces, uneven surfaces, and varying weather conditions. Follow all company safety policies and training requirements, including the use of personal protective equipment (PPE). Comprehend Job Hazard Analysis and conduct level-appropriate Job Hazard Analysis. Designated as Authorized Person for LOTO. Minimum Requirements: Proficient in the use of Microsoft Office, including Word, Excel, Outlook, PowerPoint Motivated self-starter with complex problem-solving abilities. A ‘completer-finisher’ taking accountability for ideas from inception to delivery in an environment that requires robust metrics to confirm the success. Excellent verbal and written communication skills and the ability to interact professionally with a diverse group of partners, senior managers, and subject matter experts. 3 plus years of overall experience in a technical field 2 years of experience in solar inverters or BESS Must possess the ability to work with test equipment and hand tools as required. Must be able to closely follow instructions and pre-established procedures/SOP to perform the ductions of the job Must be proficient in Microsoft Office Suite (Word, Excel, PowerPoint and Outlook) OSHA, NFPA70A, Electrical Safety Experience and/or certification with MV transformers a plus Must have a valid driver’s license with a clean driving record. Travel: 80% Plus Work Location and Status: Contract role, Columbus, OH area No visa/legal sponsorship Compensation: Compensation commensurate with experience Competitive benefits package and employee programs Strong personal and company growth opportunities For candidates in the states of California, Colorado, New York and Washington, the anticipated base pay for this role is between $36 to $40 per hour plus OT. This range does not include any other compensation components or other benefits that an individual may be eligible for. The base pay offered is dependent upon several factors, including but not limited to job-related skills, qualifications, experience, education, location, or other factors related to the role. Sungrow is an equal opportunity employer. Due to strong interests in this position, Sungrow will only reach out to those candidates who best meet the requirements. Thank you for your interest in Sungrow.

You’ll be part of a team that partners with top energy clients nationwide to build a more sustainable future—one solar project at a time. This is a traveling position (up to 100%), where you will be onsite at a project location. You have the potential to be placed on a project site located in any state throughout the US. You’ll spend 8-16 months on average per project. We offer designated daily per diem in addition to base pay to support and help you cover living expenses. A vehicle allowance will be provided. Our company has one of the industry leading rotational programs as well, with routine travel home from the jobsite. Company Overview MasTec Renewables, comprised of Wanzek Construction, IEA Constructors, and White Construction, combines over 20 years of experience in renewable energy construction. Depending on your position and project, you may work for one or more of our companies over your career with us. Join one of the largest construction firms in the country (Engineering News-Record [ENR]: 1 in Power, 17 Top 50 Domestic Heavy Contractors, 20 Transportation Contractor). We embrace diverse perspectives among our employees and across all levels of our business, including our suppliers, community partners, and clients. We have built a multidimensional workforce that brings valuable differences in perspectives, work ethics, and approaches to our organization. By collaborating across departments, we foster innovation and encourage everyone—from interns to executives—to share their ideas and make an impact. Our goal is to create a respectful work environment where all employees feel valued, included, and empowered to become innovative leaders in our industry. The MasTec Renewables market sector is part of the MasTec Clean Energy & Infrastructure business segment. MasTec’s Clean Energy & Infrastructure (CE&I) segment generates over $4.5 billion in annual revenue, providing construction services across industrial, renewables and infrastructure sectors. Our renewables sector focuses on solar, wind and battery storage. Sustainability and safety are foundational to our culture and influence everything we do. Request, review, and process submittals, RFIs, and shop drawings through digital construction management platforms (such as Procore, Aconex, or equivalent) for formal review. Communicate review statuses from the Architect/Engineer (A/E) and CM back to subcontractors and vendors, maintaining detailed records and follow-ups. Track construction schedules continuously to advise of potential cost impacts or roadblocks, immediately informing subcontractors and suppliers when appropriate. Attend weekly PM meetings and relay all pertinent scheduling, resource, and safety data to the Field Operations and site Foremen. Verify internally and externally that all subcontractors and vendors are working off approved documents and have proper site clearance (including badges, insurance, PO execution, and site safety training). title: Performance Engineer
description: Summary: The Performance Engineer is a technical role supporting Summit Ridge Energy's solar PV and energy storage portfolio, from preconstruction through commissioning and long-term operations. Working under the guidance of senior engineers, this role supports the analysis and validation of energy models, system designs, and performance data to help protect production assumptions and asset value across the project lifecycle. This is a strong opportunity for an early-career engineer to build hands-on experience across solar performance modeling, field diagnostics, and cross-functional project support. About Us: Summit Ridge Energy is the nation’s leading commercial solar power company. By merging financial innovation and unmatched execution, we deliver reliable, locally generated energy that reduces reliance on foreign energy and contributes to a more resilient and secure electric grid. Summit Ridge is driving a future where solar power generation strengthens local economies and ensures energy independence for businesses and communities across America. Role and Responsibilities: Energy Modeling & Technical Due Diligence Support energy modeling activities using PVsyst (or equivalent), assisting with proposal development, preconstruction analysis, and performance guarantee assumptions under senior engineer guidance. Assist in reviewing design inputs affecting modeled energy and performance — meteorological data, equipment selection, losses, clipping, soiling, and degradation. Support technical due diligence activities throughout the project lifecycle, helping flag potential performance risks for senior review. Performance Testing & Field Diagnostics Assist in the development and execution of capacity and availability test procedures aligned with contract requirements and industry-standard methodologies (e.g., ASTM E2848). Support capacity and availability test analyses, helping compile data to validate plant performance and determine pass/fail results. Review system troubleshooting, diagnostics, and electrical testing reports provided by the EPC (Isc, Voc, insulation resistance, IV curve tracing, thermal imaging, etc.), escalating discrepancies to senior engineers. Monitor SCADA, DAS, inverter, and tracker UIs to help identify underperformance trends and support commissioning troubleshooting. Assist in troubleshooting Summit Ridge Energy's Data Acquisition System (DAS) platform and associated databases. Stakeholder & Project Coordination Support coordination with Independent Engineer (IE) consultants, EPC contractors, and internal teams to help ensure timely project closing. Assist in interfacing with Operations, Asset Management, Engineering, and Project Management to help identify and track issues affecting performance and asset value. Communicate regularly with stakeholders and respond promptly to routine requests. Financial Alignment & Reporting Assist Project Finance and FP&A teams in compiling energy model inputs and production data for financial models and investment materials. Help prepare supporting documentation for lender, tax equity, and investor technical diligence under senior guidance. Prepare monthly, quarterly, and annual performance reports and contribute to technical memoranda and test reports. Standards & Continuous Improvement Build working knowledge of applicable codes and standards (e.g., NEC, UL, IEEE, IEC, ASTM) and industry testing methodology. Contribute ideas for improving modeling accuracy, testing procedures, and execution outcomes. Comply with all company policies and standards, including promoting a strong safety culture. Required Skills/Competencies: Education: Bachelor's degree in Electrical Engineering, Renewable Energy, Industrial Management, Physics, or a related field (ABET-accredited preferred). Experience: 1 year of related professional, internship, or co-op experience as a Performance Engineer, Solar Engineer, Assistant Project Manager, or in a closely related role within renewable energy. Some exposure to PVsyst or equivalent solar energy modeling software (coursework, internship, or professional experience). Basic understanding of capacity and availability test procedures, such as ASTM E2848 (formal execution experience not required). Exposure to system troubleshooting, diagnostics, or electrical testing concepts (Isc, Voc, insulation resistance, IV curve tracing, thermal imaging, etc.). Familiarity with SCADA, DAS, or MET station data, or a strong willingness to learn. General understanding of project contracts (EPC, O&M, Interconnection, Lease, Financing, and supply agreements) preferred but not required. Basic knowledge of technical due diligence and risk assessment concepts. Strong computer skills, including Excel and Microsoft Office Suite (Word, PowerPoint, SharePoint). Exposure to databases, CRM, and/or ERP platforms such as Salesforce and Procore is a plus. Familiarity with AI-assisted productivity tools, e.g. Claude. Strong written and verbal communication skills; strong attention to detail and organizational skills. Eagerness to learn and work methodically in a quantitative, fast-paced environment. title: Electrical Estimator
description: Job Summary Sun Tribe EPC (“Sun Tribe”) is Virginia’s premier utility-scale solar design and build firm, specializing in sub-20MW ground-mounted solar photovoltaic (PV) facilities. Our construction efforts are focused throughout the Commonwealth of Virginia, Maryland, and neighboring states. At Sun Tribe, we build with purpose - prioritizing safety, quality, and environmental stewardship in every project we deliver. Sun Tribe EPC’s Preconstruction Team’s mission is to develop quality business opportunities that enable efficient delivery in a predictable manner. The Electrical Estimator plays an important role in that mission by developing accurate and competitive electrical and mechanical project estimates for small utility-scale solar and battery energy storage projects. The Electrical Estimator independently manages the non-civil estimating scope for assigned opportunities, working closely with Civil Estimating, Project Engineering, Supply Chain, subcontractors, project owners, and developers. This role develops project estimates, evaluates subcontractor and vendor pricing, identifies scope and cost risks and opportunities, and supports projects from early-stage estimating through award, project budgeting, and deliberate handoff to Project Management. This position reports directly to the VP of Preconstruction and serves as the electrical estimating subject matter expert for Preconstruction and cross-functional project teams. Principal Responsibilities Owns the development and completion of project-level internal estimates (“Cost Stacks”), excluding civil site work developed by the Civil Estimator. Performs detailed quantity takeoffs for DC and AC electrical systems from back of module to point of interconnection for solar and battery energy storage projects. Develops detailed electrical cost estimates, budgets, and proposals based on quantity takeoffs and vendor and subcontractor pricing. Analyzes electrical drawings, specifications, owner requirements, and other project documentation to determine scope, schedule, quantities, risks, and opportunities. Analyzes labor, material, and equipment costs to develop accurate and competitive bids. Coordinates with Supply Chain and Engineering to obtain equipment, material, engineering, and other applicable project pricing and scope information. Creates comprehensive RFPs and leads bid clarification and scope review discussions with electrical and mechanical subcontractors. Reviews and levels subcontractor proposals to identify scope gaps, qualifications, exclusions, risks, and pricing differences. Develops project-specific inclusions, exclusions, and clarifications for electrical and mechanical scopes that align with client requirements and project objectives. Develops independent, stand-alone electrical estimates for assigned bids to evaluate subcontractor pricing. Collaborates with Project Management and Supply Chain to ensure estimates, RFPs, subcontractor proposals, and supporting documentation are completed in accordance with bid schedules. Supports development and maintenance of a qualified electrical and mechanical subcontractor network to promote a healthy and competitive bidding environment. Converts bid estimates into project budgets following project award and provides estimating support for change orders and RFIs as needed. Supports deliberate project handoff from Preconstruction to Project Management by communicating estimate assumptions, scope, pricing, inclusions and exclusions, risks, opportunities, and relevant bid history. Compares actual project costs to estimates and incorporates lessons learned into future estimating practices. Contributes to continuous improvement of estimating tools, templates, historical pricing data, SOPs, and processes. Basic Qualifications Required High school diploma or GED required; bachelor’s degree in an engineering discipline preferred, or equivalent relevant engineering, design, or construction experience. Minimum two (2) years of electrical estimating experience required. Strong Microsoft Excel skills required. Strong understanding of electrical engineering drawings, design documents, specifications, and construction methodologies. Ability to manage multiple estimates, priorities, and bid deadlines simultaneously. Skills & Experience Preferred Experience performing electrical quantity takeoffs and developing construction cost estimates. Experience estimating medium-voltage interconnected solar facilities. Experience with electrical estimating software such as Trimble Accubid, McCormick, ConEst IntelliBid, PlanSwift, or similar. Experience with Procore or other construction management software. Experience with scheduling software such as MS Project. Experience using AI tools to support estimating, analysis, or process efficiency. Excellent organizational, analytical, and problem-solving skills with a high degree of attention to detail. Strong written and verbal communication and negotiation skills, with the ability to effectively collaborate with subcontractors, vendors, and cross-functional internal teams. Alignment with Sun Tribe's core values: Community, Safety, Perpetual Improvement, Nature, Joy, and Respect. Commitment to a culture of safety, accountability, and high-quality project delivery. Working Conditions and Physical Requirements Hybrid work environment, with work performed remotely and from Sun Tribe’s Charlottesville office based on business needs. Ability to travel to the Charlottesville office, project sites, and other business locations as needed, typically averaging one to two trips per month. Occasional overnight travel may be required. Some evening and weekend work may be required based on bid deadlines and business needs. Ability to perform work in a general office and hybrid work environment. Exposure to typical construction site conditions and hazards during project site visits. Required to wear appropriate personal protective equipment (PPE) while on project sites. This position is eligible for Sun Tribe’s comprehensive benefits package, which includes medical, dental, and vision insurance, 401(k) with company match, life and disability insurance, paid time off, volunteer days, and access to an employee assistance program. title: Field Service Technician II – Solar
description: WORK ARRANGEMENT: ON-SITE, FIELD-BASED. THIS IS NOT A REMOTE OR WORK-FROM-HOME JOB. This role is performed in person, outdoors, on solar sites in and around St. Louis, Missouri. You must already live within commuting distance of St. Louis, or be prepared to relocate there at your own expense before your start date. You may see this listed as "field-based." That means you drive from your home to job sites rather than reporting to an office each morning. It does not mean you can work from another city or state. Applications from candidates who are not located in — or actively relocating to — the St. Louis area cannot be considered for this posting. Territory: [30–90 minutes typical, rarely over 3 hours]. Overnight travel: [under 10%]. Schedule: [M–F, 7am–3pm or 8am–4pm]. On-call: [rotational Saturday 8am–12pm]. Overtime: [paid biweekly; 40–45 hours typical; 1.5x over 40]. SOLAR EXPERIENCE HELPS. IT IS NOT REQUIRED. STRONG ELECTRICAL AND DIAGNOSTIC SKILLS ARE. Energy Support Services keeps solar and energy storage systems safe, reliable, and producing clean power. As a Field Service Technician II – Solar, you’ll work independently on advanced inspections, preventative maintenance, and system troubleshooting — operating safely in high-voltage environments without direct supervision, guiding junior technicians on site, and progressing along a defined pathway toward Technician III. If you have two or more years of serious hands-on technical work in any industry and you’re the person people bring the problem nobody else could figure out, we want your application. COMING FROM ANOTHER TRADE? THIS IS THE PART TO READ. We hire experienced technicians out of other industries at this level regularly, and we build the solar knowledge on top. Here’s how your background translates: Automotive, diesel, or heavy equipment — Root-cause diagnosis, circuit tracing, reading schematics, using a scan tool and DMM, working to torque spec, and writing up findings. You’ll trade flat-rate for a salary, and your tool box for ours. HVAC/R, especially commercial or light-industrial — Control circuits, contactors, VFDs, three-phase power, service calls run solo, and preventative maintenance on a schedule. Very close cousin to this work. Telecommunications, broadband, or utility line work — Working at height, terminations, test equipment, prints, and outdoor work in every kind of weather. Your safety habits are already right. Industrial maintenance, wind, or power generation — Lockout/tagout discipline, medium-voltage awareness, PM programs, and CMMS documentation all carry directly across. Military technical specialties — Power generation, electrical systems, avionics, and electronics maintenance transfer cleanly. The tools you’ll learn (and their equivalents you may already know) I/V curve tracer — measures the performance curve of a string of solar modules to find underperformance. Conceptually similar to putting a vehicle or motor on a load test. Megohmmeter ("Megger") / insulation resistance tester — finds insulation breakdown and ground faults. If you’ve used one in industrial or motor work, it’s the same instrument. Infrared thermography — thermal imaging to find hot spots in connections and modules. If you’ve used a thermal camera on bearings, panels, or refrigerant lines, you’re already there. Drone-based aerial thermal inspection — we pay for your FAA Part 107 and teach you the flight work. PAY $75,000 – $95,000 annually, depending on experience and qualifications. WHAT WE OFFER Tools and equipment: provided. Company truck, company fuel/credit card, and vehicle maintenance card. You will never spend your own money on tools here — no tool truck payment, no tool debt. Bonus: Up to an 8% performance bonus, paid annually. Apparel: Company-provided PPE and flame-resistant clothing kit (bibs, jackets, pants, shirts) at no cost to you. Health: Medical, dental, and vision. We pay 80% of your health insurance premiums. Retirement: 401(k) with up to a 7.5% company match. Time off: PTO accrued each pay period — 120 hours/year (years 0–2), 160 hours (years 3–9), 200 hours (10 years) — plus 11 paid holidays. Family: 8 weeks of paid parental leave. Insurance: Company-paid Life and AD&D insurance at 1x your annual salary. Certifications — we pay, you keep them: OSHA 10/30, NFPA 70E/70B, FAA Part 107 (drone), and our internal O&M Tech course series. These certifications stay with you for the rest of your career. Advancement: A published Field Tech Development Pathway with defined progression to Technician III. You move up on demonstrated capability, not on how long you’ve been here. Education: Tuition reimbursement up to $10,000 per year for approved programs. WHAT YOU'LL DO Safety Lead by example in promoting a safe working culture in the field. Perform approved hazardous electrical energy control procedures and select the exact PPE required for each task. Participate in and actively critique Pre-Job Briefs and Job Safety Analysis (JSA). Apply personal lockout/tagout as a worker, or serve as work leader once approved. Inspections and preventative maintenance Perform comprehensive electrical and mechanical inspections of solar energy systems. Conduct advanced preventative maintenance including infrared thermography, insulation resistance testing, and I/V curve tracing — all of which we train you on. Help build and implement preventative maintenance schedules for your assigned sites. Troubleshooting Independently diagnose and troubleshoot system and operational issues. Operate and troubleshoot safely in 600VAC and 1500VDC environments without direct supervision. Note: 1500VDC is a higher DC voltage than most trades encounter — this is exactly why our safety training is extensive, paid, and mandatory before you work unsupervised. Use specialized diagnostic tools and root-cause analysis to handle equipment repairs and replacements. Documentation Create and maintain detailed, accurate records of inspections, maintenance, and repairs with minimal oversight. Prepare clear technical reports and actionable equipment recommendations for the Team Lead. Knowledge sharing Stay current on industry best practices, safety updates, and emerging technology. Share your expertise and give supportive guidance to junior technicians on site. Help improve the quality, clarity, and safety content of our training materials. Support your teammates and take on other duties as assigned. WHAT YOU NEED High school diploma or equivalent. 2 years of hands-on technical, electrical, or mechanical work in any industry — solar, electrical, automotive, diesel, HVAC/R, telecommunications, wind, power generation, industrial maintenance, utilities, or a military technical specialty. Solid working understanding of electrical fundamentals — AC and DC theory, series and parallel circuits, grounding, and safe work practices around energized equipment. Confident with a multimeter and able to read, interpret, and work from electrical schematics or engineering drawings. Strong analytical, time management, and problem-solving skills, and a track record of working independently without someone checking on you. Strong communication skills and the patience to bring a junior technician along. Valid driver’s license and clean driving record. Helpful, but we’ll train and certify you Solar-specific or grid-tied PV system experience. FAA Part 107 drone certification — we pay for it. OSHA 30 and NFPA 70E — we pay for these as well. Hands-on time with I/V curve tracers, megohmmeters, or insulation testers — or comparable diagnostic instruments from another trade. Familiarity with Data Acquisition Systems (DAS) or SCADA — the monitoring systems that report site performance remotely. PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS Drive a vehicle confidently and with a high degree of safety. Stand for long periods and walk distances up to three miles per day. Navigate ladders, stairs, scaffolding, and ramps while maintaining three points of contact. Have visual acuity for depth perception, no field-of-vision issues, and the ability to distinguish between colors. Work comfortably in a range of climate conditions, including extreme heat (above 100°F) or extreme cold (below 32°F), for periods of more than one hour. Exert up to 50 pounds of force occasionally, up to 30 pounds frequently, and up to 10 pounds constantly to move objects. Applicants must be authorized to work for any employer in the U.S. We are unable to sponsor or take over sponsorship of employment visas at this time. Additionally, this position may qualify for a comprehensive benefits package, including Retirement Benefits, Medical, Dental & Vision, Health Savings Account, Flexible Spending Account, Life Insurance and Disability, Tuition Reimbursement, Voluntary Benefits, Paid Absences, and more. About Us: At New Energy Equity, a proud subsidiary of ALLETE, we’re leading the charge in transforming the energy landscape with innovative solar solutions  . As a top player in the renewable energy sector, we’ve successfully developed over 600MW of solar projects and closed more than $1.2 billion in clean energy investments  . Our projects deliver sustainable electricity to a wide range of clients, including commercial, industrial, municipal, and utility customers  . But there’s more to us than just impressive numbers.
