title: Electrical Estimator
description: Job Summary Sun Tribe EPC (“Sun Tribe”) is Virginia’s premier utility-scale solar design and build firm, specializing in sub-20MW ground-mounted solar photovoltaic (PV) facilities. Our construction efforts are focused throughout the Commonwealth of Virginia, Maryland, and neighboring states. At Sun Tribe, we build with purpose - prioritizing safety, quality, and environmental stewardship in every project we deliver. Sun Tribe EPC’s Preconstruction Team’s mission is to develop quality business opportunities that enable efficient delivery in a predictable manner. The Electrical Estimator plays an important role in that mission by developing accurate and competitive electrical and mechanical project estimates for small utility-scale solar and battery energy storage projects. The Electrical Estimator independently manages the non-civil estimating scope for assigned opportunities, working closely with Civil Estimating, Project Engineering, Supply Chain, subcontractors, project owners, and developers. This role develops project estimates, evaluates subcontractor and vendor pricing, identifies scope and cost risks and opportunities, and supports projects from early-stage estimating through award, project budgeting, and deliberate handoff to Project Management. This position reports directly to the VP of Preconstruction and serves as the electrical estimating subject matter expert for Preconstruction and cross-functional project teams. Principal Responsibilities Owns the development and completion of project-level internal estimates (“Cost Stacks”), excluding civil site work developed by the Civil Estimator. Performs detailed quantity takeoffs for DC and AC electrical systems from back of module to point of interconnection for solar and battery energy storage projects. Develops detailed electrical cost estimates, budgets, and proposals based on quantity takeoffs and vendor and subcontractor pricing. Analyzes electrical drawings, specifications, owner requirements, and other project documentation to determine scope, schedule, quantities, risks, and opportunities. Analyzes labor, material, and equipment costs to develop accurate and competitive bids. Coordinates with Supply Chain and Engineering to obtain equipment, material, engineering, and other applicable project pricing and scope information. Creates comprehensive RFPs and leads bid clarification and scope review discussions with electrical and mechanical subcontractors. Reviews and levels subcontractor proposals to identify scope gaps, qualifications, exclusions, risks, and pricing differences. Develops project-specific inclusions, exclusions, and clarifications for electrical and mechanical scopes that align with client requirements and project objectives. Develops independent, stand-alone electrical estimates for assigned bids to evaluate subcontractor pricing. Collaborates with Project Management and Supply Chain to ensure estimates, RFPs, subcontractor proposals, and supporting documentation are completed in accordance with bid schedules. Supports development and maintenance of a qualified electrical and mechanical subcontractor network to promote a healthy and competitive bidding environment. Converts bid estimates into project budgets following project award and provides estimating support for change orders and RFIs as needed. Supports deliberate project handoff from Preconstruction to Project Management by communicating estimate assumptions, scope, pricing, inclusions and exclusions, risks, opportunities, and relevant bid history. Compares actual project costs to estimates and incorporates lessons learned into future estimating practices. Contributes to continuous improvement of estimating tools, templates, historical pricing data, SOPs, and processes. Basic Qualifications Required High school diploma or GED required; bachelor’s degree in an engineering discipline preferred, or equivalent relevant engineering, design, or construction experience. Minimum two (2) years of electrical estimating experience required. Strong Microsoft Excel skills required. Strong understanding of electrical engineering drawings, design documents, specifications, and construction methodologies. Ability to manage multiple estimates, priorities, and bid deadlines simultaneously. Skills & Experience Preferred Experience performing electrical quantity takeoffs and developing construction cost estimates. Experience estimating medium-voltage interconnected solar facilities. Experience with electrical estimating software such as Trimble Accubid, McCormick, ConEst IntelliBid, PlanSwift, or similar. Experience with Procore or other construction management software. Experience with scheduling software such as MS Project. Experience using AI tools to support estimating, analysis, or process efficiency. Excellent organizational, analytical, and problem-solving skills with a high degree of attention to detail. Strong written and verbal communication and negotiation skills, with the ability to effectively collaborate with subcontractors, vendors, and cross-functional internal teams. Alignment with Sun Tribe's core values: Community, Safety, Perpetual Improvement, Nature, Joy, and Respect. Commitment to a culture of safety, accountability, and high-quality project delivery. Working Conditions and Physical Requirements Hybrid work environment, with work performed remotely and from Sun Tribe’s Charlottesville office based on business needs. Ability to travel to the Charlottesville office, project sites, and other business locations as needed, typically averaging one to two trips per month. Occasional overnight travel may be required. Some evening and weekend work may be required based on bid deadlines and business needs. Ability to perform work in a general office and hybrid work environment. Exposure to typical construction site conditions and hazards during project site visits. Required to wear appropriate personal protective equipment (PPE) while on project sites. Compensation and Benefits Compensation for this position will be determined based on experience, qualifications, geographic location, and internal equity. This position is eligible for Sun Tribe’s comprehensive benefits package, which includes medical, dental, and vision insurance, 401(k) with company match, life and disability insurance, paid time off, volunteer days, and access to an employee assistance program. description: Skilled field technician responsible for operations and maintenance of utility-scale Battery Energy Storage System (BESS) equipment and associated balance-of-plant. Works under general supervision to independently perform preventive maintenance and routine corrective maintenance, diagnose and repair common faults across electrical, controls, communications, and balance-of-plant systems within assigned scope, and maintain complete service and CMMS documentation. May perform switching when individually qualified and authorized under the site switching program and may provide informal guidance to entry-level technicians. Essential Duties and Responsibilities: • Ensure strict adherence to all safety standards, including OSHA, NFPA 70E principles (as applicable), state and local regulations, and company safety policies. Promote and support a strong safety culture, including hazard recognition, quality job briefings, stop-work authority, and safe work practices. Identify, escalate, and support resolution of electrical and operational safety hazards. • Ensure consistent application of Lockout/Tagout (LOTO), energized-work controls, and PPE requirements across assigned work scopes, performed independently as a qualified person within the limits of training and authorization. • Independently execute scheduled and unscheduled preventive and corrective maintenance on BESS equipment and balance-of-plant within assigned scope, including PCS/inverter interfaces, battery racks/enclosures, HVAC/auxiliary systems, transformers (as applicable), switchgear, and related controls. • Diagnose and troubleshoot routine electrical, controls, and communications/SCADA faults using monitoring tools, OEM diagnostic utilities, and PLC/controls interfaces where applicable; verify repairs and return equipment to service safely within scope. • Perform medium-/high-voltage switching only when individually qualified and authorized under Strata’s substation switching program, within the limits of that authorization; otherwise support switching and isolation under the direction of authorized personnel. • Interpret electrical schematics, single-line diagrams, wiring diagrams, and OEM manuals to support troubleshooting, maintenance, and safe work planning. • Use the full complement of electrical test equipment and field tools (multimeters, insulation testers, low-resistance ohmmeters as applicable, IR thermometer/camera) to diagnose issues and verify repairs. • Support monitoring and communications tasks, including alarm/event review, data extraction, basic network troubleshooting, and coordination with the Remote Operations/Monitoring team. • Coordinate with the Site Supervisor and vendor/OEM personnel for planned service activities; support safe execution and capture closeout documentation (photos, test records, service reports, as-left condition). • Maintain accurate, timely, and complete records in the CMMS, including work orders, maintenance reports, and inspection/test results. • Provide informal task guidance to entry-level (Level I) technicians as assigned. • Support emergency response activities and Emergency Action Plan execution. Maintain site readiness and housekeeping. Other duties as assigned. Environmental Responsibilities: • Participate in environmental compliance programs, inspections, and administrative recordkeeping. • Support and maintaining compliance with Resource Conservation and Recovery Act (RCRA) and Department of Transportation (DOT) regulations. • Assist with environmental incident response and mitigation activities as required. Education and/or Work Experience Requirements: • High School Diploma, GED, or equivalent. • Two (2) to four (4) years of experience in utility-scale PV, BESS sites (balance-of-plant/controls/communications), substations, or equivalent industrial electrical/power systems with directly transferable skills. • Strong knowledge of OSHA requirements, NFPA 70E principles, NESC awareness, and MV safety practices applicable to the work scope. • Valid driver’s license. • Working knowledge of AC/DC electrical theory, three-phase power systems, and energy storage system fundamentals appropriate to the role. • Ability to read and understand electrical drawings/schematics and OEM manuals. • Proficiency with test equipment and tools used in electrical maintenance (multimeters, insulation testers, IR camera/thermography tools, etc.). • Proficiency with CMMS platforms, maintenance reporting tools, and ability to learn additional software/platforms as required. • Strong communication and interpersonal skills; ability to coordinate with technicians, supervisors, vendors, subcontractors, and support teams. Physical Requirements/Work Environment: • Must be able to work in an outdoor environment for extended periods of time. • Must have the ability to travel for extended duration to remote project sites. • Must be able to stoop, kneel or bend. • Must be able to lift, push or pull 50 lbs. overhead repeatedly. • 20/40 vision in each eye, with or without correction and ability to distinguish colors. • Ability to wear full complement of Personal Protective Equipment (PPE • Must have the ability to travel, work on-call during off-shift hours and weekends. description: Job Description: Application Engineer — Solar Inverter and PCS Location: Mesa, Arizona / Remote or Hybrid as required Function: Applications Engineering / Technical Sales Support Category: S&M Employment Type: Full-time Position Summary We are seeking an Application Engineer to support the solar inverter and PCS business as part of Nextpower’s growing power conversion portfolio. This role will provide technical support for customer applications, proposals, product selection, system integration, project requirements, and field deployment of inverter and power conversion systems. The Application Engineer will work closely with Sales, Technical Sales, Product Management, Engineering, Service, Quality, Manufacturing, and customers to ensure power conversion products are properly applied in solar, energy storage, and grid-connected power conversion projects. This role requires strong technical understanding of inverters, PCS platforms, electrical systems, system-level design, and customer project requirements. Support Sales and Technical Sales teams during customer engagements, project development, RFP/RFQ responses, and technical proposal preparation. Maintain strong knowledge of competitive products, market requirements, codes, standards, and application trends in solar and energy storage. Help develop standard tools, templates, calculators, and documentation to improve application engineering efficiency. Required Qualifications Bachelor’s degree in Electrical Engineering, Power Electronics, Energy Systems, or a related technical field; Master’s degree is a bonus. 3 years of experience in applications engineering, utility-scale renewable/BESS project engineering, product/R&D engineering, systems engineering, field engineering, or technical support. Experience with solar inverters, PCS, battery energy storage systems, power electronics, electrical equipment, or grid-connected energy systems. Strong understanding of electrical systems, AC/DC power conversion, system ratings, single-line diagrams, technical specifications, and customer project requirements. Ability to read and interpret technical drawings, product datasheets, electrical schematics, project specifications, and compliance documents. Strong communication skills with the ability to explain technical concepts clearly to customers and internal stakeholders. Ability to work cross-functionally with sales, engineering, product, manufacturing, quality, service, and operations teams. Strong problem-solving skills and ability to manage multiple customer and project priorities. Proficiency with Microsoft Office, technical documentation tools, and engineering analysis or design tools as applicable. Willingness to travel occasionally for customer meetings, site visits, factory visits, and industry events. Preferred Qualifications Experience with utility-scale solar and battery energy storage, grid-tied inverter systems, or PCS platforms. Familiarity with UL, IEEE, NEC, NEMA, grid interconnection, and utility-scale project designs. Experience supporting RFP/RFQ responses, technical compliance matrices, project submittals, and customer qualification processes. Knowledge of inverter controls, communications protocols, SCADA integration, protection schemes, and grid support functions. Experience working with EPCs, developers, utilities, system integrators, or energy storage solution providers. Experience with new product introduction, product launch, or post-acquisition business integration is a plus. This person should be comfortable reviewing specifications, supporting customer discussions, solving technical application problems, and working across multiple internal teams. The successful candidate will bring a practical engineering mindset, strong ownership, and clear communication skills to help customers successfully apply power conversion products in solar and energy storage projects. The Construction Project Manager will undertake detailed site assessments, prepare, negotiate and manage project contracts, facilitate full compliance with all permits and utility requirements, and ensure that the projects are constructed, commissioned and tested in full accordance with Soltage standards and specifications. Manage projects from initiation through to operation, completion. Hand-over the completed and fully-documented projects to the Asset Management and Operations teams. Manage and ensure quality-assurances practices are upheld, either directly or through contracted Owner’s Representatives. Review and evaluate electrical, mechanical, civil and structural designs, reports, calculations and surveys. Review and evaluate environmental and land-use permits, surveys and reports. Prepare and manage project budgets and schedules. Provide concise summary reports and status updates to the Soltage management team and board members. Experience and Education Requirements: BA/BS college or university degree in an engineering discipline, preferably electrical or mechanical. NABCEP or similar solar PV certification is desirable although not required. Minimum six years’ relevant project execution experience, with at least four years of commercial or utility-scale solar PV or BESS project management experience. At least two years of commercial/industrial battery energy storage experience preferred. Budget responsibility of at least $5MM. Detailed understanding of three-phase electrical systems and the National Electrical Code. Knowledge and experience of medium-voltage electrical systems and equipment preferred. Knowledge and experience of environmental and land-use permits, restrictions and regulations. Ability to negotiate engineering, procurement, and construction bids and contracts. Excellent written and verbal communication skills. Microsoft Word, Excel, Outlook, Powerpoint and Project. AutoCAD experience is a plus. Ability to travel as needed. Ability to climb ladders and work on rooftops as needed. Own an unexpired driving license with a clean driving record. Comfortable working in a fast-paced, entrepreneurial environment. Excellent written and verbal communication skills. Microsoft Word, Excel, Outlook, Powerpoint and Project. AutoCAD experience is a plus. Location: This is a hybrid position which will be staffed out of Soltage’s headquarters in Jersey City, New Jersey. title: Former Solar Installer – Transition to Historic Preservation Trades
description: Solar gave you skills. We'll give you a career. The solar industry has left a lot of talented, skilled workers in a difficult position. At Renaissance Historic Exteriors, we see something others miss: solar installers are uniquely prepared for historic restoration trades work. You're height-comfortable. You're safety-minded. You understand roof systems, tools, and the discipline of precise, consequence-heavy installation work. We'll take those skills and build on them. You'll train alongside master craftsmen in slate, tile, copper, and historic preservation techniques — earning while you learn, in a trade with genuine long-term career depth. Historic restoration specialists are rare and in demand nationally. This is not a lateral move — it's an upgrade. WHY YOUR SOLAR BACKGROUND IS AN ASSET: Comfort and competence at heights, on pitched surfaces, with fall-protection systems. Experience with roof structure, weather sealing, and precision layout. Safety culture and situational awareness that general laborers often lack. Mechanical aptitude and a trained eye for system-level thinking. Work ethic developed in a results-oriented, high-accountability environment. WHAT YOU'LL LEARN & DO: Historic roofing restoration with natural slate, clay tile, and architectural copper. Flashing, waterproofing, and steep-slope techniques specific to landmark structures. Hands-on work on State Capitols, churches, universities, and National Register properties. Progression through our apprenticeship structure into a fully specialized historic tradesperson role. WHAT WE OFFER: $25–$40/hr — starting rate reflects your transferable skills, not a fresh-start penalty. Group Health, Dental & Vision Insurance after 90 days. Formal apprenticeship track with advancement milestones and pay increases. Year-round work with a company that has grown continuously since 1992. Travel per diem for Midwest project assignments.

We are looking for talented self-starters with imagination, creativity and vision. We are a rapidly-growing developer of large solar, wind and energy storage projects serving corporate and utility energy purchasers. We design, build, finance, own and operate projects across the US, Mexico and Asia. Headquartered in San Francisco, Ecoplexus has grown at an annual rate of over 50% per year since its founding in 2009. The Company has developed, built, and operates over 80 projects in the U.S. and Japan, and has a substantial development pipeline of solar, wind and energy storage assets in North America and Asia. We are seeking a talented self-starter, who is highly motivated and capable of assuming increasing responsibility in a dynamic growth environment. POSITION Manage the day-to-day development tasks for a set of large, complex renewable energy projects throughout their lifecycle, from inception up to construction. Supervise, coordinate and review the work of multiple development functions, consultants, technicians and others and be accountable for execution on complex, multi-disciplinary projects in the Central U.S. region (focusing on ERCOT, MISO, and SPP market areas) with remote, distributed teams. This position will work closely with interconnection, permitting, real estate, GIS, finance, origination, and engineering teams to achieve project and company goals. The position reports to the SVP of US Development & Origination. Duties and responsibilities include: • Deliver development projects on time and on budget. • Coordinate the broader development team in achieving objectives for individual projects and project portfolios. • Provide input to and support quarterly and annual regional development objectives and budget planning. • Create and implement development strategies for solar, wind, and storage projects. • Estimate staffing needs and schedules and assign work to meet completion date. • Track project risk throughout the development cycle, provide risk assessments and mitigations. Participate in the development of key account and utility relationships, support origination of contracts with such key accounts. • Develop proposal strategies for RFPs or similar processes and help coordinate bid responses. Develop/maintain business relationships with key consultants and vendors, and negotiate terms for vendors and consultants who participate in the development process. • Research and stay informed of critical client and industry policies, regulations, and issues. • Manage a Development Associate assigned to the region. • Help create Ecoplexus project development framework best practices and conduct internal training. QUALIFICATIONS 3 years of experience and a strong record of accomplishment in relevant roles Renewable energy, power industry, or project management experience required. Project Development experience preferred Skilled at organization and problem solving throughout the development lifecycle. Strong project, process and organizational skills including creating and managing project budgets and schedules. Ability to work effectively with and manage cross-functional teams. Ability to manage and support multiple projects simultaneously, with varying complexities and urgencies presented day to day. Excellent written and verbal communication skills. Bachelor's Degree required; master's degree preferred. Experience working in MS Office Suite (Office, Excel, and Powerpoint) and Google Cloud Applications (Google Docs, Sheets, Presentations). WORK ENVIRONMENT The duties and responsibilities are generally performed in an office environment. Conditions may also include extended periods of travel by automobile and/or airplane transport. May require an irregular work schedule and overtime hours. Occasional to frequent project site visits required which could be in a variety of settings (i.e., proposed pro ject sites, and offices). title: Electrical Estimator - Utility Scale Solar - Remote - Eastern / Central Time Zone
description: Paige Renewable Energy , a GCG company, is seeking an experienced Electrical Estimator to join our growing Paige Energy team and support utility-scale renewable energy projects across North America! As our Electrical Estimator, you’ll translate customer drawings, specifications, bills of material, and project requirements into accurate, executable estimates. You’ll perform detailed material takeoffs, develop project pricing, identify scope or design issues, and work closely with Sales, Engineering, Project Management, Supply Chain, and manufacturing partners to help ensure projects are positioned for successful execution. This is a strong opportunity for someone who combines practical electrical knowledge with exceptional attention to detail and ownership. You should be comfortable working through large, complex project packages, asking thoughtful technical questions, challenging assumptions when something does not look right, and taking responsibility for the accuracy and completeness of your work. While this role offers a remote work environment, we are seeking candidates in either the Eastern or Central Time Zone to align with the work schedule of the existing team. What You’ll Do Review RFQ packages, electrical drawings, site layouts, single-line diagrams, specifications, bills of material, and related documentation to understand project scope and requirements. Perform detailed electrical material takeoffs, including cable lengths, harness and string counts, connectors, assemblies, accessories, and other project-specific materials. Develop project estimates incorporating material costs, vendor pricing, freight, manufacturing costs, customer requirements, and other project-specific considerations. Identify drawing discrepancies, missing information, scope gaps, incompatible materials, and other potential risks while clearly documenting assumptions, exclusions, and required clarifications. Validate critical quantities, material selections, calculations, and drawing revisions before estimates are released. Coordinate with Supply Chain and manufacturing partners to obtain and validate supplier pricing, lead times, freight requirements, and other cost inputs. Support proposal development, design revisions, value-engineering opportunities, Best and Final Offer (BAFO) activities, and estimate revisions throughout the sales process. Evaluate changes between estimate revisions and clearly communicate impacts to quantities, scope, cost, materials, and project requirements. Maintain organized, traceable estimating files and supporting documentation that allow estimates to be independently reviewed. Participate in project award and handoff activities, confirming that final estimates, quantities, assumptions, pricing, and scope align with the awarded project and customer purchase order. Support estimating needs related to project changes, additional material requests, spare parts, and change orders. Help improve estimating templates, tools, checklists, standards, and review processes by incorporating lessons learned from awarded and completed projects. What You’ll Bring Required Qualifications 3 years of electrical estimating experience, or equivalent electrical construction or design experience that includes estimating and material takeoff responsibilities. Demonstrated ability to read and interpret electrical drawings, single-line diagrams, site plans, specifications, and bills of material. Experience performing detailed material takeoffs and developing project estimates. Strong understanding of electrical materials, cable, conductors, connectors, and electrical distribution systems. Strong mathematical and analytical skills with a high level of accuracy and attention to detail. Proficiency with Microsoft Excel and experience using Bluebeam or similar takeoff and document-review software. Strong organizational, communication, and collaboration skills with the ability to manage multiple complex estimates at different stages of development. Preferred Qualifications Experience with renewable energy, utility-scale solar, EPC organizations, electrical contracting, or industrial electrical projects. Proficiency with AutoCAD. Working knowledge of the National Electrical Code (NEC). Education in Electrical Engineering, Electrical Technology, Construction Management, or a related technical discipline; equivalent relevant industry experience will also be considered. What Success Looks Like Success in this role means producing estimates that are accurate, complete, timely, and traceable . You’ll take ownership of your work, identify inconsistencies and risks before they become costly problems, clearly communicate assumptions and technical concerns, and help projects transition smoothly from opportunity through award and execution. You’ll also contribute to improving the tools and processes the Paige Energy team uses to make estimating increasingly efficient and reliable. What We Offer Competitive base salary ranging from $80,000 to $90,000 plus annual bonus based on company and individual performance Comprehensive Health Coverage : Multiple medical plan options (CDHP and PPO) to get you the coverage you need Robust Financial Security : Company-paid life and disability insurance, 401(k) with company match, plus options for supplemental critical illness, accident, and hospital indemnity plans Generous Time Off : PTO plan with paid holidays, paid parental leave, and paid compassionate care leave to support personal well-being and family needs Wellness & Support Programs : Employee Assistance Program (EAP), wellness incentives, and telehealth access Extras That Matter : Dental and vision plans, FSAs/HSAs with company contributions, pet insurance, legal services, and ID theft protection for peace of mind An employee-centric company that values and truly appreciates our most important asset: You! Serving industries including renewable energy, data communications, industrial applications, irrigation, and more, we are committed to engineering excellence, customer-driven innovation, and high-quality products that help businesses solve complex challenges with tailored solutions. Built on a foundation of expertise, flexibility, and humility, we are dedicated to solving customer challenges, adapting to their needs, and continuously improving. At Paige, we remove ego from the equation, fostering a collaborative, customer-focused culture that drives long-term growth, innovation, and enduring partnerships. With the responsive DNA of a startup and the size of a global leader, we offer top brands and extensive value-added services that make us an invaluable partner to our customers in multiple industry verticals across the globe. As our Electrical Estimator, you'll translate customer drawings, specifications, bills of material, and project requirements into accurate, executable estimates. You'll perform detailed material takeoffs, develop project pricing, identify scope or design issues, and work closely with Sales, Engineering, Project Management, Supply Chain, and manufacturing partners to help ensure projects are positioned for successful execution. This is a strong opportunity for someone who combines practical electrical knowledge with exceptional attention to detail and ownership. You should be comfortable working through large, complex project packages, asking thoughtful technical questions, challenging assumptions when something does not look right, and taking responsibility for the accuracy and completeness of your work. While this role offers a remote work environment, we are seeking candidates in either the Eastern or Central Time Zone to align with the work schedule of the existing team. What You'll Do  Review RFQ packages, electrical drawings, site layouts, single-line diagrams, specifications, bills of material, and related documentation to understand project scope and requirements.  Perform detailed electrical material takeoffs, including cable lengths, harness and string counts, connectors, assemblies, accessories, and other project-specific materials.  Develop project estimates incorporating material costs, vendor pricing, freight, manufacturing costs, customer requirements, and other project-specific considerations.  Identify drawing discrepancies, missing information, scope gaps, incompatible materials, and other potential risks while clearly documenting assumptions, exclusions, and required clarifications.  Validate critical quantities, material selections, calculations, and drawing revisions before estimates are released.  Coordinate with Supply Chain and manufacturing partners to obtain and validate supplier pricing, lead times, freight requirements, and other cost inputs.  Support proposal development, design revisions, value-engineering opportunities, Best and Final Offer (BAFO) activities, and estimate revisions throughout the sales process.  Evaluate changes between estimate revisions and clearly communicate impacts to quantities, scope, cost, materials, and project requirements.  Maintain organized, traceable estimating files and supporting documentation that allow estimates to be independently reviewed.  Participate in project award and handoff activities, confirming that final estimates, quantities, assumptions, pricing, and scope align with the awarded project and customer purchase order.  Support estimating needs related to project changes, additional material requests, spare parts, and change orders.  Help improve estimating templates, tools, checklists, standards, and review processes by incorporating lessons learned from awarded and completed projects. What You'll Bring Required Qualifications  3 years of electrical estimating experience, or equivalent electrical construction or design experience that includes estimating and material takeoff responsibilities.  Demonstrated ability to read and interpret electrical drawings, single-line diagrams, site plans, specifications, and bills of material.  Experience performing detailed material takeoffs and developing project estimates.  Strong understanding of electrical materials, cable, conductors, connectors, and electrical distribution systems.  Strong mathematical and analytical skills with a high level of accuracy and attention to detail.  Proficiency with Microsoft Excel and experience using Bluebeam or similar takeoff and document-review software.  Strong organizational, communication, and collaboration skills with the ability to manage multiple complex estimates at different stages of development. Preferred Qualifications  Experience with renewable energy, utility-scale solar, EPC organizations, electrical contracting, or industrial electrical projects.  Proficiency with AutoCAD.  Working knowledge of the National Electrical Code (NEC).  Education in Electrical Engineering, Electrical Technology, Construction Management, or a related technical discipline; equivalent relevant industry experience will also be considered. What Success Looks Like Success in this role means producing estimates that are accurate, complete, timely, and traceable . You'll take ownership of your work, identify inconsistencies and risks before they become costly problems, clearly communicate assumptions and technical concerns, and help projects transition smoothly from opportunity through award and execution. You'll also contribute to improving the tools and processes the Paige Energy team uses to make estimating increasingly efficient and reliable. What We Offer  Competitive base salary ranging from $80,000 to $90,000 plus annual bonus based on company and individual performance  Comprehensive Health Coverage : Multiple medical plan options (CDHP and PPO) to get you the coverage you need  Robust Financial Security : Company-paid life and disability insurance, 401(k) with company match, plus options for supplemental critical illness, accident, and hospital indemnity plans  Generous Time Off : PTO plan with paid holidays, paid parental leave, and paid compassionate care leave to support personal well-being and family needs  Wellness & Support Programs : Employee Assistance Program (EAP), wellness incentives, and telehealth access  Extras That Matter : Dental and vision plans, FSAs/HSAs with company contributions, pet insurance, legal services, and ID theft protection for peace of mind  An employee-centric company that values and truly appreciates our most important asset: You! title: Entry-Level Sales Representative
description: Entry-Level Sales Representative Solar Energy Consultant Full-time (In-person) | High Commission  Weekly Bonuses | Gas Reimbursement About Suntech Solar At Suntech Solar, we are on a mission to revolutionize how our communities power their homes. We believe that clean, renewable energy should be accessible, affordable, and easy to understand. By helping homeowners transition to solar power, we don't just help them lower their utility bills—we help them take control of their energy independence while making a massive positive impact on the environment. We are a fast-growing, high-energy solar provider built on the core values of integrity, relentless drive, and absolute customer transparency. We provide the platform, the training, and the top-tier products; you provide the hustle. Position Overview The solar industry is booming, and homeowners are looking for immediate relief from skyrocketing utility rates. To meet this massive demand, we are looking for hungry, resilient, and highly motivated D2D Sales Representatives to join our elite field team. In this role, you are the tip of the spear. You will be canvassing targeted, pre-qualified neighborhoods, knocking on doors, and initiating the conversation about solar energy. You will educate homeowners on government incentives, zero-down financing options, and the long-term savings of going solar. This is a gritty, boots-on-the-ground, field-based sales role tailored for high-achievers who want to write their own paychecks and refuse to be capped by a traditional salary. Whether you are a seasoned D2D veteran or a highly driven individual looking to break into the lucrative solar market, we offer an industry-leading training program that will give you the blueprint for a six-figure income. What You’ll Do Canvass Targeted Territories: Actively knock doors in strategically assigned, high-potential neighborhoods to generate leads and initiate energy consultations. Prequalify Homeowners: Review current utility bills, assess roof viability, and determine if the home is a strong candidate for a solar installation. Educate & Overcome Objections: Clearly explain the financial and environmental benefits of solar energy, seamlessly navigating homeowner skepticism and objections at the door. Set & Close Appointments: Secure dedicated sit-down appointments for comprehensive solar proposals, and guide the homeowner through the contract signing process. Pipeline Management: Utilize our CRM to track leads, schedule follow-ups, and manage your sales pipeline from the first knock to the final installation. Compensation & Benefits Aggressive Commission Structure: We offer one of the most competitive, transparent commission models in the solar industry. Massive Income Potential: Average first-year earnings range from $75,000 to $90,000, with top D2D performers consistently clearing $150,000 annually. Performance Incentives: Weekly cash spiffs, monthly bonuses, and annual company trips for top-tier closers. Schedule Flexibility: Control your own hours—work when the homeowners are available and optimize your time for maximum earning potential. Career Advancement: Clear pathways to Team Lead and Regional Management roles for proven producers. What We’re Looking For Unmatched Grit & Resilience: Door-to-door sales is not for the faint of heart. You must possess the mental toughness to handle rejection and keep a positive, high-energy attitude at the next door. Communication Skills: Exceptional ability to build immediate rapport, speak clearly, and simplify complex concepts (like tax credits and energy offsets) for everyday homeowners. Self-Driven: You don't need a manager looking over your shoulder to get out in the field. You are strictly motivated by your goals and your income. Physical Stamina: The willingness and physical ability to walk neighborhoods, work outdoors, and stay on your feet in varying weather conditions. Experience: Previous D2D canvassing, alarms, pest control, or solar experience is highly preferred, but we will train individuals with the right drive and raw talent. Why Join Suntech Solar? Future-Proof Industry: Solar is one of the fastest-growing sectors in the world. You are selling a product that literally pays for itself. World-Class Training: Comprehensive onboarding covering solar technology, pitch psychology, objection handling, and closing techniques. Winning Culture: Join a locker-room environment of winners who celebrate success, share best practices, and push each other to elevate their game. Application Questions Do you have previous experience in Door-to-Door (D2D) or direct-to-consumer outside sales? Are you entirely comfortable working outdoors and walking neighborhoods for extended periods? How do you handle rejection, and what keeps you motivated when people tell you "no"? Are you financially prepared and motivated to work a high-yield, commission-driven structure? Work Location: In person / Field-based License/Certification: Valid Driver’s License and reliable transportation (Required) Apply Today If you are ready to stop trading your time for a capped hourly wage and want to build a highly lucrative career in renewable energy, apply today and let’s get to work!

title: Advanced Solar Field Service Technician (Operations and Maintenance)
description: At PEARCE , we've got a career for you! Pearce is a leading technology-enabled provider of asset management solutions for mission-critical electromechanical infrastructure throughout North America. Pearce provides technical maintenance, repair, operations, and engineering services for uninterruptible power supply (UPS) systems, backup power generators, battery energy storage systems (BESS), critical cooling systems, and other electrical and mechanical infrastructure across end markets such as renewable energy, telecom, and data centers. Founded in 1998, Pearce has more than 4,000 employees and 28 locations across the U.S. Pearce is a wholly owned subsidiary of CBRE Group, Inc., the world’s largest commercial real estate services and investment firm. To learn more about Pearce visit http://www.pearce-services.com . Your Impact The Advanced Solar Field Service Technician (Operations and Maintenance) in the PEARCE Renewables Solar Operations and Maintenance Division performs tasks involving physical labor at solar energy sites near New Brunswick, New Jersey. The Solar Field Service Technician is responsible for the operation and maintenance (O&M) of solar power plants in accordance with established preventative and corrective maintenance standards while always maintaining safety and professionalism. These are local sites-candidates should reside within 50 miles of the New Brunswick, New Jersey areas. Core Responsibilities Conduct preventative and corrective maintenance of Solar Utility and Sub-Station equipment. Responsible for documentation including, but not limited to, work orders, time logs, inventory control, and emergency information schedules. Provide a working knowledge of troubleshooting electrical components with help and use of digital multi-meters, meggers, amp clamps, and similar equipment. Testing/troubleshooting installed solar equipment and ensuring proper working order. Must have a strong safety background with experience in Lock Out Tag Out (LOTO) and Job Hazard Analysis (JHA). Able work in a solo as well as a group environment. Operate and maintain a motor vehicle safely and legally per the PEARCE Renewables Employee Handbook and insurance requirements. Specific duties may vary or evolve over time based on business and client needs. Core Experience 2 years’ experience in Commercial/Industrial operations and maintenance (O&M) on solar power plants is preferred. Preventative Maintenance experience on Solar Utility equipment is preferred. Candidates should possess strong mechanical and electrical experience with troubleshooting and installation skills. Specific solar experience with Inverters, Tracker Systems, or Sub-Stations Equipment (TMEIC/SMA/Sungrow/Nextracker/ATI, etc.) is preferred. Takes initiative to escalate issues at site. Ability to train, mentor, and develop laborers into Apprentices. High aptitude and a strong work ethic are a must. Physical/Work Environment At Pearce safety is our number one concern. Candidates must be able to comply with OSHA Standards. Must live within approximately 50 miles of the New Brunswick, New Jersey areas. Be exposed to ambient temperatures while working outdoors. Lift and move equipment as needed (up to 50 pounds). Employment may require working on weekends and holidays, including an "on call" service availability via telephone/text message. Travel requirements dependent on support of the company (up to 25% travel). Compensation: $30.00-$42.00 hourly/DOE At Pearce, we are committed to fair and transparent pay practices. Actual compensation is influenced by a wide array of factors including but not limited to skill set, level of experience, and location. In addition to wages, employees may also be eligible for performance and referral bonuses, production incentives, tool/equipment and fuel stipends, company vehicle, per diem or other applicable compensation. We also offer all full-time employees a comprehensive benefits package including health and life insurance, 401k with employer match, paid time off, tuition reimbursement, and professional development courses. This pay range reflects our commitment to pay equity and compliance with state and federal pay transparency laws. If you have questions about compensation, we encourage open discussions during the hiring process. Base Pay Range $30 - $42 USD What We Offer Pearce offers a family-friendly and innovative culture with opportunities for growth, competitive compensation, comprehensive health benefits including medical, dental and vision insurance, flexible spending accounts, HSA option. To help you recharge, we have paid vacation and paid holidays. For your future, we offer a company-matching 401(k) Retirement, Life Insurance, Tuition reimbursement, and professional development training. To help you be successful at work, as required for the role, we will provide a company vehicle, phone, laptop, or tablet along with all necessary tools and safety equipment. title: Solar Crew Supervisor
description: Full-time Description OUR PURPOSE SunCommon believes business should create positive change and help solve the world’s biggest problems. Our mission is to accelerate the transition to solar power in our communities because ensuring a habitable planet is the most important work of our lifetimes. ABOUT THE BUSINESS SunCommon is a market leading renewable energy company operating in Vermont and New York’s Hudson Valley and Capital District. We use an innovative approach to marketing, via high-touch, personal interactions with home and business owners who want clean electricity and more energy security. We’ve done all the legwork to put together a total package that’s easy for the customer. We picked the best equipment manufacturers, arranged attractive financing that saves our customers real money and hired up the finest installers. There’s over 8,000 happy SunCommon residential and commercial customers so far — and lots more to come. Organized as a Benefit Corporation and certified as a BCorp, we’re committed to the triple bottom line of People, Planet and Profit. Our goal is to become the largest publicly traded, BCorp in the country producing renewable energy. ABOUT THIS POSITION Reporting to the Vice President of Operations, SunCommon’s Install Crew Supervisor is responsible for reviewing plan sets, assisting in job planning, driving job site efficiencies, training new staff and new products, and ensuring safe and successful PV installations. This is a field/office hybrid position with a majority of the time based in the field on active and inactive construction sites. Strong communications skills are essential for this role. The InstallCrew Supervisor is responsible for communicating job highlights and areas of focus to Crew Leads, reporting crew efficiency highlights and shortfalls to the VP of Ops, and providing appropriate feedback to other operations managers to build towards a more efficient process. Safety - for our team, our customers, and their property - is our highest priority. The Install Crew Supervisor is expected to follow all safety protocols and keep up with advancements in PV and other relevant technologies. In depth knowledge of PV and electrical installation and design are a must for this role. The Install Crew Supervisor will spend the majority of their time working on-site with the installation crews but may work independently to gather vital information from the Design Team, Electrical Program Manager, Commercial Program Manager, Project Management Team and other support staff. The Install Crew Supervisor will be a go-to source for Installation Teams for on site troubleshooting, and any field obstacle that affects an installation's efficiencies. Significant driving across the state is part of the job, and a dedication to taking the best possible care of our customers and your colleagues is essential. ESSENTIAL JOB FUNCTIONS Reporting to the Vice President of Operations and collaborating closely with members of the Installation Team, specific responsibilities of the Install Crew Supervisor include but are not limited to: Field Leadership & Site Execution Work with staff to complete PV installations in a safe and efficient manner, ensuring the highest standards of quality and efficiency. Provide on-site leadership for installers and coordinate installation flow, including setting clear install benchmarks and goals with Crew Leads on larger Commercial projects. Support installations through direct on-the-ground work. Fill in as Crew Lead and/or Residential Electrician as needed. Identify potential issues or blockers in advance of installation, and work to find solutions before we roll trucks to the jobsite. Perform site evaluations to gather data for engineering and pre-construction walkthroughs and rough-ins on new construction, commercial, and residential PV installation sites. Provide support for PV installations and perform O&M work on commercial and residential PV systems as necessary. Ensure all project close-out documentation including photos, as-builts, performance testing, and final approved permits has been received and saved in appropriate databases. Team Management & HR Administration Lead personnel development for the installation team by assisting with candidate interviews and training new crew members. Conduct regular check-ins and formal performance evaluations, and actively support installers in advancing through the internal Install Certification Tiers. Help roll out field-based training and relay potential training opportunities to other Ops Managers and Leadership. Support the VP of Operations in essential HR administration for field staff, including holding staff accountable for timely and correct timesheets, coordinating PTO requests, and assisting with commercial bonus calculations. Quality, Safety & Fleet Logistics Ensure that PV systems are installed in accordance with NEC and SunCommon standards using design drawings, schematics, and instructions. Keep up-to-date with current code and solar installation techniques, and apply new knowledge to the job. Maintain strict compliance with all relevant safety standards and participate in Quality Audit meetings. Monitor daily weather forecasts, collaborating with Ops Leadership, and help make judgment calls for work delays or cancellations related to safety. Ensure these operational changes are clearly communicated to all impacted team members, including field crews and project management staff. Support the Warehouse Supervisor with upkeep of the install team vehicle fleet by ensuring that required maintenance and repairs are completed in a timely manner. Ensure that install teams have the tools and equipment they need to work effectively, including ensuring adequate availability of consumables. Analyze projects to drive down labor, material, and equipment costs. Communication & Culture Communicate key installation updates and estimated project completion times on a regular basis to the appropriate personnel. Support SunCommon’s Culture. Actively contribute to a positive, enthusiastic, and adaptable team environment. We need to love what we do, work well with our teammates, and appreciate our customers in order to achieve and deliver success. Requirements The ideal candidate for this position will have: Technical Experience & Expertise 3 or more years of leading solar installations, including roof and ground-mounted systems, in both residential and commercial settings. Electrical license or relevant experience with equipment layout, pipe runs, wiring, and interconnection preferred. NABCEP PV Installation Professional certification preferred. Experience setting up monitoring for PV systems. Thorough knowledge of electrical code and standards. Computer Proficiency: Comfort with Google suite, and data management. Maintain accurate and timely records in project management platforms, Google Calendars, and other systems. Leadership & Analytical Skills Team management experience, specifically in building teams to work collaboratively together to develop trust and accomplish tasks. Experience inspecting equipment, structures, or materials to identify the cause of errors or other problems or defects. Ability to analyze information and evaluate results to choose the best solution and solve problems. A Solutions-Oriented Mindset: Able to quickly identify effective and efficient resolutions to challenges. Culture, Attributes & Soft Skills Commitment to SunCommon’s purpose and vision. Top-notch customer service skills. A passion for delivering a joyful customer experience. Team Player & Cross-Team Collaboration: Demonstrated experience as a strong team member with superior oral and written communication skills, and solid relationship-building skills. Effective communication across departments is essential to the team’s success. Tenacity: The candidate must gain great satisfaction from a job well done and 100% complete. Adaptability: Thrives in an ever-changing environment, and meets tight deadlines. Physical Requirements Ability to regularly lift up to 50lbs, bend, twist, kneel, squat, balance, climb ladders and work in varying weather conditions. Valid drivers license and flexibility to travel throughout Vermont, including long hours of driving. COMPENSATION & BENEFITS SunCommon provides our employees a competitive salary and strong package of benefits for employees and their family, including dental and vision. Paid personal leave starting at 2 weeks for the first year, which increases to 3 weeks after 1 year of employment. 10 Paid holidays annually Retirement savings with company match Life Insurance Student Loan Paydown Program Employee Assistance Program (EAP) SunCommon branded gear SUNCOMMON VALUES Achieving our mission is critical work, and how we do that work matters. One way SunCommon creates positive change is internally, by instituting and measuring ourselves against practices that do right by our employees, customers, and communities. The following core values are critical to our operations and our success: Embody Excellence, Maintain Humanity, Prioritize Inclusivity, Cultivate Joy. We do it by celebrating creativity, cross-functional collaboration, high energy, hard work, good play, deep networking and with the acknowledgement that we’ll each make mistakes and learn from them. We know success. We know fun. Come do both with us. As a certified BCorps, we take seriously our responsibility to succeed and to honor our triple bottom line commitments to People (our employees and their families, our Customers and residents of the communities where we do business), Planet (our beloved environment and the broader globe, given climate change) and Profit (providing capital to grow, revenue to share among our employees, and a reasonable return to our investors). This is important work, and we have fun doing it. Innovation is fun stuff. SunCommon of course is an equal opportunity employer and we don’t tolerate harassment or other discrimination based upon sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, marital status, caregiver status, pregnancy, military or veteran status, race, color, religion, national origin, place of birth, ancestry, age, physical or mental disability, genetic information or any other legally protected status. Salary Description $35.00-$40.00 hourly

  • Valid State of Texas Master Electrician License in good standing.

seoDescription:
Pearce Services seeks an Advanced Solar Field Service Technician for operations and maintenance work at solar energy sites near Huntsville, Alabama. This role focuses on preventative and corrective maintenance of utility-scale solar equipment while maintaining strict safety and professional standards.

About the Role

You will support the operations and maintenance of solar power plants serving the Huntsville, Alabama area. Candidates must reside within approximately 50 miles of Huntsville. The position involves both independent work and team collaboration, with potential weekend, holiday, and on-call availability via phone or text. Travel may be required up to 25% of the time based on operational needs.

Responsibilities

  • Conduct preventative and corrective maintenance on solar utility and sub-station equipment.
  • Troubleshoot and test installed solar equipment using digital multimeters, meggers, amp clamps, and similar diagnostic tools to ensure proper operation.
  • Perform electrical component troubleshooting and diagnostics with documented results.
  • Execute Lock Out Tag Out (LOTO) procedures and Job Hazard Analysis (JHA) protocols with demonstrated safety expertise.
  • Complete and maintain work orders, time logs, inventory control documentation, and emergency information schedules.
  • Operate and maintain a motor vehicle safely and in compliance with company policy and insurance requirements.
  • Work effectively in both solo and team environments.
  • Train, mentor, and develop laborers into apprentices when applicable.

Requirements

  • 2+ years of experience in commercial or industrial operations and maintenance on solar power plants (preferred).
  • Demonstrated preventative maintenance experience on solar utility equipment (preferred).
  • Strong mechanical and electrical troubleshooting and installation skills.
  • Hands-on solar experience with inverters, tracker systems, or sub-station equipment from manufacturers such as TMEIC, SMA, Sungrow, Nextracker, or ATI (preferred).
  • Ability to comply with OSHA standards and safety regulations.
  • Valid driver's license and ability to operate and maintain a motor vehicle safely and legally.
  • Capacity to lift and move equipment up to 50 pounds.
  • Ability to work outdoors in varying ambient temperatures.
  • Initiative to identify and escalate site issues.
  • Strong work ethic and high aptitude for technical problem-solving.
  • Residency within 50 miles of Huntsville, Alabama.

Benefits

Pearce provides a comprehensive benefits package for full-time employees, including health, dental, and vision insurance; flexible spending accounts; HSA option; 401(k) with employer match; paid vacation and holidays; tuition reimbursement; and professional development training. The company also supplies a vehicle, phone, laptop or tablet, and all necessary tools and safety equipment as required for the role. Performance and referral bonuses, production incentives, tool/equipment stipends, and per diem may also be available depending on circumstances.

Compensation

$30.00–$42.00 per hour, depending on experience.

title: Solar Construction Manager
description:
Ampliform originates, develops, builds, operates, and optimizes utility-scale solar and solar + storage projects in the United States. Ampliform is led by a team of veteran developers, investors and operators in the energy sector with collectively over 100 years of management experience. Ampliform's team has originated and developed multiple gigawatts of solar energy projects and overseen several gigawatts of power generation investments.


Ampliform is a joint venture between Prospect14—a solar development platform with a data-driven approach to scaled project origination and development—and a seasoned team of infrastructure investors and operators with a track record of optimizing merchant coal, gas, and renewable power generation facilities.

The Solar Construction Manager is responsible for leading utility-scale solar projects through the engineering, procurement, and construction (EPC) lifecycle, from project handoff through commercial operation. This role oversees project planning, budgeting, scheduling, procurement, contract administration, construction execution, and stakeholder coordination to ensure projects are delivered safely, on schedule, within budget, and in compliance with contractual, regulatory, and quality requirements.

The Solar Construction Manager serves as the primary point of coordination between Development, Engineering, Procurement, Construction, Operations, external contractors, consultants, lenders, and project owners.

 

Essential Duties and Responsibilities

Project Development & Pre-Construction

  • Partner with the Development team to ensure all development milestones are completed prior to project handoff.
  • Manage the seamless transition of projects from Development to EPC execution.
  • Provide technical and operational input during project design, engineering, constructability reviews, and pre-construction planning.
  • Coordinate engineering support for permitting and development activities as required.
  • Develop comprehensive project execution plans, schedules, staffing plans, and resource requirements.

Project Planning & Financial Management

  • Develop and manage project budgets covering engineering, procurement, construction, commissioning, and project closeout.
  • Monitor project costs, forecast expenditures, identify variances, and implement corrective actions to maintain budget objectives.
  • Track project performance using established metrics and provide regular reporting to executive leadership.
  • Manage project schedules and ensure timely completion of all critical milestones.

Procurement & Contract Management

  • Lead competitive bidding and procurement activities for equipment, materials, and construction services.
  • Prepare bid packages, evaluate proposals, negotiate contracts, and provide vendor recommendations.
  • Ensure detailed scopes of work are established for all service agreements.
  • Support contract development, negotiation, and execution for:
    • EPC Agreements
    • Construction Management Agreements
    • Equipment Supply Agreements
    • Warranty Agreements
    • Commissioning Agreements
    • Memorandums of Understanding (MOUs)
    • Letters of Intent (LOIs)
    • Term Sheets
  • Review commercial and execution terms of EPC contracts and provide recommendations to senior leadership.

Project Execution & Construction Management

  • Lead project execution throughout engineering, procurement, construction, commissioning, and closeout.
  • Coordinate internal teams and external contractors including civil, mechanical, electrical, interconnection, and quality assurance personnel.
  • Organize and facilitate recurring project meetings to communicate project status, assign action items, and resolve issues.
  • Ensure contractors perform work in accordance with contract requirements, project specifications, safety standards, and quality expectations.
  • Monitor project risks and proactively develop mitigation strategies.

Regulatory Compliance & Commercial Operations

  • Ensure compliance with EPC contracts, lender requirements, permitting conditions, and reporting obligations.
  • Oversee compliance related to:
    • Interconnection Agreements
    • Inflation Reduction Act (IRA) requirements
    • Power Purchase Agreements (PPAs)
    • Environmental and regulatory requirements
  • Manage project energization, initial in-service dates, commissioning activities, and achievement of commercial operation.
  • Ensure all contractual conditions precedent are satisfied before declaring commercial operation.

Project Closeout & Operational Transition

  • Coordinate project turnover with the Operations team to ensure a successful transition into long-term operations and maintenance.
  • Verify completion of punch list items, turnover documentation, warranties, as-built drawings, and project closeout deliverables.
  • Support continuous improvement initiatives by developing project processes, reporting tools, performance metrics, and documentation standards.

Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Construction Management, Project Management, or a related technical discipline preferred.
  • 2-5 years of project management experience within utility-scale solar, renewable energy, power generation, or heavy industrial construction.
  • Strong understanding of utility-scale solar project development and EPC execution.
  • Excellent contract administration and vendor management experience.
  • Working knowledge of transmission and interconnection processes is preferred.
  • Knowledge of construction safety standards and quality management practices.
  • Strong analytical, negotiation, and problem-solving abilities.
  • Excellent verbal, written, and presentation communication skills.
  • Ability to manage multiple complex projects simultaneously in a fast-paced environment.
  • Proficiency with Microsoft Office Suite and project management software.
  • Native to project site, and ability to travel to other project sites.
  • Ability to work in outdoor construction environments and navigate active job sites.
  • Occasional extended hours may be required to support project milestones and commissioning activities.

 

Benefits

  • Company bonus eligible
  • Company sponsored medical, dental, and vision.
  • Company sponsored long-term and short-term disability.
  • Company sponsored 401(k) with company match.
  • Unlimited Paid Time Off
  • Company Paid Holidays
  • Other benefits in Ampliform's highly competitive package.

Equal Employment Opportunity

Ampliform provides equal employment opportunities to all employees and applicants for employment and prohibits discrimination and harassment of any type without regard to race, color, religion, age, sex, national origin, disability status, genetics, protected veteran status, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, or any other characteristic protected by federal, state, or local laws. We believe that a diverse team is a better team. The perspectives and experiences that people from different backgrounds bring to a company drive better decisions and improved results. Ampliform is committed to a culture of inclusion and believes that diversity drives the best results.

    • Update and refine EPC contractual agreements and requirements for BESS, with a focus on EPC obligations and the division of responsibilities.

  • Knowledge of utility equipment specifications.

  • Experience in utility electrical power system projects or distributed energy resource projects preferred.

title: Manager, Operations Solar & BESS Engineering
description:
What The Role Is

The Solar & BESS Engineering Manager is responsible for leading Operations Engineering support for Clearway solar photovoltaic (PV) and Battery Energy Storage System (BESS) assets. This role manages day-to-day technical support, reliability improvement, root cause analysis, operational readiness, and performance optimization for solar and storage facilities across the operating fleet.

The manager provides technical leadership for solar modules, inverters, trackers, and battery energy management systems. The role also develops engineering standards, strengthens technical knowledge management, reviews new project construction and acquisitions, and mentors engineers and technical contributors to assure safe, reliable, efficient, and cost-effective operation.

Our Scottsdale office is the preferred location for this hybrid position. If you don’t meet 100% of the qualifications but see yourself contributing, please submit your resume

What You'll Be Doing

Fleet Technical Leadership

  • Lead Operations Engineering support for Solar PV and BESS throughout the Clearway operating fleet.
  • Direct reliability improvements, corrective action development, and root cause analysis for Solar and BESS systems.
  • Oversee systems testing (Capacity, Round-Trip Efficiency, etc) to ensure plants meet offtake requirements.
  • Recommend, prioritize, and drive solutions that maximize reliability, availability, production, safety, and lifecycle value of Solar and BESS equipment.
  • Provide technical leadership for solar modules, inverters, trackers, BESS controls, and battery energy management systems.
  • Partner with O&M, Asset Management, Performance Analytics, Real-time Performance Monitoring Center, NERC/Compliance, Construction, Procurement, Warranty, Insurance, and external vendors to resolve issues and implement fleetwide lessons learned.

Engineering Standards, Programs, and Knowledge Management

  • Develop, maintain, and improve internal Solar/BESS technical specifications, operational procedures, testing and operational readiness checklists, lessons-learned, and engineering knowledge databases.
  • Establish consistent practices for solar module performance analysis, inverter issue resolution, BESS capacity test support, battery augmentation planning, equipment obsolescence reviews, and repowering evaluations.
  • Review drawings, single-line diagrams, site layouts, technical manuals, test reports, and vendor documentation to support safe and effective operations.
  • Support training programs for site personnel and internal stakeholders by translating technical findings into practical inspection, maintenance, troubleshooting, and operating guidance.

Project, Vendor, and Lifecycle Support

  • Support new project construction and acquisition integration by identifying technical risks and gaps and ensuring preparedness for turnover to operations.
  • Provide technical support for warranties, insurance claims, vendor performance discussions, equipment replacements, product issues, and corrective action plans.
  • Manage technical workstreams, cross-functional action plans, consultant scopes, and vendor deliverables related to Solar and BESS reliability, performance, and lifecycle management.
  • Assess equipment obsolescence, repowering, augmentation, retrofit, and performance-improvement opportunities for existing solar and storage plants.

People Leadership and Team Development

  • Manage, coach, and develop Solar/BESS engineering staff and technical contributors, including goal setting, prioritization, work planning, technical review, and professional development.
  • Balance urgent fleet support with longer-term reliability, standards, documentation, and improvement initiatives.
  • Promote a strong safety culture, disciplined technical decision-making, clear communication, and practical engineering solutions that support operational excellence.

What You'll Bring

  • B.S. in Electrical Engineering, Power Engineering, Energy Systems, Engineering Technology, or a related engineering field.
  • 7+ years of experience related to renewable energy, energy storage, power distribution, power systems, plant operations, equipment reliability, or related industry experience.
  • Prior experience leading engineers, managing technical programs, or coordinating cross-functional technical workstreams.
  • Demonstrated ability to identify and implement detailed solutions to complex technical problems and to convert lessons learned into practical standards and fleet procedures.
  • Excellent written and oral communication skills with the ability to communicate effectively with site teams, executives, internal stakeholders, customers, owners, contractors, consultants, OEMs, integrators, and external partners.
  • Advanced knowledge of Solar PV and BESS operation, maintenance, controls, performance, and reliability requirements.
  • Experienced understanding of electrical power generation, plant operations, maintenance practices, inverter systems, BESS controls, and hybrid ESS + PV configurations.
  • Able to read and interpret electrical drawings, technical manuals, test reports, control diagrams, communication drawings, and plant layouts.
  • Knowledgeable in real and reactive power support and load flow analysis.
  • Knowledgeable in applicable technical standards, including UL1703, UL1741, UL9540, UL9540A, NFPA 68, NFPA 69, NFPA 70, NFPA 72, and NFPA 855.
  • Must successfully function as both a technical leader and a member of a cross-functional team.
  • Must be able to maintain a professional and positive company image and constructive relationships with owners, customers, internal contractors, and external contractors.
  • Must be able to communicate clearly, prioritize effectively, and drive closure on technical issues with appropriate urgency and documentation discipline.
  • May be required to work flexible hours at times to support fleet events or urgent operational issues.
  • Position is located in Scottsdale, Arizona, where several Operations Engineers, the Real-time Performance Monitoring Center, Procurement, and Construction are prevalent.
  • Ability to travel up to 40%.

  • Advanced degree or professional engineering credentials are preferred.

Origis Energy is accelerating the transition to a carbon-free future by Reimagining ZeroSM. Origis Energy puts customers first to deploy a wide range of sustainable solutions for grid power generation, performance optimization, and long-term operation of solar and energy storage plants across the U.S. Founded in 2008, Origis Energy is headquartered in Miami, FL.

**Please note that all Solar Technician jobs are safety sensitive positions

 

Position Overview

The Solar PV & BESS O&M Technician is responsible for the maintenance, troubleshooting, and repair of utility-scale solar PV and energy storage systems. This role requires understanding of solar operations and electrical systems, with the ability to perform tasks independently while following established safety procedures. Technicians contribute to the overall efficiency of site operations through preventative maintenance, corrective repairs, and system monitoring.

Responsibilities

Technicians in this role will:

  • Perform inspections, preventative maintenance, and corrective repairs on AC and DC systems, including inverters, PV modules, transformers, switchgear, and high-voltage components
  • Monitor plant operations through SCADA and contribute to commissioning, testing, and system modifications
  • Follow strict safety protocols, including Job Hazard Analysis (JHA) and Lock-Out-Tag-Out (LOTO), ensuring compliance with site procedures
  • Troubleshoot electrical systems and support maintenance as required
  • Work with remote operators to identify and resolve site issues efficiently
  • Maintain accurate records of all maintenance activities using CMMS software
  • Provide guidance to other technicians as appropriate to experience level
  • Execute installation tasks with proficiency in torquing, calibration, and the use of specialized tools

 

May also be required to:

  • Lead advanced troubleshooting across multiple OEM platforms, including controls interface and system diagnostics
  • Develop and implement Lock-Out-Tag-Out (LOTO) procedures and electrical work plans
  • Read, interpret, and develop complex work procedures, schematics, and safety protocols
  • Serve as the primary customer interface, communicating site conditions, needs, and technical findings to internal and external stakeholders
  • Verify tooling and parts against work plans, relay necessary adjustments, and generate reports on findings and recommendations
  • Train and mentor junior technicians, fostering deep safety standards and adherence to industry-approved practices
  • Develop and execute work plans and maintenance schedules 

Requirements

  • Valid driver's license
  • High school diploma or equivalent; electrical certifications or industry training preferred
  • Experience in large-scale solar O&M (experience requirements vary by position level)
  • Competency in industrial or utility power operations, troubleshooting, and general maintenance procedures
  • Proficiency in reading electrical schematics, operating SCADA systems, and using CMMS for maintenance tracking
  • Strong computer skills, particularly in SCADA and CMMS applications

Advanced positions may require:

  • 4+ years of direct or related experience in the solar industry
  • Advanced knowledge of LOTO procedures and electrical work planning
  • Proficiency in troubleshooting and maintaining multiple OEM systems
  • Ability to create complex schematics and work instructions
  • Strong experience with industrial control interfaces
  • Advanced organizational skills with the ability to multitask and prioritize competing requests

Fitness for Duty Requirements

Technicians should be physically and mentally prepared to:

  • Stand, walk (including covering 2+ miles in a day), climb, bend, and kneel for extended periods in varying weather conditions
  • Lift and carry tools or equipment weighing up to 80 pounds
  • Maintain clear visual acuity (with or without corrective lenses) for reading schematics and working with tools and meters
  • Handle precise tasks that require fine motor skills and strong hand-eye coordination
  • Work outside of normal business hours as necessary.  Maintain on-call rotation schedule
  • Follow company policies on drug-free and alcohol-free workplace compliance, ensuring safety and readiness on the job

Job Level: Solar Technician 2 - Solar Technician 4

Hourly Rate: $25 - $45/hour 

Location: Palatka, FL 

Travel: Regional travel may occasionally be required to support various site demands

  • Monitor plant operations through SCADA and contribute to commissioning, testing, and system modifications

  • Develop and implement Lock-Out-Tag-Out (LOTO) procedures and electrical work plans
  • Read, interpret, and develop complex work procedures, schematics, and safety protocols
