What The Role Is

Reporting to the Pre-Construction Director, the Pre-Construction Analyst works with the Development, Engineering, and Procurement teams during early-, middle-, and late-stage Development Projects, bringing a Construction perspective.  The Pre-Con Analyst will review project studies and designs, engineering-procurement-construction schedules, Owner Furnished Equipment deliveries, construction feasibility and risk, environmental compliance, budgets, safety plans, quality plans, contract terms and exhibits, and project finance requirements.  This person will represent the Construction Team until handoff to the Construction Project Manager at Full Notice to Proceed.

This position will be based in the San Francisco, Scottsdale, Denver, or San Diego office.

If you don’t meet 100% of the qualifications but see yourself contributing, please submit your resume

What You'll Be Doing

  • Early Design and Site Feasibility: Review site and early designs for feasibility and efficiency via desktop and site visits.  Identify traffic patterns, access, existing topography and soils characteristics, vegetation and trees to remove, potential protected biology and cultural resources, watercourses, wetlands, neighbors, safety and security concerns, and interconnection access.
  • Schedule Analysis and Development: Review and provide input on assumed schedule timelines for RFP process, Engineering and Procurement durations, Construction, and Commissioning timelines to Guaranteed Milestones. Work with Procurement group to coordinate Owner Furnished Equipment schedule deliveries with EPC.
  • Construction Risk: Evaluate site for risks related to access to Interconnection Facilities, neighbors and context, site access and transportation, vegetation, existing structures to demolish, security and safety requirements, temporary facilities and O&M building location, water availability, geological and hydrological considerations, soil red flags, weather impacts, dust control requirements, Fire Department Requirements, and Labor requirements.
  • Project Budget Review: Provide input on Owner’s overall project budget including EPC costs, Owner’s Construction Management costs, Per Diem requirements, and cost of key risks to be incorporated into Contingency.

Relay final requirements to Clearway Safety and Construction Execution team prior to Full Notice to Proceed.
  • EPC Contract Term and Exhibit negotiation:  Review, redline, and negotiate EPC Agreement Terms related to Scope of Work, Contractor Deliverable formats, Safety Requirements, Operational Spare Parts, Payment Application-Schedule of Values-Cash flow, Quality Assurance, Liquidated Damages, and Guaranteed Milestone requirements.

title: Solar Electrician / Technician
description:
Origis Energy is accelerating the transition to a carbon-free future by Reimagining ZeroSM. As one of America’s leading renewable energy and decarbonization solution platforms, the company continues to expand and reimagine its contribution to the world’s net-zero goals. Origis Energy puts customers first to deploy a wide range of sustainable solutions for grid power generation, performance optimization, and long-term operation of solar and energy storage plants across the U.S. Founded in 2008, Origis Energy is headquartered in Miami, FL.

**Please note that all Solar Technician jobs are safety sensitive positions

 

Position Overview

The Solar PV & BESS O&M Technician is responsible for the maintenance, troubleshooting, and repair of utility-scale solar PV and energy storage systems. This role requires understanding of solar operations and electrical systems, with the ability to perform tasks independently while following established safety procedures. Technicians contribute to the overall efficiency of site operations through preventative maintenance, corrective repairs, and system monitoring.

Responsibilities

Technicians in this role will:

  • Perform inspections, preventative maintenance, and corrective repairs on AC and DC systems, including inverters, PV modules, transformers, switchgear, and high-voltage components
  • Monitor plant operations through SCADA and contribute to commissioning, testing, and system modifications
  • Follow strict safety protocols, including Job Hazard Analysis (JHA) and Lock-Out-Tag-Out (LOTO), ensuring compliance with site procedures
  • Troubleshoot electrical systems and support maintenance as required
  • Work with remote operators to identify and resolve site issues efficiently
  • Maintain accurate records of all maintenance activities using CMMS software
  • Provide guidance to other technicians as appropriate to experience level
  • Execute installation tasks with proficiency in torquing, calibration, and the use of specialized tools

 

May also be required to:

  • Lead advanced troubleshooting across multiple OEM platforms, including controls interface and system diagnostics
  • Develop and implement Lock-Out-Tag-Out (LOTO) procedures and electrical work plans
  • Read, interpret, and develop complex work procedures, schematics, and safety protocols
  • Serve as the primary customer interface, communicating site conditions, needs, and technical findings to internal and external stakeholders
  • Verify tooling and parts against work plans, relay necessary adjustments, and generate reports on findings and recommendations
  • Train and mentor junior technicians, fostering deep safety standards and adherence to industry-approved practices
  • Develop and execute work plans and maintenance schedules

 

Requirements

  • Valid driver's license
  • High school diploma or equivalent; electrical certifications or industry training preferred
  • Experience in large-scale solar O&M (experience requirements vary by position level)
  • Competency in industrial or utility power operations, troubleshooting, and general maintenance procedures
  • Proficiency in reading electrical schematics, operating SCADA systems, and using CMMS for maintenance tracking
  • Strong computer skills, particularly in SCADA and CMMS applications

 

Advanced positions may require:

  • 4+ years of direct or related experience in the solar industry
  • Advanced knowledge of LOTO procedures and electrical work planning
  • Proficiency in troubleshooting and maintaining multiple OEM systems
  • Ability to create complex schematics and work instructions
  • Strong experience with industrial control interfaces
  • Advanced organizational skills with the ability to multitask and prioritize competing requests

 

Fitness for Duty Requirements

Technicians should be physically and mentally prepared to:

  • Stand, walk (including covering 2+ miles in a day), climb, bend, and kneel for extended periods in varying weather conditions
  • Lift and carry tools or equipment weighing up to 80 pounds
  • Maintain clear visual acuity (with or without corrective lenses) for reading schematics and working with tools and meters
  • Handle precise tasks that require fine motor skills and strong hand-eye coordination
  • May be required to work outside of normal business hours as necessary.  Maintain on-call rotation schedule.
  • Follow company policies on drug-free and alcohol-free workplace compliance, ensuring safety and readiness on the job

 

Job Level: Solar Technician 2 - Solar Technician 4

Hourly Rate: $25 - $45/hour 

Location: Wing, AL

Travel: Regional travel may occasionally be required to support various site demands

 

We currently have sites in Texas, Tennessee, New Mexico, Florida, Mississippi, Alabama, Illinois, Missouri and Indiana.

Position Description

Origis Energy is adding to its existing in-house transmission and grid analysis team and is seeking an experienced, creative, self-starting and highly motivated individual to manage the utility-scale solar and energy storage Interconnection pipeline across the US. They will work alongside our team of Generation Interconnection experts, which is part of our larger Project Development Team. The ideal candidate should be knowledgeable in a broad range of electrical engineering applications, have experience in the solar/storage energy sector, and be able to work collaboratively with a diverse team. 

The Generator Interconnection (Transmission) Manager/Director is heavily involved in the company’s development strategy related to its portfolio of existing and proposed utility-scale solar and energy storage projects. Director level depends on the experience of the candidate.  The Manager/Director of Interconnection will interact daily with the company’s project development team that consists of subject matter experts in real estate, environmental & permitting, engineering, origination, finance, GIS, procurement, etc. The ideal candidate will work alongside with our internal Transmission Modeling team to provide ongoing technical engineering support for various generation interconnection (GI) studies, coordinate with outside consultants to manage the GI study process associated with various utilities and ISOs, review and critique interconnection study results. The Manager of Transmission will also ensure compliance with relevant tariffs and represent the company’s interests at various Utilities/ISOs/RTOs to shape renewable energy policy.

This role is a regular, full-time position, and is eligible for our generous employee benefits package, including employer paid health insurance, paid time off, a 401(k) plan with employer matching contributions, and other great benefits.

Key Responsibilities

  • Familiar with ISOs all throughout the US including but not limited to SERC, TVA, ERCOT, MISO, CAISO, and WECC
  • Work closely with in-house Grid Analysis team or consultant in coordinating system modeling to identify potential POI’s for new greenfield projects
  • Familiar with load flow modeling software but not actually running models
  • Familiarity with load study applications and related load requirements for data centers and other large commercial loads
  • Evaluation of Interconnection study reports and coordination with Business Development, Project Dev, and Finance Team
  • Oversee and coordinate the entirety of the interconnection process from filing to post-GIA phases
  • Manage daily interconnection tasks for various renewable projects for prospective projects and projects under development
  • Develop transmission strategy and provide expert opinion for grid transmission related topics
  • Familiar with Regulatory orders that may benefit renewables
  • Perform due diligence on interconnection materials to support project acquisition efforts
  • Working knowledge of ISO/Utility interconnection Tariffs
  • Provide creative and knowledgeable input to assist in the growth of the company’s resource development pipeline; including project site identification, project size optimization, fatal flaw analysis, interconnection queue management, tariff assessment and risk mitigation strategies.
  • Support budget forecasting and provide guidance to minimize financial risk throughout the GI study process.
  • Suggest creative bidding strategies that utilize knowledge of the transmission system and thoughtful assessment of study results and hedging options.
  • Maintain accurate GI data in the company’s proprietary database.
  • Develop processes to effectively manage all interconnection planning activities.
  • Provide regular reports to management and project teams regarding project milestones and critical path decisions.
  • Coordinate with internal teams and outside consultants to reach consensus on interconnection strategy and estimated project costs.
  • Participate in various public forums and represent the interests of the company at industry related meetings, conferences and/or legislative events.
  • Develop strong relationships with outside stakeholders such as ISO/RTO representatives.
  • Final – Coordination with management and legal to support execution of the Interconnection Agreement

Preferred Qualifications

  • Bachelor of Science Degree in Electrical Engineering required, preferably with an emphasis in power systems.
  • Master of Science Degree in Power Systems and/or a Master of Business Administration Degree highly preferred.
  • 5-7 years of experience in renewable power system analysis or related fields.
  • Experience using industry relevant software such as PSSE, PSLF or PowerWorld 
  • Generation Interconnection model development experience at a utility or RTO is strongly preferred.
  • Demonstrated competence in FERC/ISO RTO working groups, contract negotiations, or other related business experience is also valued.
  • Must have good analytical, decision-making, communication, creative problem-solving, and human relations skills.
  • Must be organized, self-motivated and capable of working both independently and in group settings.

Key Attributes for Success

  • Ability to attract, train, mentor, and retain talented employees
  • Excellent communication skills, both verbal and written
  • Strong organizational, problem-solving, and leadership skills
  • High attention to detail
  • Ability to multi-task and work in a very fast-paced environment
  • Team-oriented with excellent interpersonal skills and ability to develop collaborative working relationships across multiple functional areas in the organization
  • Has a strong customer mindset
  • Ability to work with all levels of management and key stakeholders

The role will have a hand in crafting the overall performance strategy for the organization and define the technical critical processes, systems, and tools that will allow the overall performance engineering group to drive the highest value/MWh possible across all operating renewable energy assets. This role partners closely with the Medium Voltage engineering team at SMA AG to work through solutions for SMA U.S. customers and suppliers, and supports warranty repairs, technical support, and extensive testing of the internal workings of SMA Medium Voltage products.
We are building this team across three experience levels. We currently have 3 openings across the Central region, filled across Houston, Dallas and Fort Worth, and San Antonio. If you are early in your medium voltage career and coming from utility scale inverter commissioning, substation work, transformer service, military electrical service, or an electrical trade, we want to hear from you. If you are a seasoned medium voltage technician who leads crews and owns complex troubleshooting, we want to hear from you as well.

WHAT WE PROVIDE
You show up with your experience. We provide the rest.

  • A company truck, including fuel, insurance, and maintenance. You are not putting miles on your own vehicle.
  • Tools, work clothing, and safety footwear. You are not buying your own gear.
  • Medium voltage certification through the AVO Training Institute, sponsored by SMA, including course cost and travel.
  • Two to three weeks of inverter training at our headquarters in Rocklin, California, followed by field training alongside experienced technicians.
  • A defined three level technical career path with a clear line of sight from Level I to Level III.

HOW THIS ROLE IS LEVELED
This is one posting covering three levels. You apply once. We determine level during the interview process based on your experience, certifications, and the scope of work you are ready to own. Compensation is set to the level you are placed in.

  • Level I. Assists crews with testing, inspection, and maintenance under the direction of a senior technician. Focused on building foundational medium voltage skills, terminations, print reading, and safe work practice.
  • Level II. Performs testing, maintenance, and troubleshooting independently. Owns documentation and serves as a field point of contact for customers.
  • Level III. Leads crews and complex troubleshooting, approves reports and closure packages, mentors Level I and II technicians, and serves as the senior technical resource on site.

PRIMARY DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES
At every level:

  • Participates in daily job site safety briefings, proactively identifying, eliminating, and mitigating hazards.
  • Performs testing, inspection, maintenance, and repair of SMA Large Scale Medium Voltage systems in the field, including Medium Voltage transformer core testing, operations and maintenance, and site visits.
  • Conducts DGA sampling and applies the results of DGA reports to determine the correct course of action.
  • Regularly works with high voltage DC, three phase power, high AC voltage, and the related software and firmware of SMA products.
  • Completes accurate documentation, including test reports, discrepancy lists, and field service reports.
  • Performs and maintains maintenance activities in accordance with the SMA product maintenance manual on assigned sites with SMA customer contractual obligations.
  • Maintains accurate inventory count of spare parts provided by SMA, and maintains assigned tools and vehicle in safe working condition.
  • Maintains a high level of customer satisfaction while striving to lower the costs of field service expenditure.
  • Other duties may be assigned or required.

At Level II and above:

  • Performs independent troubleshooting of electrical and control systems, determining root cause and implementing corrective actions.
  • Repairs external leaks and performs cold weld patches on Medium Voltage transformers.
  • Serves as a field point of contact for customers, providing updates and addressing concerns on site.
  • Collaborates cross functionally with the Global Service Organization, Quality, and suppliers to provide customers with Root Cause Analysis of failures, and keeps customers informed of RCA status.

At Level III:

  • Leads crews in the testing, inspection, and maintenance of high, medium, and low voltage electrical equipment.
  • Applies expert knowledge of high voltage test equipment to identify root causes for SMA internal quality 8D reports.
  • Reviews and approves test reports, discrepancy lists, and project closure packages.
  • Works directly with Medium Voltage engineering counterparts at SMA AG for technical assistance and guidance on MV systems, attending meetings on a daily or weekly basis.
  • Trains, mentors, and qualifies Level I and Level II technicians, supporting their technical development and safe work practice.
  • Develops detailed knowledge to aid in the creation of processes and procedures for SMA Medium Voltage products and associated SMA or third party accessories sold by SMA.

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS
These apply at every level. Experience beyond this moves you to a higher level rather than being required to apply.

  • At least one year of hands on experience in an electrical, electronic, utility, or field service role. Relevant military experience qualifies, including Army 12P Prime Power Production Specialist, Navy Electrician's Mate, and Construction Electrician.
  • Demonstrated exposure to medium voltage equipment such as transformers, switchgear, circuit breakers, terminations, or substation work, through employment, an apprenticeship, a trade program, or military service.
  • An associate degree in electrical or electronic technology, a completed trade or apprenticeship program, military technical training, or equivalent qualified experience.
  • Comfort with electronic test equipment, at minimum a digital voltmeter and common hand tools, and the ability to read prints, schematics, and wiring diagrams.
  • Ability to analyze and solve problems effectively.
  • Ability to work nonstandard business hours occasionally to support service customer contracts, including weekend or night work when customer requirements at the site call for it.
  • Ability to meet the travel requirements outlined below.
  • A valid driver's license and a driving record that meets SMA insurance requirements, since a company vehicle is assigned to this role.
  • Proficiency with Microsoft Office Suite, including Word, PowerPoint, and Excel.

WHAT MOVES YOU TO A HIGHER LEVEL
None of the following is required to apply. Each strengthens your candidacy and factors into the level you are placed in.

  • Additional years of direct medium voltage field experience. Level II generally reflects three to five years. Level III generally reflects ten or more.
  • Hands on experience with high voltage test equipment and the ability to interpret results, including power factor, megger, CT ratio and saturation, and hipot testing.
  • Experience with pad mounted transformers, Medium Voltage terminations, splicing, and switchgear operation.
  • Hands on experience with cold weld patch repairs and field transformer repairs.
  • Certifications through the AVO Training Institute or another accredited institution or trade school, including Medium Voltage Transformer Levels I and II, Switch Gear and Circuit Breaker Maintenance with grounding and bonding, Electrical Safety for Utilities, and Substation Maintenance I and II.
  • NETA certification at any level, NFPA 70E, or comparable electrical safety and testing credentials.
  • Crew leadership, mentoring, or project coordination experience in the field.
  • Advanced knowledge of power plant measurement devices and techniques.
  • Knowledge of solar or alternative energy markets, and of the National Electric Code.
  • A bachelor's degree in a technical field.

TRAINING AND CERTIFICATION SUPPORT
Medium voltage certification is part of this role rather than a barrier to entering it. Technicians hired without the AVO certifications listed above are expected to complete them within the first year of employment, and SMA sponsors that training, including course cost and travel.

  • Travel: Approximately 80% travel, primarily to customer sites across the Central region, with occasional travel elsewhere in the United States.
  • Vehicle: A company truck is provided for site travel, including fuel, insurance, and maintenance.
  • Standard rotation: Approximately two weeks on site at a time, with weekends home possible when site conditions allow.
  • First year onboarding: Travel is heavier during the first year, including 2 to 3 weeks of mandatory inverter training at SMA America headquarters in Rocklin, CA, and extended on the job field training at project sites alongside experienced team members, which may require two weeks or more away from home at a time.

Why Work at SMA America

Power the future. Build your career at SMA America.

As the U.S. subsidiary of SMA Solar Technology AG, we have been at the forefront of solar inverter technology since 1981, developing solutions that make photovoltaic power plants simpler, more reliable, safer, and more cost effective. Headquartered in Rocklin, California, SMA America has spent more than two decades helping homes, businesses, and utilities across the country generate clean, reliable power. We are the only inverter manufacturer in the world offering solutions for every system size, from residential rooftops to large scale utility plants, backed by more than 1,500 patents and a presence in over 190 countries.

Innovation is only part of the story. We invest in our people, create room to grow, challenge conventional thinking, and protect a culture where teammates genuinely care about each other and the work. We hire capable people and give them the space to do the job, with clear expectations, open door leadership, and real autonomy.

If you are passionate about driving positive change and want a career where you can take ownership of your work, we would love to meet you. Together, we are not just part of the energy transition, we are helping drive it forward.

Field Service Engineer, Medium Voltage, Western (Phoenix, AZ)

LOCATION AND WORK MODEL
This position is field based and covers the Western region. Candidates must currently reside in the Phoenix metropolitan area or within commuting distance of it. This position requires significant regional travel across the Western region, with occasional travel elsewhere in the United States. A company truck is provided, so no personal vehicle is required for site travel.

WORK AUTHORIZATION
Applicants must be authorized to work in the United States on a full time basis. SMA America does not offer employment visa sponsorship of any kind, including H-1B, OPT, CPT, or TN visas. Candidates who currently require or will in the future require visa sponsorship are not eligible for this role. Candidates operating under a temporary work permit or any visa tied employment authorization are also not eligible.

AI GENERATED APPLICATION MATERIALS
We review all resumes and application materials for AI generated content. Submissions that show evidence of AI manipulation, including AI written resumes, cover letters, or responses, will be disqualified from consideration without further review. We want to hear your authentic voice and see your genuine experience.

RECRUITMENT FRAUD NOTICE
All SMA America openings are posted on our official careers page and all recruiter communication comes from an @sma-america.com address. We never request payment, banking information, or a Social Security number during the recruitment process. If you are contacted about an SMA America role from a personal email account, or asked for any of the above, please forward the message to HRGeneralmailbox@sma-america.com.

PURPOSE OF THE POSITION
The Field Service Engineer, Medium Voltage is responsible for the testing, maintenance, troubleshooting, and repair of SMA Medium Voltage systems in the field, including handling Medium Voltage escalations for SMA customers and suppliers. This role partners closely with the Medium Voltage engineering team at SMA AG to work through solutions for SMA U.S. customers and suppliers, and supports warranty repairs, technical support, and extensive testing of the internal workings of SMA Medium Voltage products.
We are building this team across three experience levels. We currently have 3 openings across the Western region, filled across Phoenix, Las Vegas, and San Diego. If you are early in your medium voltage career and coming from utility scale inverter commissioning, substation work, transformer service, military electrical service, or an electrical trade, we want to hear from you. If you are a seasoned medium voltage technician who leads crews and owns complex troubleshooting, we want to hear from you as well.

WHAT WE PROVIDE
You show up with your experience. We provide the rest.

  • A company truck, including fuel, insurance, and maintenance. You are not putting miles on your own vehicle.
  • Tools, work clothing, and safety footwear. You are not buying your own gear.
  • Medium voltage certification through the AVO Training Institute, sponsored by SMA, including course cost and travel.
  • Two to three weeks of inverter training at our headquarters in Rocklin, California, followed by field training alongside experienced technicians.
  • A defined three level technical career path with a clear line of sight from Level I to Level III.

HOW THIS ROLE IS LEVELED
This is one posting covering three levels. You apply once. We determine level during the interview process based on your experience, certifications, and the scope of work you are ready to own. Compensation is set to the level you are placed in.

  • Level I. Assists crews with testing, inspection, and maintenance under the direction of a senior technician. Focused on building foundational medium voltage skills, terminations, print reading, and safe work practice.
  • Level II. Performs testing, maintenance, and troubleshooting independently. Owns documentation and serves as a field point of contact for customers.
  • Level III. Leads crews and complex troubleshooting, approves reports and closure packages, mentors Level I and II technicians, and serves as the senior technical resource on site.

PRIMARY DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES
At every level:

  • Participates in daily job site safety briefings, proactively identifying, eliminating, and mitigating hazards.
  • Performs testing, inspection, maintenance, and repair of SMA Large Scale Medium Voltage systems in the field, including Medium Voltage transformer core testing, operations and maintenance, and site visits.
  • Conducts DGA sampling and applies the results of DGA reports to determine the correct course of action.
  • Regularly works with high voltage DC, three phase power, high AC voltage, and the related software and firmware of SMA products.
  • Completes accurate documentation, including test reports, discrepancy lists, and field service reports.
  • Performs and maintains maintenance activities in accordance with the SMA product maintenance manual on assigned sites with SMA customer contractual obligations.
  • Maintains accurate inventory count of spare parts provided by SMA, and maintains assigned tools and vehicle in safe working condition.
  • Maintains a high level of customer satisfaction while striving to lower the costs of field service expenditure.
  • Other duties may be assigned or required.

At Level II and above:

  • Performs independent troubleshooting of electrical and control systems, determining root cause and implementing corrective actions.
  • Repairs external leaks and performs cold weld patches on Medium Voltage transformers.
  • Serves as a field point of contact for customers, providing updates and addressing concerns on site.
  • Collaborates cross functionally with the Global Service Organization, Quality, and suppliers to provide customers with Root Cause Analysis of failures, and keeps customers informed of RCA status.

At Level III:

  • Leads crews in the testing, inspection, and maintenance of high, medium, and low voltage electrical equipment.
  • Applies expert knowledge of high voltage test equipment to identify root causes for SMA internal quality 8D reports.
  • Reviews and approves test reports, discrepancy lists, and project closure packages.
  • Works directly with Medium Voltage engineering counterparts at SMA AG for technical assistance and guidance on MV systems, attending meetings on a daily or weekly basis.
  • Trains, mentors, and qualifies Level I and Level II technicians, supporting their technical development and safe work practice.
  • Develops detailed knowledge to aid in the creation of processes and procedures for SMA Medium Voltage products and associated SMA or third party accessories sold by SMA.

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS
These apply at every level. Experience beyond this moves you to a higher level rather than being required to apply.

  • At least one year of hands on experience in an electrical, electronic, utility, or field service role. Relevant military experience qualifies, including Army 12P Prime Power Production Specialist, Navy Electrician's Mate, and Construction Electrician.
  • Demonstrated exposure to medium voltage equipment such as transformers, switchgear, circuit breakers, terminations, or substation work, through employment, an apprenticeship, a trade program, or military service.
  • An associate degree in electrical or electronic technology, a completed trade or apprenticeship program, military technical training, or equivalent qualified experience.
  • Comfort with electronic test equipment, at minimum a digital voltmeter and common hand tools, and the ability to read prints, schematics, and wiring diagrams.
  • Ability to analyze and solve problems effectively.
  • Ability to work nonstandard business hours occasionally to support service customer contracts, including weekend or night work when customer requirements at the site call for it.
  • Ability to meet the travel requirements outlined below.
  • A valid driver's license and a driving record that meets SMA insurance requirements, since a company vehicle is assigned to this role.
  • Proficiency with Microsoft Office Suite, including Word, PowerPoint, and Excel.

WHAT MOVES YOU TO A HIGHER LEVEL
None of the following is required to apply. Each strengthens your candidacy and factors into the level you are placed in.

  • Additional years of direct medium voltage field experience. Level II generally reflects three to five years. Level III generally reflects ten or more.
  • Hands on experience with high voltage test equipment and the ability to interpret results, including power factor, megger, CT ratio and saturation, and hipot testing.
  • Experience with pad mounted transformers, Medium Voltage terminations, splicing, and switchgear operation.
  • Hands on experience with cold weld patch repairs and field transformer repairs.
  • Certifications through the AVO Training Institute or another accredited institution or trade school, including Medium Voltage Transformer Levels I and II, Switch Gear and Circuit Breaker Maintenance with grounding and bonding, Electrical Safety for Utilities, and Substation Maintenance I and II.
  • NETA certification at any level, NFPA 70E, or comparable electrical safety and testing credentials.
  • Crew leadership, mentoring, or project coordination experience in the field.
  • Advanced knowledge of power plant measurement devices and techniques.
  • Knowledge of solar or alternative energy markets, and of the National Electric Code.
  • A bachelor's degree in a technical field.

TRAINING AND CERTIFICATION SUPPORT
Medium voltage certification is part of this role rather than a barrier to entering it. Technicians hired without the AVO certifications listed above are expected to complete them within the first year of employment, and SMA sponsors that training, including course cost and travel.

TRAVEL REQUIREMENTS

  • Extent of responsibility: Regional.
  • Travel: Approximately 80% travel, primarily to customer sites across the Western region, with occasional travel elsewhere in the United States.
  • Vehicle: A company truck is provided for site travel, including fuel, insurance, and maintenance.
  • Standard rotation: Approximately two weeks on site at a time, with weekends home possible when site conditions allow.
  • First year onboarding: Travel is heavier during the first year, including 2 to 3 weeks of mandatory inverter training at SMA America headquarters in Rocklin, CA, and extended on the job field training at project sites alongside experienced team members, which may require two weeks or more away from home at a time.
  • Schedule changes: Travel schedules may shift based on customer needs, site conditions, and project timelines.

PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS

  • While at site, the employee is required to stand, walk, talk, hear, and observe surroundings.
  • The employee is occasionally required to sit, reach above the shoulder, stoop, bend, squat, and kneel.
  • The employee must routinely lift up to 50 pounds.
  • The work environment is constrained to a field service environment, with occasional functions in a corporate office.
  • The employee is occasionally exposed to electrical hazards and to weather of extreme temperatures.
  • The noise level in the work environment is usually moderate.

WE OFFER

  • Compensation: $33.00 to $43.00 per hour, dependent on level, experience, and qualifications.
  • Vehicle: Company truck provided, including fuel, insurance, and maintenance. No personal vehicle required for site travel.
  • Tools and gear: Company provided tools, work clothing, and safety footwear. You do not buy your own.
  • Benefits: Comprehensive health, dental, and vision coverage, including $0 premium options.
  • Work Model: Field based, with a home office in the Phoenix, Arizona metropolitan area.
  • Retirement: 401(k) plan with company match.
  • Growth: A defined three level technical career path, with sponsored certification and training at every step.
  • Culture: Inclusive, collaborative, and innovative work environment.

Our EEO Policy

We are an equal opportunity employer and we make our employment decisions on the basis of merit and without regard to one's race, color, creed, sex (includes gender, pregnancy, childbirth and related medical conditions), gender identity, religion, marital status, age (over 40), national origin or ancestry, physical or mental disability (includes HIV/Aids), medical condition (cancer, genetic characteristics), veteran's status, sexual orientation, or any other consideration made unlawful by law.

In accordance with applicable law protecting qualified individuals with known disabilities, SMA will attempt to reasonably accommodate qualified applicants with known disabilities, unless doing so would create an undue hardship on SMA. Any qualified applicant with a disability who believes he or she requires an accommodation in order to perform the essential functions of the job for which he or she is applying should identify the accommodation(s) needed in the application.

Our Privacy Policy

During your job application or recruitment process with us: (a) SMA may collect your personal information directly from you, such as when you submit your application and resume on our online portal or when you have job interviews with us. We may also obtain your personal information from third parties, including but not limited to your former employers, background or employment check service providers or third-party recruiters; and, (b) SMA may use or process applicants' personal information for relevant purposes including but not limited to general communications with you, identity verification, background or employment checks, determination of eligibility, and making hiring decisions. For successful job applicants who become SMA's staff, we may retain and integrate your personal information collected during the recruitment process into your records at SMA.

If you are a California resident, you have specific rights regarding your personal information under the California Consumer Privacy Act of 2018, as amended including by the California Privacy Rights Act of 2020, and its implementing regulations (the "CCPA"). This Company Personnel and Covered Individuals Privacy Notice for California Residents issued by SMA is applicable to you and explains your CCPA rights and our collection, use or disclosure of your personal information.

If you have any question regarding our privacy policy, please contact us at US_DataPrivacy@sma-america.com

title: Project Manager
description:
Opportunity

 

Adapture Renewables, Inc. is on a mission to be a leader in this new era of sustainable energy. Drawing upon an extensive knowledge base, we develop, finance, engineer, build, own, and operate high quality utility-scale photovoltaic projects and battery energy storage projects. Our Construction team is looking for a talented Project Manager to help support the efforts of our fast-growing company. Adapture Renewables is owned by KIRKBI Climate – the private holding and investment company of the Kirk Kristiansen family founded to build a sustainable future for the LEGO® brand through generations.

 

Overview

 

This position will work in our Construction team and lead the end-to-end delivery of utility-scale solar PV and battery energy storage projects, from development and preconstruction handoff through commercial operation, owning project plans, budgets, schedules, and EPC execution while leading a project team of APMs, CMs, and Quality Managers. This position reports to the Director of Construction. The candidate may be based remotely in the U.S., with periodic travel to our Bay Area home office and other company locations.

 

Core Responsibilities

 

  • Lead and manage internal and external resources to execute through development and precon handoff to project team
  • Lead contract negotiations with EPCs and drive contract execution process
  • Lead project procurement coordination activities (e.g., modules, MPT, HV breakers)
  • Assist the development team by providing site risk assessment and mitigation options
  • Analyze site for key constructability factors based on constraint data including, but not limited to, environmental risks, easements, wetlands, and pipelines
  • Interview, hire, lead, and retain APMs, CMs, and Quality Managers to manage projects from inception to O&M
  • Manage project plans and budgets; compile revenue and cash flow forecasts; compile financial reports for executive management and shareholders
  • Manage utility requirements and GIA, including substation, switchyard, and T-line construction
  • Manage and build BESS projects, including standalone, co-located, and combined configurations
  • Drive project schedule to meet contractual EPC milestones, Utility/GIA milestones, ISO COD, and PPA COD deadlines
  • Provide support to the precon team on RFP bid reviews and technical documentation, including support in the EPC selection process
  • Conduct monthly owner site visits and assessments to monitor and manage construction EPCs
  • Implement, monitor, and improve the following systems on a project-by-project basis:
    • Site-specific safety program and site safety audits
    • Quality management program and QA/QC inspections
    • Cost management system
    • Schedule management system
  • Lead and coordinate communications with landowners, utilities, and offtakers as needed during construction
  • Report on project health regularly to management
  • Represent the construction department in relevant development and delivery meetings as required
  • Represent the construction department during relevant third-party stakeholder meetings and events as required
  • Coordinate weekly one-on-one meetings with the project team

 

Qualifications and Experience

 

  • Demonstrated experience managing utility-scale solar PV and BESS construction projects from inception through commercial operation
  • Bachelor’s degree in engineering, construction management, or a related field, or equivalent industry experience
  • PVsyst energy modeling software experience
  • Experience with PV utility-scale design, including layouts and single-line diagrams
  • Experience with civil design requirements for the development of PV utility-scale projects, including site access, site drainage, and hydrology
  • Experience with various PV technologies used in utility-scale projects in the U.S. market
  • Experience with resource analysis and performance metrics and KPIs, including leading training and certification processes
  • OSHA 30 certification; CPR/First-Aid/AED; SWPPP and erosion control
  • Strong leadership, negotiation, and stakeholder communication skills
  • Position requires regular travel to project sites and other company locations

 

Benefits Package

 

  • 401(k) plan with company matching contribution
  • Competitive health, vision, and dental benefits
  • Attractive personal time off and company holiday package
  • Work-from-home policy
  • Salary commensurate with experience
  • $135,000 - $155,000, DOE

 

Note

 

Qualified candidates only. No search firms. Adapture Renewables, Inc. is committed to equal employment opportunity.

title: Solar Field Service Technician II
description:
At PEARCE, we've got a career for you!

Pearce is a leading technology-enabled provider of asset management solutions for mission-critical electromechanical infrastructure throughout North America. Pearce provides technical maintenance, repair, operations, and engineering services for uninterruptible power supply (UPS) systems, backup power generators, battery energy storage systems (BESS), critical cooling systems, and other electrical and mechanical infrastructure across end markets such as renewable energy, telecom, and data centers. Founded in 1998, Pearce has more than 4,000 employees and 28 locations across the U.S. Pearce is a wholly owned subsidiary of CBRE Group, Inc., the world’s largest commercial real estate services and investment firm. To learn more about Pearce visit http://www.pearce-services.com.

Your Impact

title: Manager, Business Development and M&A
description:
What The Role Is

Reporting to the Director of Business Development and M&A, the role is responsible for growing the Clearway development and operating platform for utility-scale wind, solar, and energy storage projects, as well as multi-technology complexes. This includes managing the acquisition of both development and operating assets, as well as greenfielding new development projects, in support of Clearway’s profitability and strategic goals.  The role requires close collaboration with internal subject matter experts, external consultants, and legal counsel.    

This hybrid role will be located in our Denver, CO office. If you don’t meet 100% of the qualifications but see yourself contributing, please submit your resume.

What You'll Be Doing

  • Manage the project acquisition process: deal origination, valuation, structuring, due diligence, negotiation, and closing of project acquisitions as a key member/manager of a transaction team.
    • Coordinate with internal and external counsel to negotiate and draft definitive transaction documentation.
    • Coordinate with internal constituents and third-party consultants to perform due diligence activities.
    • Work with subject matter experts in project development, engineering, procurement, capital markets, O&M, and others to ensure conformance with underwriting guidelines, investment metrics, and forecasted cash flows. Run sensitivity analyses and generate ideas to optimize valuations and transaction structures.
    • Prepare detailed memos and presentations for senior management and the investment committee.
    • Create and manage tools to monitor market activity and track internal origination strategy to identify new growth areas and M&A targets.
  • Support ongoing origination, development, and financing activities for projects that Clearway owns.
    • Support pricing analysis and bidding strategy to originate offtake contracts for Clearway’s 30 GW+ development portfolio of utility-scale wind, solar, and energy storage projects, as well as multi-technology complexes.
    • Work with functional groups, third-party consultants, and various other stakeholders to drive projects forward and perform quantitative analyses to support development and financing judgments.
  • Craft and implement overall strategy within specific regions, identify opportunities, and work with development to allocate the development budget strategically.
  • Drive strategy and execution in emerging growth segments including non-traditional offtake, technology, and/or financing structures, as opportunities present.
    • In consultation with external and internal resources, develop market assessments, production cost models, analytical tools, and business cases for early investments in emerging growth segments.
    • Help connect the dots internally to reposition existing assets (development or operating) for opportunities in emerging growth segments.
    • Support formation and ongoing management of strategic partnerships with major equipment suppliers, operators, investors, project developers, and other value chain participants.
  • Guide strategic initiatives to improve analytical tools and inform key business activities at Clearway.
    • Assist with ongoing efforts to improve financial optimization, underwriting, deal tracking, etc.
    • Develop innovative financial and offtake structures and improve existing quantitative analysis tools.
    • Guide special projects across internal functional groups to drive value creation throughout the development, procurement, construction, and financing processes.
    • Leverage AI tools effectively in support of the aforementioned scope.

What You'll Bring

  • Bachelor's Degree required in finance, business administration, or economics.
  • A minimum of 4-5 years of relevant work experience at a U.S. solar, wind, or energy storage development company/Independent Power Producer in an M&A, finance, or development role with a specific focus on M&A transactions, financial modeling/valuation, project development, and energy markets. Alternatively, the candidate may bring similar and transferable experience from an investment banking firm.
  • Comfort navigating transactions, particularly negotiation of M&A transactions.
  • Excellent aptitude for analytical and financial modeling with demonstrated attention to detail. Strong quantitative skills are a must for this position. Advanced capabilities in Excel and PowerPoint are essential.
  • Ability to effectively summarize complex issues and recommend next steps, both in writing and verbally, in a compelling manner that resonates with the audience.
  • Ability to manage simultaneous projects/work streams, set priorities, and exercise sound judgment unsupervised. 
  • Previous mentoring and team management experience.
  • Knowledge of renewable energy project development areas, such as real estate, permitting, grid integration, transmission, offtake, tax, and financing structures.

Clearway will not sponsor non-immigrant visas for this position (H-1B, TN, E-3, etc.).

This role is eligible to earn an annual cash bonus, subject to personal and company performance goals.

  • Monitor plant operations through SCADA and contribute to commissioning, testing, and system modifications
  • Follow strict safety protocols, including Job Hazard Analysis (JHA) and Lock-Out-Tag-Out (LOTO), ensuring compliance with site procedures
  • Troubleshoot electrical systems and support maintenance as required

  • Maintain accurate records of all maintenance activities using CMMS software
  • Provide guidance to other technicians as appropriate to experience level

  • Develop and implement Lock-Out-Tag-Out (LOTO) procedures and electrical work plans
  • Read, interpret, and develop complex work procedures, schematics, and safety protocols
  • Serve as the primary customer interface, communicating site conditions, needs, and technical findings to internal and external stakeholders
  • Verify tooling and parts against work plans, relay necessary adjustments, and generate reports on findings and recommendations
  • Train and mentor junior technicians, fostering deep safety standards and adherence to industry-approved practices

  • Experience in large-scale solar O&M (experience requirements vary by position level)

  • Proficiency in troubleshooting and maintaining multiple OEM systems

  • Strong experience with industrial control interfaces
  • Advanced organizational skills with the ability to multitask and prioritize competing requests

Technicians should be physically and mentally prepared to:

  • Stand, walk (including covering 2+ miles in a day), climb, bend, and kneel for extended periods in varying weather conditions
  • Lift and carry tools or equipment weighing up to 80 pounds
  • Maintain clear visual acuity (with or without corrective lenses) for reading schematics and working with tools and meters
  • Handle precise tasks that require fine motor skills and strong hand-eye coordination
  • Work outside of normal business hours as necessary.  Maintain on-call rotation schedule

title: Reliability Engineer - Photovoltaics
description:
About the company

At Swift Solar, our mission is to unlock the full potential of solar energy. We believe solar can provide affordable, reliable, resilient, clean energy to virtually anyone, anywhere. But while today’s solar technology is good, it’s not good enough.

Swift Solar’s breakthrough perovskite-silicon tandem technology will drive solar power to commanding new heights. Our tandem cells stack a perovskite layer on top of a heterojunction (HJT) silicon cell, delivering dramatically higher efficiency than traditional silicon alone. In 2026, we acquired Meyer Burger’s HJT intellectual property and manufacturing assets, giving us the world’s most extensive HJT patent portfolio and a clear path to gigawatt-scale domestic production.

This vertically integrated approach means we can design, manufacture, and scale next-generation solar solutions entirely in the United States—from silicon foundations to perovskite innovations. Our technology enables applications ranging from space solar to utility-scale power generation, creating American-made solutions for a world facing growing energy challenges.

Swift Solar is on a journey to bring revolutionary clean-energy technology to market. We’re in it for the long haul, with support from world-class investors. Join our extraordinary team building the cutting-edge solar technology that will power the future.

 

A day in the life

As a Reliability Engineer at Swift, you’ll drive cell-package interactions and module-level reliability, addressing the unique challenges of a first-generation technology moving from concept through certification and towards manufacturing.

On a typical day, you might schedule and execute reliability tests on tandem mini-modules and full modules—spanning environmental, thermomechanical, and accelerated life tests such as damp heat, thermal cycling, UV, and outdoor exposure—then evaluate the results. You might perform failure analysis on tandem modules, design a non-standard accelerated stress protocol to reproduce a field failure, or coordinate third-party testing with external labs.

You’ll contribute a reliability perspective, collaborate with the Product Management team on lifetime modeling, and develop hypotheses you communicate clearly to the Materials R&D, Process Engineering, and Product Development teams. As an early hire, you’ll help shape how the reliability function operates as the team grows and interacts with every part of the company along the way.

You might be a good fit if you... 

  • Have 3–5 years of experience in PV module reliability, spanning from R&D to third-party validation and certification.
  • Have a demonstrated ability to diagnose failure mechanisms and translate findings into data-driven insights for cross-functional teams.
  • Have experience working with external testing labs to define and complete testing.
  • Have a solid understanding of PV cell and module device physics.
  • Have a proven ability to work well with cross-functional teams (R&D, Product Development, Engineering, Manufacturing), showing strong communication and empathy.
  • Are proficient in statistical analysis software (e.g., JMP) and the application of statistics to reliability analysis.

A strong candidate might bring one or more of the following…

  • Experience with more than one PV cell type.
  • Experience developing non-standard accelerated testing protocols for a first-generation technology.
  • Familiarity with reliability engineering tools (e.g., FMEA, 8D, RCA, DFR).
  • Experience sourcing reliability test equipment.
  • An understanding of why solving climate change is an urgent and critical challenge.
  • Genuine enthusiasm for the challenges that come with working at a startup.

The logistics

  • Compensation: Competitive package including salary, equity, and benefits
    • Expected Pay Range: $110,000 - $150,000 per year
    • The actual offer, reflecting total compensation and benefits, will be determined by factors such as relevant experience, skills, and other qualifications 
  • Ideal start date: July-August 2026
  • Job type: Full-time
  • Location: San Carlos, CA (Swift Solar HQ)

What you’ll love about Swift

  • Work with purpose: Join our mission to unlock the full potential of solar energy and make a global impact. 
  • Lead with innovation: Be part of an extraordinary team building cutting-edge solar technology - growth mindset; culture
  • Thrive with benefits: Have 100% of your monthly premiums for HMO / PPO group healthcare plan options and 75% of your dental and vision insurance premiums covered by us. Employees also benefit from 401(k) matching, clean commuter benefits, and meaningful equity. 
  • Invest in your career: You’ll grow your skills, your network, and your perspective at Swift. We’ll support you in attending conferences and taking online courses, as long as you share your new insights with the team.

We recognize that candidates from underrepresented backgrounds often hesitate to apply if they don’t meet all the criteria. If you’re excited about this role and believe you can contribute to our team, we encourage you to apply—even if you don’t meet every qualification listed. We're eager to meet people from all backgrounds, and your unique skills and experiences could be exactly what we need.

If you believe in our mission, but this isn’t the right job for you, please check out other career opportunities on our website and email us at careers@swiftsolar.com with any questions. And if you have a friend who would be a perfect fit, send them this link. Thanks!

Swift is an equal opportunity employer. We value an inclusive work environment and welcome team members of all backgrounds and perspectives.

Geothermal Innovation Engineering 

  • Design innovative geothermal heating and cooling solutions, evaluating detailed HVAC, fluid flow, and geothermal modeling for novel approaches.

title: Sr. Estimator
description:
Brightcore Energy provides end-to-end energy efficiency and clean energy measures to commercial, industrial, and institutional clients. We have the intellectual and financial capital to develop, implement, fund, operate, and maintain clean energy solutions. Our diverse solutions range from lighting, controls, geothermal heating and cooling, and other energy efficiency measures to renewable energy solutions such as solar and battery storage. We are about Building Energy Performance.

Summary/Primary Role:

We are seeking a skilled and detail-oriented Sr. Estimator to join our team. The Estimator will be responsible for analyzing project specifications and drawings to determine accurate cost estimates, collaborating with construction site teams, and utilizing specialized software to prepare detailed estimates. The ideal candidate will have a strong background in civil/site construction, superior estimating technique, excellent research and analytic skills, and the ability to communicate effectively with various stakeholders.

Principal Duties & Responsibilities:

  • Update costs as necessary based on new information and project scope changes..
  • Collaborate with construction site teams to gather necessary information for estimating.
  • Utilize software such as HeavyBid and Bluebeam to prepare detailed estimates.
  • Conduct thorough research on materials, labor, and equipment costs.
  • Prepare and submit competitive bids for projects.
  • Communicate effectively with contractors, suppliers, and project managers.
  • Participate in value engineering efforts to optimize project costs.
  • Perform neat, orderly and accurate takeoff and pricing with no supervision or direction.
  • Produce proposals and assemble bid packages required by the procuring entity.
  • Effectively and articulately communicate work product to the Director of Estimating.
  • Interact with project owners, engineers, subcontractors and vendors as needed.
  • Create complete and fully functional Excel spreadsheets and Word documents.
  • Perform other related duties as assigned by management.
  • All other duties and projects as assigned.

  • Experience with overall ground-up construction through completion for site/civil projects.
  • Proficiency in using HeavyBid, Blue Beam, Excel, Word.
  • Ability to learn new software platforms, if implemented.

As one of the Northeast’s fastest-growing residential energy companies, we help homeowners take control of their utility bills through solar, battery storage, and modern electrical upgrades.If you’re passionate about sustainability, love connecting with people, and want to make a tangible difference in your community, we want you to be part of the team!About the RoleWe are seeking experienced, driven Solar Sales Consultants who excel at building relationships and closing deals. title: Lead Installer
description: Join the Crew: Experienced Solar InstallersVenture Solar is expanding! We are looking for hardworking individuals on our installation team. The Solar Sales Energy Consultant role at Venture Solar is based in Westchester County, NY.   • Educate customers on system operations and financing sources to support purchase decisions

  • Base salary plus uncapped commission with on-target earnings of $100,000-$250,000

  • Health, dental, and vision insurance
  • Paid training

seoDescription:
Venture Solar is hiring an Experienced Solar Installer for residential projects with daily reporting to Youngstown, OH. The position centers on rooftop assembly and mechanical work for pitched-roof installations as part of the installation team. The role supports conduit and wiring tasks under electrician supervision.

Responsibilities

  • Install racking, mounting hardware, and solar modules on pitched roofs.
  • Handle the structural mounting and physical layout of the solar array.
  • Assist with conduit runs and basic wiring under the guidance of the Electrician.

  • Previous solar installation experience.
  • Ability to work at heights and on roofs.

  • Proficiency with power tools.
  • Valid clean driver’s license.

seoDescription:
The Retail Solar Sales Representative role at Venture Solar is located in Warwick, RI, and places the representative inside assigned Lowe's retail locations. The position focuses on engaging homeowners about solar energy, battery storage, and electrical upgrades, then scheduling in-home consultations. Representatives work a minimum of 30 hours per week on set shift patterns.

Responsibilities

  • Represent the company at designated Lowe's retail locations.
  • Engage homeowners in conversations about solar energy and home energy savings.
  • Qualify homeowners using basic solar eligibility criteria.
  • Educate customers on financial and environmental benefits of solar.
  • Schedule qualified homeowners for complimentary in-home consultations with an Energy Consultant.
  • Document customer information and appointments accurately.
  • Attend training sessions on products, promotions, and industry knowledge.
  • Meet appointment and performance goals.

Requirements

  • Reliable transportation to assigned Lowe's locations.
  • Ability to respond via phone, text, and email.
  • Previous experience in retail sales, customer service, lead generation, marketing, or hospitality preferred.

Benefits

  • On-target earnings of $55,000–$85,000 annually.
  • Competitive hourly pay plus uncapped commission.
  • Flexible scheduling with full-time options on shifts of 9 AM–3 PM or 3 PM–9 PM, either Fridays–Tuesdays or Wednesdays–Sundays.
  • Medical, dental, and vision insurance for eligible full-time employees.
  • Paid time off.
  • Paid training.
  • 401(k) retirement plan with company match.
  • Career advancement opportunities.

  • Maintain tool inventory and comply with tool management standards.

  • Respond promptly to customer service needs and maintain high standards of professionalism.

  • Possess valid government-issued identification acceptable for domestic air travel.

Requirements

  • 2 or more years of hands-on experience in electrical installation and service work.
  • Valid state driver's license with a clean driving record and ability to be insured.

  • Proficiency with computer applications and working knowledge of Microsoft Office (Outlook, Word, Excel, PowerPoint).
  • Ability to read and interpret electrical system plan sets.
  • Strong verbal and written communication skills.
  • Capability to manage multiple tasks and priorities effectively with strong time management and organizational skills.
  • Detail-oriented approach with focus on accuracy and quality workmanship.
  • Knowledge of and commitment to safety and security procedures.
  • Ability to accept direction, respond constructively to feedback, and demonstrate sound judgment.
  • Flexibility and adaptability in managing change, delays, and unexpected challenges.
  • Willingness to learn and apply various tools and techniques for electrical and rooftop work.
  • Ability to work outside regular business hours as needed.
  • Positive, collaborative team attitude with demonstrated integrity and strong work ethic.

Physical Requirements

  • Regularly lift, carry, and move up to 60 pounds of tools and equipment.
  • Frequently use hands to handle, grasp, and reach for tools and materials.
  • Operate hand and power tools safely and effectively.
  • Frequently stand, walk, climb, balance, and perform stooping, kneeling, crouching, and crawling movements.
  • Ascend and descend ladders on a regular basis.
  • Work on rooftops, uneven surfaces, at heights, and in confined spaces.
  • Work outdoors in various weather conditions with potential exposure to electrical hazards.

Hourly rate: $32–$46, based on experience, skills, and location. Compensation determined in accordance with applicable laws and internal equity.

seoDescription:
Enphase Energy, a global provider of solar, battery, and EV charging systems, is hiring a Field Service Technician in Richmond, VA to deliver on-site technical support to distribution and installation partners, servicing residential and commercial PV and storage systems.

About the Role

This position supports Enphase customers across an assigned territory, performing diagnostics, maintenance, and system updates on microinverter-based solar installations. The role involves significant travel (up to 50%), rooftop work, and direct coordination with homeowners and scheduling teams to resolve technical issues and ensure system reliability.

Responsibilities

  • Travel up to 50% within assigned territory, including out-of-state trips, overnight stays, and extended assignments up to two consecutive weeks; must possess valid domestic travel identification.
  • Service and maintain Enphase PV and battery storage systems at customer sites.
  • Conduct onsite testing, diagnostics, and performance evaluation of solar installations to identify system issues.
  • Perform microinverter maintenance and update the Enlighten monitoring system to document all changes.
  • Install, route, and manage conduit, copper piping, flexible tubing, and wiring as required.
  • Work regularly on rooftops and elevated structures, maintaining safety protocols at all heights.
  • Coordinate with scheduling teams and homeowners to arrange and manage site visits.
  • Complete solar maintenance reports and required documentation accurately and on schedule.
  • Operate standard field tools including drills, levels, squares, tape measures, and ladders.
  • Maintain tool inventory and adhere to tool management standards.
  • Follow all OSHA safety standards and company safety protocols; participate in regular safety training.
  • Respond promptly to customer needs and deliver high-level customer service throughout all interactions.
  • Train and mentor team members on proper installation techniques and industry best practices.
  • Review system designs and develop job-specific bills of materials (BOM/BOS).
  • Work independently with minimal supervision and drive continuous improvement in processes and workmanship standards.
  • Perform additional duties as assigned.

Requirements

  • High school diploma or GED.
  • 2+ years of experience in electrical installation and service.
  • Valid state driver's license with a clean driving record; must be insurable.
  • Commercial or residential electrical license.
  • NABCEP (North American Board of Certified Energy Practitioners) certification.
  • Proficiency with computer applications and working knowledge of Microsoft Office (Outlook, Word, Excel, PowerPoint).
  • Ability to read and interpret electrical plan sets.
  • Strong communication and presentation skills.
  • Strong time management and organizational skills; ability to manage multiple priorities effectively.
  • Detail-oriented with focus on accuracy and quality workmanship.
  • Knowledge of and commitment to safety and security procedures.
  • Ability to follow instructions and respond constructively to feedback.
  • Sound judgment and decision-making skills.
  • Flexible and adaptable; able to manage change, delays, and unexpected challenges.
  • Willingness to learn various tools and techniques related to electrical work and solar installation.
  • Positive team player with integrity, professionalism, and strong work ethic.
  • Ability to work outside regular business hours as needed.
  • Regularly lift and/or move up to 60 pounds of tools and equipment.
  • Frequently stand, walk, climb, balance, stoop, kneel, crouch, and crawl.
  • Ascend and descend ladders as required.
  • Perform work on rooftops, uneven surfaces, at heights, and in confined spaces.
  • Work outdoors in various weather conditions and tolerate exposure to electrical hazards.
  • Frequently use hands to handle, grasp, and reach; operate hand and power tools safely.

Benefits

This position offers an hourly rate of $23–$36, based on experience, skills, and location. The role is eligible for bonus, equity, and benefits, with final compensation determined in accordance with applicable laws and internal equity guidelines.

Enphase Energy, a leading provider of solar, battery, and EV charging products, seeks a Field Service Technician for on-site support across Massachusetts. This role involves diagnosing and servicing residential and commercial photovoltaic and battery storage systems for distribution and installation partners.

About the Role

You will provide field-based technical support and maintenance for Enphase PV and storage systems within an assigned territory. You will coordinate directly with homeowners and scheduling teams, perform system diagnostics and maintenance, complete required documentation, and work independently with minimal supervision.

Responsibilities

  • Service Enphase photovoltaic and battery storage systems within the assigned territory
  • Perform on-site testing and diagnostics to evaluate system performance and identify issues
  • Perform microinverter maintenance and update the Enlighten monitoring system to reflect all changes
  • Coordinate site visits and scheduling between customers and the Enphase support team
  • Work on rooftops and elevated structures, including installation and routing of conduit, copper piping, and flexible tubing
  • Pull and manage wiring as needed for system completion
  • Complete solar maintenance reports and required documentation accurately and in a timely manner
  • Utilize standard field tools including drills, levels, squares, tape measures, and ladders
  • Operate hand and power tools safely and effectively
  • Participate in regular safety training and adhere to all OSHA safety standards

  • Review system designs and develop job-specific bills of materials (BOM/BOS)
  • Identify opportunities to enhance processes, efficiency, and workmanship standards
  • Travel domestically as required, possessing valid identification acceptable for air travel
  • Work outside of regular business hours as needed

Requirements

  • High school diploma or GED
  • 2+ years of experience in electrical installation and service
  • Commercial or residential electrical license
  • NABCEP (North American Board of Certified Energy Practitioners) certification
  • Valid state driver's license with a clean driving record; must be insurable
  • Ability to read and interpret plan sets
  • Proficiency with computers and Microsoft Office (Outlook, Word, Excel, PowerPoint)
  • Strong communication and presentation skills

  • Detail-oriented with focus on accuracy and quality
  • Knowledge of and commitment to safety and security procedures
  • Ability to follow instructions and respond constructively to feedback
  • Sound judgment and decision-making skills
  • Flexible and adaptable; able to manage change, delays, and unexpected challenges
  • Willingness to learn and apply a variety of tools and techniques related to electrical work
  • Ability to work independently with minimal supervision

seoDescription:
RES is hiring a Lead Estimator for high-voltage substations and battery energy storage systems (BESS) projects. Based remotely, this role prepares detailed cost estimates for utility-scale renewable energy infrastructure, including substation construction up to 500kV, transmission components, and battery storage facilities. You will lead a team of estimators, manage complex multi-phase proposals, and coordinate with preconstruction managers and engineering teams on EPC (Engineer-Procure-Construct) and design-build projects.

Responsibilities

  • Prepare cost estimates for utility-grade substation, high-voltage transmission, and BESS projects, incorporating labor, material, equipment, and productivity factors
  • Lead and oversee multiple estimators on concurrent project proposals for Bid-Build and EPC construction RFPs
  • Review RFP documents to identify project scope, pricing elements, and technical requirements
  • Complete quantity take-offs from construction plans and design documents for substation systems up to 500kV
  • Compile indicative budgets in the absence of fully engineered documents
  • Manage vendor and subcontractor quote requests; evaluate responses for accuracy and schedule compliance
  • Coordinate with preconstruction managers on engineering support services and project schedule alignment
  • Maintain and apply current market data for construction, material, and soft costs; assess impacts from local labor, commodity pricing, and client specifications
  • Identify and document project risks in risk registers
  • Create bid proposal documents including Statements of Value (SOV), technical forms, and Assumptions/Clarifications/Exclusions (ACE) documents
  • Present project scope, risks, and cost estimates to operations and executive leadership
  • Collaborate with proposal strategists and preconstruction managers on final RFP responses
  • Compile and maintain historical cost data for project analysis

Requirements

  • Associate's degree in Engineering, Construction Management, or related field; OR high school diploma with 2+ years equivalent industry experience
  • 7+ years hands-on estimating experience for substation and high-voltage systems
  • 1+ year field-based construction experience
  • 2+ years leading a team of estimators on project pursuits or supervisory experience (preferred)
  • 2+ years estimating BESS DC and AC coupled systems (preferred)
  • Extensive experience with EPC and Balance of Plant (BOP) estimate structures for utility-scale renewable energy projects
  • Knowledge of design-build construction methods and production-based cost estimation
  • Ability to complete quantity take-offs from construction plans and geotechnical reports
  • Proficiency with Blue Beam or Adobe for quantity take-off work
  • Experience with HCSS HeavyBid or similar estimating software
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Outlook, Excel, Word, Project, OneNote, Teams, and SharePoint
  • Ability to evaluate site conditions and develop competitive estimates based on labor, equipment, and material resources
  • Ability to travel 5–15% as required
  • Pre-employment background check and drug screening required

Benefits

  • Medical, dental, and vision coverage
  • Health Savings Account with employer contribution
  • Flexible Spending Accounts
  • 4× salary basic life insurance and voluntary life insurance
  • Short- and long-term disability coverage
  • Accident, hospital, and critical illness insurance
  • 401(k) plan with 6% company match
  • 4 weeks paid time off and 10 paid holidays
  • Tuition reimbursement and green car reimbursement
  • Volunteer and charity matching
  • Paid parental leave and paid sabbatical leave
  • Employee referral bonus
  • Employee discounts and wellness programs
  • Wellness reimbursement
  • Position is bonus eligible
  • Salary range: $142,000–$178,000 based on education, qualifications, experience, and location

  • Operate company vehicle safely in all conditions and commit to short- or long-term remote site assignments.
