We are committed to building a workplace where everyone feels heard and respected, and extending our culture of care so that every individual can reach their full potential. We want you to have a sense of belonging and feel valued for your contributions and the perspectives you bring.

\u00A0

Summary:\u00A0

The Sr. Engineer IV - Solar Engineering provides solar PV performance and design expertise on utility-scale solar and solar plus storage projects during the development, design, construction, and commissioning phases.

\u00A0

This role will be hybrid requiring a minimum of 3 days in office.

\u00A0

Requirements:\u00A0\u00A0\u00A0

  • Serves as a lead Solar Engineering subject matter expert for internal departments, including development, procurement, construction, commissioning, and engineering (civil, electrical, SCADA, and engineering delivery).
  • Leads the evaluation and resolution of complex technical issues with clients, developers, engineers, procurement, subcontractors, and construction. Communicates material risks and recommendations to leadership.
  • Drafts, reviews, and approves contracts, exhibits, scopes of work, and technical documentation related to design, energy yields, commissioning, testing, and performance.
  • Leads analysis of plant and equipment performance using SCADA, MET, inverter, tracker, meter, and DC collection data to identify underperformance, data-quality issues, and likely root causes.
  • Develops and maintains engineering data structures, equipment hierarchies, mappings, and validation workflows that connect design, commissioning, SCADA, and performance information.
  • Leads technical roles with clients, internal leadership, and procurement on technical items that inform commercial design decisions related to risk management.
  • Coordinates engineering priorities, assignments, subconsultant activities, and progress to maintain project schedules, quality requirements, and conformance with contract documents. Leads technical feedback to clients and subcontractors based on the review of external design documentation, including design basis, overall site plans, energy models, contractual exhibits, and performance test results.
  • Works closely with clients and construction teams to guarantee delivery of a quality PV system that meets contractual expectations.
  • Generates and responds to design RFIs related to design and project performance.
  • Leads the creation and continuous improvement of team templates, tools, processes, scripts, calculators, visualizations, technical specifications, analysis methodologies, test procedures, and standardization and automation of workflows.
  • Provides leadership, coaching, and mentoring to the solar engineering team.
  • Coordinates with Development on preliminary layouts, technology assessments, and basis of design. Drafts, reviews, and approves standard processes that impact team templates and workflow.
  • Attends work regularly and punctually, as scheduled or expected.
  • Complies with Employee Handbook, Code of Conduct, and Company Policies & Procedures.

\u00A0

Additional Responsibilities:

  • Presents, supports, and leads-by-example with a safety and quality-oriented attitude.
  • Provides support to construction during the construction and commissioning phases.
  • Reviews work instructions periodically to ensure compliance with industry and client standards.
  • Develops new methods and standards for Group design activities.

Safety:

  • Follows safety and security procedures and determines appropriate action.\u00A0 Reports potentially unsafe conditions and uses materials and equipment properly.

\u00A0Qualifications:

  • Bachelor's degree in Engineering or a related field of study required. Master\u2019s degree preferred.
  • 8 or more years of progressive experience, including utility-scale PV engineering and technical expertise related to site feasibility, energy modeling, major equipment selection, and site layout is required.
  • Ability to travel domestically and internationally 5 to 15% required.
  • Must possess a valid Driver\u2019s license.\u00A0
  • Strong oral and written skills.
  • Technical writing: Drafting reports, papers, and assessments to a high standard
  • Ability to communicate issues and to communicate complex technical issues to peers across internal departments, suppliers and clients, and a non-technical audience as required.
  • Clear and concise writing.
  • Negotiation skills.
  • Interpersonal skills, including the ability to work well in a team environment.
  • Ability to organize and prioritize work. Project management and time management skills, including balancing multiple Projects under tight deadlines and establishing and maintaining good relations with internal team members and clients.
  • Ability to think analytically.
  • Advanced /Expert level Knowledge in:
  • PV plant performance analysis, energy modeling, expected-versus-actual evaluation, uncertainty analysis, and regression methods.
  • Engineering review of equipment hierarchies, design drawings, SCADA tags, data mappings, and large time-series datasets to support performance diagnostics and project decision-making.
  • PV Plant Capacity and Operational Testing\u00A0
  • National and international codes and standards applicable to PV design, construction, commissioning, and testing, including NEC, NFPA, ASTM, IEC, IBC, ASCE, and NETA requirements. PV Electrical Design\u00A0
  • Design for Constructability
  • Installation and Application
  • Solar Industry best practices
  • Major equipment specification, selection, and application, including modules, inverters, trackers, MET stations, meters, SCADA systems, and DC collection equipment.
  • Ability to lead the team members and advise clients regarding performance analysis, solar Project design/development, module/inverter/tracking system technology selection.
  • Ability to lead the team on risks and opportunities for incorporating new technologies into PV designs and performance modeling.
  • Experience with Design Software:
  • Autodesk AutoCAD Civil 3D
  • PV simulation software PVsyst,SAM, PVfarm, and Solar Resource Compass
  • Global Mapper or GIS software
  • Python-based data analysis and automation, including processing, validating, visualizing, and reporting large engineering and time-series datasets.Statistics including uncertainty analysis and regression models.
  • MS Office (Excel, Word, Outlook, etc.)\u00A0
  • Functional competencies include accountability, attention to detail, customer focus, prioritization, and continuous improvement.

\u00A0

\u00A0

Anticipated base salary range:\u00A0 $127,000 \u2013 $158,000

\u00A0

The final agreed upon compensation is based on individual education, qualifications, experience, and work location. This position is bonus eligible.

\u00A0

RES offers benefits that are effective first day of employment. These benefits include the following:

\u00A0

  • Medical, Dental and Vision
  • Health Savings Account with employer contribution
  • Flexible Spending Accounts
  • 4x pay Basic Life and Voluntary Life
  • Short and Long Term Disability
  • Accident, Hospital, and Critical Illness
  • 401 (k) plan with 6% company match
  • 4 weeks Paid Time Off (PTO) and 10 Paid Holidays
  • Tuition Reimbursement and Green Car Reimbursement
  • Volunteer and Charity Matching
  • Paid Parental Leave and Paid Sabbatical Leave
  • Employee Referral Bonus
  • Employee Discounts and Wellness programs
  • Wellness Reimbursement

\u00A0

Physical requirements and environment:

\u00A0

The work environment and physical demands characteristics are representative of those the employee encounters while performing the essential functions of this job.\u00A0 Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

\u00A0

Rarely: Climbing, crouching, kneeling, pulling/pushing/lifting between 5-15lbs., and stooping are required.\u00A0

\u00A0

Freedom Solar Power seeks Commercial Solar Installers to deploy photovoltaic systems on commercial projects across the United States. Based in Austin, TX, this role involves extensive travel—approximately 90% of the time, typically in 4-week assignments with occasional weekend commitments.

About the Role

You will install commercial-scale solar PV systems ranging from 10kW to 1MW capacity as part of dedicated installation crews. This position requires significant on-site presence at project locations nationwide.

Responsibilities

  • Install photovoltaic modules, racking systems, and electrical components on commercial rooftop and ground-mount installations
  • Perform DC and AC wiring for solar arrays and interconnection points
  • Work collaboratively with crew members to meet project timelines and safety standards
  • Maintain tools and equipment in working condition
  • Follow blueprints, engineering specifications, and installation best practices

Requirements

  • Prior experience in construction, electrical work, or solar installation
  • Physical ability to work at heights, lift heavy materials, and perform manual labor in outdoor conditions
  • Willingness to travel extensively and work away from home for multi-week periods
  • Ability to work weekends when project schedules require
  • Valid driver's license and reliable transportation
  • High school diploma or equivalent

Benefits

Freedom Solar Power provides competitive compensation and the opportunity to work on large-scale energy infrastructure projects with a Texas-based company operating nationwide.

description:

Austin, TX   Full-Time   On-Site
Some jobs pull wire. This one powers an entire revolution — and puts you at the center of it.
Freedom Power was born when Freedom Solar and Freedom HVAC joined forces to become Texas's complete whole-house energy company. We don't just install solar panels. We hand homeowners the keys to something bigger: control over their energy, their bills, and their future. We call it Energy Empowerment, and it's not a tagline — it's the reason we show up every day.
If you've got electrical mastery in your hands and hustle in your blood, this is your shot to do more than run conduit. You'll walk into homes as a skilled technician, execute precise solar electrical installations, upgrade service panels, and bring whole-home energy systems to life. Solar, batteries, generators — you'll be the hands-on expert making Energy Empowerment real, one installation at a time. Every job is local, and you'll roll in your own company truck.
Competitive pay and performance bonuses on top.
What You'll Do
Install electrical equipment and circuits, complete DC conduit runs, and interconnect PV systems to existing residential services.
Upgrade customer electrical service as needed — main panel upgrades and meter bases, external disconnects, and code compliance assessments.
Perform system testing — voltage, amperage, and power tests for each installation.
Complete commissioning and inspection checklists with precision.

description:
About Us
 
Solar Landscape is the leading commercial rooftop solar developer in the U.S. Only 4% of commercial rooftops host solar today — we’re changing that, fast. Commercial rooftop solar is the fastest, smartest way to build new clean power — delivering megawatts of generation in months, not years, and powering America’s energy and future right where it’s needed most. By turning rooftops into local power plants, we’re reshaping how — and how fast — energy gets built in the U.S.
 
Recognized as the #1 Distributed Generation Developer by New Project Media, the #1 National Commercial Rooftop Solar Developer by Solar Power World, and winner of the U.S. Department of Energy’s Grand Prize for Clean Energy, Solar Landscape is defining the future of energy generation in America.

We move fast, solve hard problems, and take our work seriously — but never ourselves. We value clear thinking, accountability, and execution. At the same time, we’re collaborative by default, and believe the best work happens when people enjoy working together. Our team is made up of smart, grounded people who show up for each other — whether that’s troubleshooting a system design or catching up over lunch.
 
If you’re looking to do meaningful work in a high-performance environment — and be part of the team reshaping how energy gets built in the U.S. — we’d love to meet you.

We are seeking a Mechanical Engineer to join our optics team. The team owns the full design-to-commissioning lifecycle for our tracker hardware: precision optical elements and the structures that position them, solar tracking architectures, structural analysis under wind and gravity loading, and the instrumentation that turns prototypes into measured systems. The core problem is deceptively hard: hold optical precision on a large structure that moves all day, outdoors, under wind, gravity, and thermal swings, all at a cost that can scale to thousands of units.

At its core, this is a builder's role. Your main focus will be optomechanical assemblies: designing, fabricating, assembling, aligning, and testing the hardware that positions optical elements (lenses and mirrors, for example) on our trackers. The full loop is yours: idea to CAD to built hardware to test data, learning from what breaks and turning the next revision around in days, not months. You will spend most of your time hands-on in the shop, at the assembly bench, and on the test stand. The work spans structures, optics, precision assembly, sensors, and the code and AI agents that read them. This is an AI-native team: agents already drive our simulation campaigns and babysit our long-running tests, and we expect you to work at that level from day one. Everything around your hardware that is code, calculation, or documentation is something an agent should be running for you. Expect real ownership, a steep learning curve, and senior engineers who will review your work closely and push you to grow fast.

title: Electrical/Solar Engineer - Utility Scale
description: Description Pure Power is seeking an experienced Electrical Engineer to design and produce construction documents for utility-scale solar PV and battery energy storage (BESS) projects of 50 MW and larger. Pure Power is an engineering firm specializing in complex, high-profile renewable energy projects across North America. This is an exciting opportunity to work on industry-leading renewable energy projects while collaborating with a highly experienced engineering team. The ideal candidate is technically strong, detail-oriented, and passionate about delivering high-quality engineering solutions for utility-scale generation facilities. About Pure PowerPure Power is an engineering firm specializing in designing big, challenging, and high-profile Solar PV systems. As a full-service engineering firm, we create the electrical and structural drawings and calculation packages for bidding, permits and construction, as well as supporting the lead up to the full engineering drawings, primarily interconnection support and electrical/structural feasibility studies.Those that join the company have an opportunity to:Work in a fast growing, exciting, & innovative industryHave a career with purpose and impact on the environmentContribute to the best and largest firm in the solar industry with a great reputation built over the past 10 yearsTake pride in the fact that our services really are the best in the industry. There is no “fake it until you make it” here Responsibilities Support the design and engineering of utility-scale solar PV and BESS projects under the guidance of senior engineers. Perform electrical engineering design tasks including: Overall system layouts Equipment selection and technical specifications Single-line and three-line diagrams Medium-voltage AC and DC cable sizing and routing SCADA and communication system design Grounding system design Protection, control, and wiring diagrams Underground collection system and trench layouts Perform engineering calculations with training and review, including voltage drop, cable ampacity, conduit fill, equipment loading, and related analyses. Prepare complete construction drawing packages using AutoCAD. Coordinate with internal project teams and support communication with clients, utilities, permitting agencies, contractors, equipment manufacturers, and consultants as needed. Support projects during construction by helping respond to Requests for Information (RFIs), reviewing equipment submittals, researching field issues, and participating in site visits when needed. Balance work on multiple project tasks while communicating progress, questions, and priorities with project leads. Learn to break down engineering problems into practical design solutions with support from senior engineers and project managers. Ensure designs comply with applicable codes, industry standards, client requirements, and company quality procedures. Maintain compliance with company safety policies and applicable industry and regulatory standards. Participate in internal design reviews and quality assurance/quality control (QA/QC) processes to develop sound engineering judgment. Perform other duties as assigned. Requirements Required Qualifications Bachelor's degree in Electrical Engineering or a related engineering discipline. 1-3 years of relevant internship, co-op, academic project, or professional experience related to electrical engineering, solar PV, power systems, or renewable energy. Exposure to AutoCAD or similar drafting/design software; experience with construction documents, layer management, Xrefs, blocks, plotting, or file management is preferred. Basic familiarity with the National Electrical Code (NEC), electrical safety concepts, and applicable industry standards, with a willingness to continue learning. Foundational understanding of electrical circuits, power systems, and engineering design principles. Proficiency with Microsoft Office applications, including Excel and Word. Strong analytical, organizational, and problem-solving skills with attention to detail. Clear written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to ask questions, document work, and collaborate with engineering teams. Ability to manage assigned tasks, follow direction, and communicate workload or schedule risks early. Ability to read and interpret engineering drawings, technical specifications, and other engineering documentation. Preferred Qualifications Engineer-in-Training (EIT) certification or interest in pursuing professional licensure. Internship, co-op, academic, or entry-level experience with solar PV, BESS, power systems, or renewable energy projects. Experience designing Battery Energy Storage Systems (BESS). Familiarity with PVSyst, CYMCAP, ETAP, or similar engineering software. Exposure to electrical studies such as cable ampacity, voltage drop, grounding, short-circuit, or load flow analyses. Interest in utility interconnection requirements and utility-scale project development. NABCEP certification. LocationThis position will be based out of our exciting Kansas City, KS area office with the flexibility to work a hybrid in-office and remotely weekly schedule. We also provide a parking spot for the days when an employee wishes to drive to the office and for those that utilize public transportation, we will cover the costs associated with traveling to and from the office.Salary Range$85,000- 120,000 AnnuallyCompensation and BenefitsWe offer a competitive salary commensurate with experience. We pay 100% of our employee medical, dental, and vision benefits costs, provide paid leaves, offer 401k matching, commuter benefits, sick time and paid time off, internal & external professional development opportunities and much more! Purpose 

Support the advancement of utility-scale solar and BESS projects through all phases of electrical design by providing technical oversight, coordination, and review of electrical deliverables. Ensure electrical design quality, constructability, code compliance, and alignment with project scope, schedule, cost, customer requirements, and execution objectives. 

Responsibilities 

  • Lead the progression of electrical design from preliminary design through IFC and construction phases, ensuring deliverables are completed in sequence to support project schedules. 
  • Review and validate electrical design outputs, including conductor schedules, equipment specifications and layouts, monitoring and communication systems, grounding, string layouts, voltage drop calculations, and related electrical deliverables. 
  • Serve as a Subject Matter Expert (SME) for electrical design and constructability, including DC collection, AC collection, MV systems, equipment selection, grounding, monitoring, communications, and electrical code compliance. 
  • Provide technical guidance to internal teams, external engineering partners, vendors, and subcontractors. 
  • Collaborate with Engineering, Preconstruction, Estimating, Procurement, and Operations teams to align electrical design with project execution, procurement strategy, installation sequencing, and cost expectations. 
  • Conduct structured electrical design reviews at key milestones, including 30%, 90%, IFC, and construction-phase revisions. 
  • Identify risks, gaps, and inconsistencies in electrical design packages and drive resolution with internal and external stakeholders. 
  • Evaluate electrical design decisions for constructability, installation efficiency, equipment availability, code compliance, customer requirements, and cost impacts. 
  • Interface with customers, developers, AHJs, external engineering firms, regulatory agencies, vendors, and subcontractors to align on electrical design approach, technical requirements, and compliance expectations. 
  • Support permitting and regulatory coordination by ensuring electrical designs comply with NEC requirements, customer specifications, jurisdictional requirements, and applicable standards. 
  • Provide technical support during construction, including review of field issues, design clarifications, RFI responses, change impacts, and resolution of electrical installation or constructability concerns. 
  • Manage and maintain project electrical files, drawings, documents, records, and design information in company systems. 
  • Support continuous improvement of electrical design processes, review standards, templates, and lessons learned to improve consistency, quality, and execution across utility-scale projects. 
  • Balance multiple complex projects and design priorities while maintaining a high level of accuracy, accountability, and execution. 
  • Travel to project sites as needed to review existing conditions, support design coordination, assist with field issue resolution, and validate electrical systems or installation requirements.

  • 1–2 years of experience in solar or power systems design

  • Strong communication and organizational skills
  • Valid driver’s license and clean driving history

title: Solar Electrical Technician - Eastern Shore
description: Come join our growing team and make your mark on renewable energy as a Solar Electrical Technician! The Solar Electrical Technician I is directly responsible for electrical, telecommunication, and mechanical maintenance activities, to include testing and repair of all major and balance-of-system components utilized in solar photovoltaic (“PV”) power generation. This is considered the entry level on our team of technicians. This individual will receive comprehensive on-the-job, classroom-based, and online training pertaining to all aspects of PV fundamentals, installation, testing, maintenance, and repair of small commercial and large utility-scale PV systems. As training milestones are completed, the Technician will become qualified to perform and supervise more and more maintenance activities which will lead to a range of future growth opportunities within Strata. If you have electrical experience and have an interest in furthering your solar maintenance capabilities, please keep reading! Responsibilities Safety First! All of our Technicians are champions of safety at our PV plants. Ensure that all peers and subcontractors demonstrate safe work practices in accordance with OSHA, NFPA, state and local codes, and Strata Solar Services safety policies and procedures in the performance of regional plant maintenance activities. Technicians must demonstrate a strong understanding of these applicable policies after training & before being authorized to begin work activities on site. Develop a strong working knowledge of electrical theory in order to understand electrical design drawings as well as quickly identify & escalate electrical safety hazards. Perform scheduled and unscheduled plant maintenance activities in the assigned region at the direction of your Regional Manager with the objective of optimizing plant performance and plant operating efficiency, as well as preserving warranties on plant equipment exceeding $100 million in value. Work on and around energized electrical parts in compliance with all electrical codes and company policies as instructed during training sessions. Use multimeter, low resistance Ohm-meter, PV Analyzer, IR thermometer, IR camera, and hand-held irradiance meter as well as a variety of hand tools in the performance of electrical maintenance work. Supervise Lockout/Tagout activities to ensure work is always performed in compliance with intended electrical isolation procedures. Troubleshoot & diagnose common Direct Current (“DC”) faults within the PV plant. Complete and submit all assigned inspection and testing data as required. Create excellent, detailed documentation within our work ticketing software system so that we can always deliver professional reporting to our customers. Perform acceptance inspections on newly assigned PV plants in the assigned region. Pull data files, troubleshoot communications issues, and maneuver monitoring software using a PC or Tablet. Provision replacement devices and upload/share photos via service tickets. Conduct basic networking, such as changing IP addresses on laptop to connect with equipment. Other duties as assigned. Qualifications Education and/or Work Experience Requirements: Minimum three (3) years experience working with energized AC or DC systems or other relevant experience. Ability to demonstrate basic working knowledge of electrical theory & PV power generating system fundamentals. Aptitude for learning and understanding operation of various testing equipment, tools and procedures utilized in the maintenance of PV power generation systems. Ability to collaborate and coordinate well with peer Technicians and other personnel, vendors, and subcontractors. Proficiency with MS Office applications to include but not limited to MS Word and Excel, as well as an ability to learn new computer programs without difficulty. Ability to operate in a professional workmanlike manner consistent with the organization’s policies, procedures and vision. Physical Requirements/Work Environment: Must be able to work in an outdoor environment and be able to travel occasionally to remote project sites. Must be able to sit, stand or walk for the entire duration of a shift. Must be able to stoop, kneel or bend. Must be able to lift, push or pull 50 lbs overhead repeatedly. 20/40 vision in each eye, with or without correction and ability to distinguish colors. Ability to wear full complement of Personal Protective Equipment (PPE) ar required. Must have the ability to travel, work on-call during off-shift hours and weekends. Perform technical review of I&C and SCADA design documentation from third party vendors including, but not limited to, SCADA integrators, substation vendors, and tracker and inverter suppliers. Specify components to meet project requirements and work with vendors and clients to develop solutions. Review and prepare bills of materials and control narratives for I&C systems. Work with other engineering disciplines to coordinate, develop, document, and execute control solutions. Remotely support commissioning of I&C systems, and interface with Strata field personnel to ensure project requirements are satisfied expeditiously. Engineer solutions for Strata’s repower projects to replace obsolete field equipment. Provide technical / commercial input to support Strata business development. Develop / coordinate RFPs, and review / evaluate proposals from vendors. Education and/or Work Experience Requirements: BS in Electrical Engineering, or equivalent, from an ABET accredited university. Minimum 2 -3 years relevant work experience. Experience with renewable energy (PV or BESS) projects desired but not necessary. Physical Requirements/Work Environment: Work is performed in an office environment and in the field. title: BESS Field Technician
description: The PPM BESS Field Technician supports the safe, reliable, and efficient operation and maintenance of utility-scale Battery Energy Storage System (BESS) facilities and associated balance-of-plant equipment. The Technician performs preventive and corrective maintenance, inspections, troubleshooting, repairs, testing, alarm and event review, and maintenance documentation across electrical, controls, communications/SCADA, auxiliary, and mechanical systems. The position may be filled at different experience levels based on demonstrated competency, technical knowledge, electrical qualifications, and ability to work independently. Work involving energized equipment, medium-voltage systems, or switching may only be performed by personnel who are specifically trained, qualified, and authorized. Essential Duties and Responsibilities: Perform work in accordance with OSHA requirements, NFPA 70E principles, applicable regulations, and Strata safety policies and procedures. Participate in effective job briefings, identify and communicate hazards, use required PPE, and exercise stop-work responsibility when unsafe conditions exist. Apply Lockout/Tagout, electrical isolation, and energized-work controls within the limits of individual training, qualification, and authorization. Perform scheduled and unscheduled preventive and corrective maintenance on BESS equipment and associated balance-of-plant systems. Inspect, maintain, troubleshoot, and support repair of battery systems, Power Conversion Systems, switchgear, transformers, auxiliary AC and DC systems, HVAC, fire detection and suppression interfaces, controls, protection systems, SCADA, networking, and communications equipment. Review alarms, event records, operating trends, and equipment status to identify abnormal conditions, isolate faults, and support safe restoration. Troubleshoot electrical, mechanical, controls, communications, and balance-of-plant issues using OEM diagnostic tools, technical documentation, monitoring systems, and electrical test equipment. Interpret single-line diagrams, schematics, wiring and control drawings, procedures, and OEM manuals to support maintenance and safe work planning. Use appropriate tools and test equipment, including multimeters, insulation-resistance testers, low-resistance ohmmeters, clamp meters, and thermal-imaging equipment. Verify repairs and document as-found and as-left equipment conditions before returning equipment to service. Write and perform switching orders when qualified and authorized under Strata’s switching program to establish electrical isolation boundaries and support safe restoration. Support commissioning, recommissioning, functional testing, point-to-point verification, system modifications, and punch-list resolution. Coordinate maintenance and troubleshooting activities with supervisors, Remote Operations, engineering, OEMs, vendors, contractors, utilities, and other support personnel. Support vendor and contractor field activities, including work-area coordination, safety alignment, scope verification, and collection of service and closeout documentation. Maintain accurate and timely CMMS records, including work orders, inspection results, test records, photographs, material usage, corrective actions, and equipment status. Collect technical information required for warranty claims, engineering review, recurring-failure analysis, and contractual reporting. Maintain assigned tools, test equipment, spare parts, materials, and company property in serviceable condition. Provide task guidance and technical support to less-experienced technicians or contractors when assigned and qualified. Support emergency response and Emergency Action Plan activities within assigned training and responsibilities. Maintain site readiness, equipment-area cleanliness, and housekeeping. Participate in on-call coverage and travel to other operating facilities as required. Perform other duties as assigned. Environmental Responsibilities:• Participate in environmental compliance programs, inspections, and administrative recordkeeping.• Support and maintaining compliance with Resource Conservation and Recovery Act (RCRA) and Department of Transportation (DOT) regulations.• Assist with environmental incident response and mitigation activities as required. Education and/or Work Experience Requirements:• High School Diploma, GED, or equivalent.• Four (4) or more years of experience in utility-scale PV, BESS sites (balance-of-plant/controls/communications), substations, or equivalent industrial electrical/power systems with directly transferable skills.• Strong knowledge of OSHA requirements, NFPA 70E principles, NESC awareness, and MV safety practices applicable to the work scope.• Valid driver’s license.• Working knowledge of AC/DC electrical theory, three-phase power systems, and energy storage system fundamentals appropriate to the role.• Ability to read and understand electrical drawings/schematics and OEM manuals.• Proficiency with test equipment and tools used in electrical maintenance (multimeters, insulation testers, IR camera/thermography tools, etc.).• Proficiency with CMMS platforms, maintenance reporting tools, and ability to learn additional software/platforms as required.• Strong communication and interpersonal skills; ability to coordinate with technicians, supervisors, vendors, subcontractors, and support teams. Physical Requirements/Work Environment:• Must be able to work in an outdoor environment for extended periods of time.• Must have the ability to travel for extended duration to remote project sites.• Must be able to stoop, kneel or bend.• Must be able to lift, push or pull 50 lbs. overhead repeatedly.• 20/40 vision in each eye, with or without correction and ability to distinguish colors.• Ability to wear full complement of Personal Protective Equipment (PPE• Must have the ability to travel, work on-call during off-shift hours and weekends. You will serve as the electrical foreperson for assigned residential solar installation projects, directly supervising a crew of 3 to 6 installers. This is a working field position where you'll manage safety, quality, customer service, and productivity while actively participating in PV system installation. Sunrun's vertically integrated model provides opportunities to develop skills across sales qualification, installation, inspection, and service work, which can help reduce seasonal downtime and strengthen job security.

  • Maintain accurate project documentation, photo requirements, and time sheet records

  • Identify and resolve crew performance issues and recommend solutions
  • Provide constructability feedback to management and maintain open communication lines
  • Perform service calls and emergency work as needed

  • High school diploma or equivalent

  • Current knowledge of the National Electrical Code (NEC); must maintain an up-to-date NEC code book

seoDescription:
Sunrun is hiring a Certified Electrician 1 based in Santa Fe Springs, CA. The role centers on electrical work for residential solar arrays and battery storage systems, including interconnections to the grid and main panel upgrades. The position includes 5% travel and participation in the company's incentive program.

Responsibilities

  • Lead installation of electrical systems connecting solar arrays to residential grid power.
  • Verify that all electrician work meets workmanship standards and complies with NEC and local codes.
  • Complete assigned solar battery storage installations.
  • Troubleshoot system issues and resolve electrical problems.
  • Plan and perform main panel upgrades safely.
  • Coordinate with branch teams and homeowners on system upgrades or repairs.
  • Coordinate with local inspectors to meet requirements.
  • Perform additional duties as assigned.

Requirements

  • Electrical installation and repair experience.
  • Experience wiring systems up to 600 VDC and 480 VAC.
  • Working knowledge of replacing residential electrical services and distribution panels preferred.
  • Valid Journeyman License or Electrician Certification meeting local and state requirements.
  • Clean driving record and ability to pass a driving background check.
  • Minimum age of 21 with a valid driver's license.
  • Ability to lift and transport materials up to 50 pounds frequently and up to 100 pounds with assistance.
  • Ability to work on rooftops with various angles, requiring frequent bending, twisting, squatting, climbing, kneeling, crawling, and balancing.
  • Ability to work in confined spaces such as attics, basements, and crawl spaces.
  • Ability to work outdoors in extreme heat, cold, wet conditions, humidity, and excessive noise.
  • Ability to perform fine motor tasks including grasping and pinching.
  • Ability to use ladders, fall protection harnesses, and other personal protective equipment safely.
  • Ability to wear heavy protective equipment such as arc flash suits, gloves, and face shields.
  • Ability to maintain balance on roofs and elevated areas.
  • Ability to work in direct sun or low-light conditions.
  • Ability to walk on rafters, roof tiles, and shingles without damage.

title: Senior Quality Inspector
description: Job Overview: The Senior Quality Inspector serves as the technical lead for manufacturing quality inspection activities within Premier PV’s Dallas manufacturing operations. This is a hands-on, production-floor position responsible for performing dimensional, visual, and electrical inspections of incoming materials, in-process assemblies, and finished products. The Senior Quality Inspector interprets prints, manufacturing drawings, diagrams, wire cards, and inspection criteria; trains and provides technical guidance to new hires and other Quality Inspectors; and documents inspection activity in Smartsheet and other applicable systems. This is a non-exempt individual contributor role and does not carry formal supervisory responsibility. Company Overview: Premier PV is a leading manufacturer of solar electrical balance of systems solutions and renewable energy products, dedicated to advancing sustainable energy technologies. Our mission is to provide innovative, efficient, and reliable products that enhance solar energy systems. Key Responsibilities: • Serve as the technical lead for manufacturing quality inspection activities and help coordinate daily inspection priorities, workload, and coverage. • Work directly on the production floor to perform incoming, in-process, and final inspections using approved drawings, specifications, work instructions, control plans, checklists, and acceptance criteria. • Conduct visual, dimensional, and electrical inspections of materials, components, subassemblies, and finished products using appropriate measurement and test equipment. • Interpret engineering prints, manufacturing drawings, diagrams, wire cards, bills of material, tolerances, and quality requirements to determine product conformance. • Provide hands-on training, technical guidance, and mentoring to newly hired and less-experienced Quality Inspectors. • Promote consistent inspection methods, documentation practices, and adherence to established quality requirements. • Enter and maintain accurate inspection results, quality records, production-floor findings, and other required information in Smartsheet and applicable systems. • Identify, document, segregate, and communicate nonconforming materials or products to the appropriate team members. • Support initial review and basic analysis of quality issues, including gathering relevant inspection information and assisting with containment or corrective actions when needed. • Support calibration schedules, equipment identification and traceability, and the proper handling of measuring or test equipment found to be out of calibration. • Collaborate with Production, Engineering, Supply Chain, and other departments to communicate and resolve manufacturing quality concerns. • Assist with identifying recurring defects or inspection trends and recommend practical improvements when appropriate. • Provide support during internal or external audits when needed. • Promote a safe, organized, and quality-focused work environment and perform other duties as assigned to support production needs. Benefits and Pay: • Competitive hourly compensation based on qualifications, experience, work location, and other job-related factors. • Generous benefits including paid holidays, PTO, sick leave as required by applicable state regulations, medical, dental, and vision insurance, FSA/HSA options, disability coverages, and a 401(k) plan with matching contributions. The compensation range is based on a full-time schedule. Premier PV reserves the right to ultimately pay more or less than the posted range and offer additional benefits and other compensation, depending on circumstances not related to an applicant’s sex or other status protected by local, state, or federal law. Work Environment and Physical Requirements: This position works primarily on the production floor in a manufacturing environment and may be exposed to moving mechanical equipment, electrical components, noise, dust, fumes, varying temperatures, and other conditions typical of an active production facility. Required personal protective equipment must be worn, and all safety rules and procedures must be followed. • Must comply with safety requirements, which may include being clean-shaven when required for respirator use, wearing long sleeves, and wearing steel-toe or other required protective footwear. • Must be able to stand and walk for extended periods and frequently use hands and arms to handle, inspect, position, or test materials and components. • Must be able to bend, stoop, kneel, crouch, crawl, climb, and maintain balance on ladders, scaffolding, and stairways, as the work requires. • Must be able to work at heights or in confined spaces, including towers, vessels, or excavations, when assigned and properly trained. • Must be able to lift and carry up to 50 pounds; assistance must be used for heavier loads. • Must be able to visually inspect product details and distinguish conditions necessary to determine conformance, with or without reasonable accommodation. • Must be able to pass a drug screen and background check. Required Skills and Knowledge: • High school diploma or GED required; technical school coursework or a related certification preferred. • 5+ years of hands-on manufacturing quality inspection or closely related experience preferred. Candidates with three to four years of strong, directly related experience may also be considered. • Demonstrated experience performing inspections directly within an active manufacturing or production-floor environment. • Experience training, mentoring, or providing technical guidance to new or less-experienced employees. • Demonstrated proficiency with inspection and measurement tools such as calipers, micrometers, gauges, multimeters, and other equipment applicable to the work. • Ability to read and interpret engineering drawings, specifications, tolerances, diagrams, wire cards, work instructions, and inspection plans. • Working knowledge of incoming, in-process, and final inspection methods, nonconformance controls, calibration requirements, and equipment traceability. • Basic knowledge of quality issue analysis, root-cause concepts, corrective actions, and manufacturing quality systems. • Ability to accurately enter, maintain, and communicate inspection information using Smartsheet and other standard computer or quality systems. • Ability to provide technical direction and mentorship, prioritize work, communicate expectations, and collaborate effectively across departments. • Strong problem-solving, documentation, organization, and attention-to-detail skills. • Ability to work with limited supervision while escalating safety, quality, or production risks appropriately. • Experience supporting quality audits and analyzing defect or inspection trends is preferred but not required. • Prior training in general safety, electrostatic discharge awareness, foreign object damage awareness, and quality system awareness preferred. title: Commissioning Project Manager, BESS
description: SOLV Energy is a leading provider of infrastructure services to the power industry, designing, building and maintaining utility scale solar, battery storage and high voltage substation projects nationwide. The role functions as the project manager for the assigned technical scope from early planning and readiness through energization, testing, acceptance, substantial completion, and turnover. This position owns scope, schedule, resource planning, cost awareness, risk, technical coordination, stakeholder alignment, documentation, and issue resolution. The Commissioning Project Manager exercises independent judgment within the assigned scope and serves as the primary commissioning point of contact for project teams, customers, utilities, OEMs, and commissioning partners. This role is hybrid, with onsite presence required at job sites and partial remote work. Specific location details and expectations will be discussed during the interview process. Job Description: *This job description reflects management's assignment of essential functions; it does not prescribe or restrict the tasks that may be assigned. Position Responsibilities and Duties: Own the assigned HV or BESS commissioning scope across typically 2-3 concurrent projects, including deliverables, milestones, schedule, resources, risks, constraints, documentation, and turnover. Develop and maintain a project-specific commissioning execution plan, milestone and deliverables register, responsibility assignments, readiness criteria, integrated schedule activities, and resource forecast. Translate contract requirements, technical specifications, interconnection requirements, permit conditions, OEM requirements, and company standards into an executable commissioning scope and work plan. Establish priorities and make day-to-day project decisions within the assigned scope; promptly escalate safety, contractual, technical, schedule, cost, or resource issues that require leadership action. Track progress, productivity, forecasted completion, constraints, and corrective actions; provide accurate daily and weekly reporting to commissioning and project leadership. Technical and Field Execution Review applicable IFC drawings, one-line and three-line diagrams, equipment data, control narratives, relay and protection documentation, sequence-of-operations documents, OEM manuals, test requirements, and interconnection deliverables. Coordinate the development, technical review, approval, and field implementation of commissioning plans, procedures, test forms, energization prerequisites, and acceptance criteria with Commissioning Engineering and subject-matter experts. Lead readiness reviews and verify that construction, quality, engineering, documentation, communications, controls, equipment, staffing, and safety prerequisites are complete before testing or energization proceeds. Manage execution of pre-commissioning, cold, warm, and hot commissioning activities applicable to the assigned scope, including functional, protection and control, communications, synchronization, utility capability, performance, and acceptance testing. Direct and coordinate field commissioning teams, technicians, OEM technical advisors, third-party testing providers, subcontractors, and other specialists; confirm responsibilities, sequencing, access, and witness requirements. Evaluate technical issues, test failures, deficiencies, and nonconformances; lead troubleshooting, assign corrective actions, confirm retesting, and manage closure without compromising safety or quality. For HV assignments, coordinate substation apparatus, protection and control, SCADA/communications, station service, metering, utility, energization, and operational turnover interfaces. For BESS assignments, coordinate battery enclosures, inverters/PCS, transformers, controls, EMS/PPC/SCADA, fire and life-safety interfaces, OEM requirements, functional testing, and performance or capacity testing interfaces. Schedule, Cost, Risk, and Stakeholder Management Develop and manage detailed commissioning activities within the integrated P6 schedule; maintain logic, durations, sequencing, constraints, and forecast dates with project controls and execution teams. Develop and maintain the commissioning resource plan and forecast for the assigned scope; coordinate labor, equipment, test sets, specialty services, OEM support, utility support, and third-party providers. Monitor commitments, hours, third-party costs, and potential change impacts within the assigned scope; identify variances and support forecasts, change management, and recovery planning. Lead commissioning coordination meetings and daily plan-of-day meetings during active execution; document decisions, constraints, owners, and due dates. Coordinate with owners, utilities, ISOs/RTOs as applicable, OEMs, engineering, construction, quality, project management, operations, SCADA/controls, safety, and other affected parties while protecting contractual witness and notice requirements. Coordinate energization plans, switching plans and procedures, LOTO, tagging, permit-to-work, red-rope, grounding, and energized-work requirements with authorized personnel and responsible stakeholders. Verify roles, boundaries, approvals, communication protocols, care/custody/control requirements, and operational authority before energization or system turnover. Ensure commissioning activities comply with company procedures, project requirements, NFPA 70E, applicable codes and standards, environmental requirements, and site-specific safety plans. Documentation, Turnover, and Continuous Improvement Ensure complete, accurate, and timely daily reports, test records, issue logs, deficiency and punch lists, redlines, approvals, turnover packages, training records, and commissioning closeout documentation. Support milestone documentation for mechanical completion, energization, substantial completion, commercial operation, and final completion, as applicable to the assigned scope. Lead organized turnover to the owner and Operations and Maintenance teams, including system status, open items, warranties, procedures, training, and operational documentation. Capture lessons learned and improve commissioning templates, work methods, estimating assumptions, schedules, readiness gates, and standards. Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities Strong working knowledge of utility-scale HV substation or BESS systems and their commissioning sequence, interfaces, risks, and acceptance requirements. Ability to read and interpret contracts, scopes of work, specifications, IFC drawings, electrical one-lines, schematics, control narratives, relay and protection documents, OEM manuals, and interconnection requirements. Knowledge of HV and MV electrical systems, switching and grounding concepts, LOTO and energized-work controls, protection and control, SCADA/communications, and electrical test methods. For BESS assignments, knowledge of PCS/inverters, batteries, transformers, EMS/PPC/SCADA controls, communications, auxiliary systems, fire and life-safety interfaces, and OEM commissioning requirements. Working knowledge of applicable NEC, NFPA 70E, NETA, IEEE, NERC, utility, ISO/RTO, and manufacturer requirements. Project management capability in scope, schedule, resource, risk, stakeholder, cost, change, issue, and document management. Ability to lead technical teams through complex, time-sensitive work and communicate clearly with field personnel, customers, utilities, executives, and technical specialists. Proficiency with Microsoft Office and experience with scheduling, document-control, and project-management systems; P6 experience is strongly preferred. Safety Demonstrates visible safety leadership and reinforces that safe execution takes priority over schedule or production pressure. Understands and applies site operating procedures, electrical safe-work practices, PPE requirements, job hazard analysis, LOTO, switching, grounding, and permit-to-work requirements. Intervenes in at-risk conditions or behaviors, verifies corrective actions, and supports a learning-focused safety culture. Physical Demands and Environmental Conditions Frequent travel and extended project-site assignments are expected based on project phase and portfolio needs. Work may occur outdoors in variable weather, around construction equipment, and near energized medium- and high-voltage systems. Requires the ability to walk active project sites, climb ladders or stairs, access equipment areas, bend or crouch, and lift or carry up to 50 pounds with or without reasonable accommodation. Must be able to wear required PPE and work varied hours, including early mornings, nights, weekends, or outage windows when project activities require. Demonstrated ownership of a technical project scope, including schedule, resources, stakeholders, risk, issue resolution, documentation, and delivery commitments. Experience coordinating multiple concurrent projects or complex workstreams and leading cross-functional field teams without relying on direct reporting relationships. Strong problem-solving, planning, organization, negotiation, written communication, and stakeholder-management skills. Valid driver's license and ability to satisfy project access requirements. Preferred Qualifications Bachelor's degree in engineering, construction management, project management, or related discipline; equivalent relevant experience may be considered. Project Management Professional (PMP), Certified Construction Manager, NETA certification, electrical license, or other relevant technical credentials. Experience with EPC contracts, utility interconnection, owner or utility witness testing, commercial milestones, and project change management. The Test Engineer will work closely with other Reliability Laboratory Associate Engineers, Engineers, Managers, and other stakeholders to ensure that testing is performed in alignment with ISO 17025 , relevant IEC standards (e.g., IEC 61215, IEC 61730) , and internal quality requirements. This position is highly technical and data-driven, requiring strong analytical skills, attention to detail, and the ability to translate test results into practical guidance. Responsibilities: Daily Laboratory Testing Support Develop and use expertise in Reliability Testing for solar panels towards test method development and validation. Establish and maintain I-V intercomparison programs to verify consistency between laboratory I-V testers, line testers, and external reference laboratories. Oversee the production, characterization, and maintenance of primary and secondary standard modules. Provide technical support to laboratory staff during test setup, execution, and troubleshooting, ensuring that methods are applied correctly and efficiently. Support investigation of anomalous or unexpected test results and provide guidance on next steps or additional testing. Standards Compliance & Documentation Develop, update, and maintain standard operating procedures (SOPs), work instructions, and test method documents to ensure alignment with ISO 17025 and relevant IEC standards. Define and implement validation methodologies for new or modified test methods, including criteria for method acceptance, precision, and robustness. Plan and execute measurement system analysis (MSA) activities (e.g., repeatability, reproducibility, stability studies) to quantify measurement variation and support uncertainty evaluation. Document test methods, validation studies, intercomparison results, and MSA outcomes in a clear, traceable, and audit-ready manner. Collaborate with Quality and Reliability leadership to ensure test methods and documentation support laboratory accreditation and ongoing audits. Equipment Care & Method Readiness Work with the Calibration Engineer and Laboratory Managers to ensure that test methods are compatible with the capabilities and limits of laboratory equipment and fixtures. Participate in the selection, configuration, and qualification of new test equipment, including method integration and verification. Quality, Safety & Cross-Functional Support Ensure that all method development and validation activities are conducted in accordance with safety protocols and laboratory best practices. Provide technical input during internal and external audits, customer visits, or witness testing related to reliability methods and laboratory capabilities. Support reliability investigations and root-cause analysis efforts by recommending appropriate test methods, sequences, and data evaluation approaches. Communicate method capabilities, limitations, and data interpretation guidance to internal stakeholders such as Manufacturing, Quality, Technical, and external partners as needed. Identify and lead continuous improvement projects that increase test efficiency, data quality, and method robustness. Mentor Associate Engineers and Technicians in method application, data interpretation basics, and good measurement practices. Proactively seek opportunities to simplify methods, reduce turnaround time, and increase the value of test information provided to the business. Experience working under formal quality systems such as ISO 17025 and/or ISO 9001 is advantageous. Familiarity with PV module standards (such as IEC 61215 and 61730) or willingness to rapidly learn and apply them. Proficiency with Microsoft Office (Excel, Word, PowerPoint) is required; experience with data analysis tools or scripting (e.g., Excel macros, Python, Minitab, JMP, or similar) is a plus. Ability to design and interpret basic statistical analyses for method validation, intercomparison, and MSA. High attention to detail and commitment to data integrity, traceability, and documentation quality. Effective communication skills, with the ability to explain technical topics to both technical and non-technical stakeholders. Ability to work collaboratively within a multidisciplinary team while also managing individual responsibilities and priorities. Industry experience in automotive, semiconductor, or solar is highly desirable. Technical Proficiency Strong familiarity with data acquisition systems, testing instrumentation, and standard operating procedures (SOPs). Able to understand product drawings, material specifications, and manufacturing process flows. Knowledgeable in Measurement System Analysis (MSA) and Statistical Process Control (SPC) Familiarity with reliability or statistical analysis software (e.g., JMP, Minitab, Reliasoft), preferred. Experience with ISO 9001, ISO 17025, and related quality management systems is advantageous. Skills & Abilities Strong attention to detail, with the ability to multitask and adapt to evolving responsibilities. Proficiency in Microsoft Office; experience with Laboratory Information Management Systems (LIMS) is a plus. title: Product Applications Engineer - Tools
description: Job Description: Job Description Position: Product Applications Engineer - Tools Department: Application Engineering Reports To: Sr. Manager, Product Applications Location: Fremont, CA Position Overview / Role Purpose The Product Applications Engineer - Tools plays a critical role in testing, validating, and qualifying tools, fasteners, and related installation equipment used with Nextpower tracker products. This role ensures that approved tools and fasteners are compatible with Nextpower tracker systems, meet engineering and quality requirements, and support safe, repeatable, and efficient field installation. By conducting Form-Fit-Function testing, tool and fastener qualification testing, compatibility assessments, and vendor qualification testing, the Product Applications Engineer helps ensure that Nextpower tracker products can be installed reliably using approved tools, fasteners, torque methods, and field procedures. This role partners closely with R&D Design Engineering, Quality, Supply Chain, Field Applications, and Installation teams to identify risks early, validate installation methods, and deliver customer-ready solutions. Key Objectives Qualify Tools and Fasteners for Nextpower Tracker Products Test and approve tools, fasteners, and installation equipment to confirm compatibility with Nextpower tracker components, assemblies, installation requirements, and field-use conditions. Validate New Products and Installation Interfaces Ensure new product concepts, prototypes, and tracker components satisfy engineering requirements, customer needs, installation expectations, tool access requirements, fastener performance criteria, and safety standards. Test and Approve Updated Designs of Existing Offerings Confirm revisions to existing components, assemblies, tools, or fasteners maintain or improve system reliability, manufacturability, installation repeatability, and compatibility with adjacent tracker parts. Qualify New Vendors and Manufacturing Sources Assess whether new suppliers of tools, fasteners, and related components can consistently meet Nextpower’s design specifications, quality requirements, installation needs, and manufacturing standards. Core Responsibilities Tool and Fastener Qualification Testing Conduct qualification testing of tools, fasteners, torque equipment, and related installation hardware used with Nextpower tracker products. Evaluate compatibility between tools, fasteners, and Nextpower tracker components, including access, fit, torque performance, clamp load, installation repeatability, and field usability. Test torque tools, sockets, bits, drivers, Skidmore equipment, gauges, and other installation or measurement tools to confirm suitability for approved installation processes. Validate fastener performance across relevant tracker assemblies, including engagement, seating, torque behavior, joint integrity, reusability where applicable, and compatibility with mating parts. Develop and execute structured test plans for tool and fastener qualification, including acceptance criteria, sample sizes, test conditions, and documentation requirements. Identify tool or fastener failure modes, installation risks, ergonomic concerns, and compatibility issues before release to field teams or customers. Provide recommendations for approved tool lists, fastener specifications, torque requirements, installation methods, and service procedures. New Product Testing & Validation Conduct Form-Fit-Function testing on new concepts, prototypes, pre-production assemblies, tools, and fasteners to confirm alignment with design intent and installation requirements. Build representative test setups in the R&D yard to simulate tracker installation, tool usage, fastening operations, and operational conditions. Evaluate whether product notes, installation manuals, fastener specifications, torque requirements, and engineering requirements are sufficient and accurate. Confirm that Nextpower tracker products can be safely and repeatably installed using approved tools, fasteners, and installation methods. Identify design gaps, tool access issues, fastener compatibility concerns, or installation-related failure modes and partner with R&D engineering to resolve issues prior to GTM launch. Perform safety evaluations on new designs, tools, and fastener applications, verifying compliance with internal and industry standards. Document all test results through structured data collection, analysis, and professional test reports. Testing of Updated / Revised Designs Validate updated designs of existing products to ensure manufacturability, mechanical performance, installation repeatability, and compatibility with system interfaces, tools, and fasteners. Review updated drawings, specifications, product notes, fastener requirements, and installation instructions for completeness and ability to achieve design goals. Test individual parts and full tracker assemblies to confirm they meet functional requirements, installation procedures, torque requirements, and approved tool compatibility. Assess the impact of design revisions on tool access, fastener fit, assembly sequence, field installation time, and installation quality. Provide recommendations for improving installation instructions, product notes, fastener specifications, approved tool lists, or design features based on test outcomes. Replicate customer-reported tool, fastener, or installation issues in the R&D yard and develop data-driven, field-ready solutions. Vendor Qualification & Supplier Assessment Conduct Form-Fit-Function and qualification testing on first-article tools, fasteners, and related components from new vendors to verify compliance with Nextpower specifications. Verify adherence to drawings, product notes, fastener specifications, material requirements, dimensional tolerances, and compatibility with adjacent tracker components. Evaluate new vendor tools and fasteners for performance, consistency, durability, installation repeatability, and suitability for field deployment. Travel to vendor facilities for onsite inspections, test reviews, tool/fastener evaluations, and pre-production validations as needed.Provide structured test feedback to Supply Chain, Vendor Quality, and Engineering to support vendor qualification and sourcing decisions. Additional Responsibilities Support R&D tracker installation sites by assisting with test setup, construction activities, tool trials, fastener evaluations, and data gathering. Lead or assist in building test fixtures, partial product assemblies, and representative tracker sections for tool and fastener evaluation. Coordinate testing priorities with cross-functional teams and communicate status updates clearly. Review, update, and validate installation manuals to ensure accuracy and alignment with tested tool, fastener, and tracker assembly results. Support the creation and maintenance of approved tool lists, fastener qualification records, test reports, and installation validation documentation. Manage multiple projects concurrently, ensuring timely completion under tight schedules. Maintain a strong commitment to safety during all testing, construction, tool operation, fastening operations, and field activities. Qualifications 5+ years of experience in product testing, mechanical systems, fastening systems, tool qualification, quality engineering, installation engineering, or related field; or a BA/BS in engineering or related discipline. Strong proficiency in interpreting engineering drawings, specifications, GD&T, product notes, fastener requirements, and installation documentation. Hands-on experience with measurement and testing tools, including torque tools, Skidmore equipment, 3D scanners, thread gauges, calipers, sockets, bits, drivers, and related installation equipment. Experience testing or qualifying fasteners, torque methods, mechanical joints, installation tools, or field assembly processes is highly desirable. Familiarity with Arena, Jira, SolidWorks/CAD systems. Ability to safely lift up to 40 lbs. and work in outdoor R&D field environments. Knowledge of Nextpower tracker products, solar tracker installation methods, tools, and fastener applications is highly desirable. Availability for travel to vendor facilities and project sites up to 25% of the time. Skills & Competencies Technical & Analytical Demonstrated ability to conduct rigorous tool, fastener, and product testing and interpret results accurately. Strong analytical skills for evaluating mechanical performance, fastening behavior, compatibility, installation quality, and failure modes. Ability to assess tool access, torque application, fastener fit, assembly sequence, and field usability in tracker product applications. High attention to detail with strong documentation, reporting, and data-presentation capabilities. Collaboration & Communication Excellent communication skills for conveying technical test results to both technical and non-technical stakeholders. Proven ability to work cross-functionally with Engineering, Quality, Supply Chain, Field Applications, Installation, and Vendor Quality teams. Customer-focused mindset with the ability to support field teams and address customer tool, fastener, and installation issues. Execution & Project Management Strong organizational skills with the ability to prioritize and manage multiple concurrent tool, fastener, and product test efforts. Adaptability to evolving project needs, new technologies, new tools, alternate fasteners, and changing design directions. Ability to work under pressure while maintaining high quality standards. This position owns scope, schedule, resource planning, cost awareness, risk, technical coordination, stakeholder alignment, documentation, and issue resolution. The Commissioning Project Manager exercises independent judgment within the assigned scope and serves as the primary commissioning point of contact for project teams, customers, utilities, OEMs, and commissioning partners. Position Responsibilities and Duties: Own the assigned HV or BESS commissioning scope across typically 2-3 concurrent projects, including deliverables, milestones, schedule, resources, risks, constraints, documentation, and turnover. Develop and maintain a project-specific commissioning execution plan, milestone and deliverables register, responsibility assignments, readiness criteria, integrated schedule activities, and resource forecast. Translate contract requirements, technical specifications, interconnection requirements, permit conditions, OEM requirements, and company standards into an executable commissioning scope and work plan. Establish priorities and make day-to-day project decisions within the assigned scope; promptly escalate safety, contractual, technical, schedule, cost, or resource issues that require leadership action. Evaluate technical issues, test failures, deficiencies, and nonconformances; lead troubleshooting, assign corrective actions, confirm retesting, and manage closure without compromising safety or quality. For BESS assignments, coordinate battery enclosures, inverters/PCS, transformers, controls, EMS/PPC/SCADA, fire and life-safety interfaces, OEM requirements, functional testing, and performance or capacity testing interfaces. Verify roles, boundaries, approvals, communication protocols, care/custody/control requirements, and operational authority before energization or system turnover. Support milestone documentation for mechanical completion, energization, substantial completion, commercial operation, and final completion, as applicable to the assigned scope. Lead organized turnover to the owner and Operations and Maintenance teams, including system status, open items, warranties, procedures, training, and operational documentation. Capture lessons learned and improve commissioning templates, work methods, estimating assumptions, schedules, readiness gates, and standards. Project management capability in scope, schedule, resource, risk, stakeholder, cost, change, issue, and document management.
